findings.title: Linda H. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Not a family friendly resort! Security man followed my kids (teens) back to their rooms because they were sitting in the lobby. Guess he thought they weren't staying at the resort. They were not misbehaving. So scary!!

findings.title: Sepi N. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
chose The Phoenician for my birthday getaway over Memorial Day weekend because it is marketed as a luxury resort. I invited four girlfriends to join me, and each of them booked their own rooms. Unfortunately, after spending four days at the property, I can confidently say this was one of the most disappointing luxury hotel experiences I've ever had.

The problems started at check-in. The front desk associate barely engaged with me, offered no overview of the property, amenities, or resort experience, and didn't ask whether it was my first visit. When I mentioned I was celebrating my birthday, there wasn't even a simple "Happy Birthday." I was handed a key and what turned out to be a property map, with no explanation whatsoever.

My next stop was the concierge desk to inquire about pool cabanas. I was simply told they were sold out. No alternatives were offered, no waitlist was mentioned, and no effort was made to assist. Instead, I was told to look at an outside website myself. At a luxury resort, isn't the concierge's role to help guests find solutions and make arrangements? When I later asked if the resort did anything special for birthday guests, the concierge emailed me a list of items I could purchase. That response perfectly summarized the level of hospitality we experienced.

The room itself was another disappointment. It felt outdated and in need of renovation, hardly what one would expect from a luxury property. Ironically, when I later visited the pool and asked an attendant about cabanas, she immediately offered to place me on a waitlist in case of cancellations--an option the concierge never bothered to mention.

The following morning, I spoke with a manager, Alley, about my experience. She apologized and offered a $100 food and beverage credit, which I appreciated. However, when I returned to my room, I discovered something far more concerning: one of the pillows had visible mold on it. Since I don't sleep with pillows, I hadn't noticed it the first night. As I looked closer, I found stains on the bedding, pillows, lampshade, and even areas of the room that clearly had not been properly cleaned.

Housekeeping came and changed the sheets and pillowcases, but shockingly left behind the actual moldy pillow. At that point, this had moved far beyond a service issue and into a cleanliness and health concern.

I reported everything again to management. The additional response was a $50 credit.

At this point, the property had failed in virtually every area that defines a luxury hotel: guest service, concierge support, cleanliness, attention to detail, and problem resolution. My friends who booked rooms experienced similar frustrations with both customer service and housekeeping.

We ultimately spent much of our time dining at restaurants off property and even rented a cabana at another resort because our experience at The Phoenician was so disappointing.

For a stay that cost me over $2,000, offering a total of $150 in credits felt completely out of touch with the severity of the issues. The amount wasn't the problem, it was the lack of accountability and genuine concern.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but travelers should know that this property did not deliver anything close to the luxury experience it advertises. Between the poor service, moldy pillow, cleanliness concerns, and overall lack of hospitality, I cannot recommend The Phoenician. I will also be filing a complaint through Marriott Bonvoy regarding my experience.

Luxury hotels are defined by service, attention to detail, and how they handle problems when they arise. Unfortunately, The Phoenician failed on all three.

findings.title: Deborah W. (2/5)
findings.snippet: The resort is looking very rundown and dated. Front desk didn't recognize Marriott status at all. Took 3 tries to get a room that was decent and then it still faced the lobby parking so was noisy and had zero view. First room smelled like sewer - so bad you could smell it in the hallway. 2nd room's balcony literally faced a wall. Everything was extremely overpriced - $28 for an espresso martini! Cold shower in spa didn't work and didn't have instructions on how to use. Spa services were great but very pricey - especially with the 22% required gratuity added. Food was decent but very overpriced. The tea was nice but the food was just ok. Room service delivery person was very friendly and helpful, food was hot and tasty. Pool was surprisingly a little chilly and our reserved chaise lounges were at the family pool when we had requested the adult pool. First impression was that this would be a fun place to come with friends (I was with my adult daughter on this trip). But after seeing the clientele and the prices I don't think I would return. I would try a different place in Scottsdale - though maybe Scottsdale isn't my scene.

findings.title: Terrence O. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
We took a mini stay vacation the other day.
There's the truth, we were very disappointed.
The grounds and the hotel's public spaces are beautiful.
Our room described as a Casita, was nothing more than a regular room in a separate building we that we had to walk to and then lug our bags up a flight of stairs as it was on the second floor.
Only to be met by garbage at the door. YES I took a picture, of it.
After unpacking I opened a bottle of wine but the table and chairs legs were so bad, I was afraid to put my glass down for fear it fall over.
Of the two dining rooms in the main building, one was closed and the other we couldn't get in. At over $1,000 a night, for the room our dining choice end up being in the golf club house. 
So between all the kids running around the entire property.
I felt like I was staying at a tired Holiday Inn on the freeway as opposed to a 5 Star Marriott Luxury Collection Resort.

findings.title: Patricia Z. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Luxury at its finest one of the best hotels I've ever stayed at! Service is top notch. They sent us complementary strawberries. We have a daybed by the pool with catered service all day long (for a fee& you need to reserve it),  Genaro was our Adult pool server!  He was on point. I don't wanna leave. And the rooms are impeccable. This hotel has something for everyone. There's an adult pool area. No kids allowed. but the pool area for the kids has a giant slide and plenty to do.

findings.title: Sean S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Beautiful hotel that we've stayed at a few times while coming out for spring training. It really has everything you need for a relaxing day by the pool, and it's conveniently located for driving to games, heading into town for restaurants, or exploring downtown Palm Springs.

The amenities are great. The gym is well equipped, there are tennis courts, and the pools are beautiful with a nice balance between adult and family-friendly areas. The restaurants are solid as well, which makes it easy to stay on property and unwind.

Overall, a really great experience. We would definitely come back again for our next spring training trip.

findings.title: M S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Luxury Collection is the last place The Phoenecian should be categorized. It is the furthest from modern day luxury. If you are looking for a Spring Break experience on par with the masses, then sign up,but otherwise stay far away. 
The nightly rate is abhorrent considering the lack of service and condition of the property.
- Day 1 our room was not cleaned by 3:30PM
- Our toilet was leaking, puddles on the bathroom floor
-When someone came to clean, he stepped on the bathmat and a filthy footprint was left, alongside a filthy dirty shoe puddle on the floor
-Room key stopped working 3x and it took the third time for security to change the batteries on th e door lock
-The pool was murky and had piles of sand and empty drink cups floating in it and filthy chewed up pool noodles.
-Two trips to the pool and no one offered us any towels to sit, and it took 20 minutes to get someone to order drinks
-Rat poop in the pool towel cart that we had to access ourselves because no one offered.
-The last day of the stay, some of our personal belongings, in a grocery bag were thrown out that were in the room. 
-The gym is full of children and there is no room for anyone do do anything with all machines full.
-Manager refused to address our issues at checkout, and management has yet to reply to an email.
-Food is shockingly good, but long wait times.
-Golf course is lovely

findings.title: Anthony K. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Overall, we were surprised by the ups and downs of the hotel/spa. 
- Pros - expansive facility with everything on site. Great spa, gym and tennis courts.  The golf course looked amazing. 
- Cons - the pools were not well-maintained. Lots of stuff floating in the pool. Yikes. J&G Restaurant was a big miss. Their ribeye was awful. Worst steak I've had in a long time. The service was great so we left a 20% tip. We would have left more if the food was just decent. Given the pros/cons, we won't be going back.

findings.title: Anna H. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We're currently staying at The Phoenician in Scottsdale, and while the property itself is beautiful, the billing practices have completely overshadowed the experience.

We were originally quoted around $10,600 for our stay. Upon arrival, we were charged the full cost of the room (despite the confirmation stating no deposit required). Since then, an additional ~$12,000 has been charged to the card for "potential purchases."

At this point, over $22,000 has been pulled from the account and we have not actually spent anywhere near that amount.

When we asked, we were told this is standard and that the additional charges would be refunded later if unused. We've stayed at many high-end properties and have never experienced anything remotely like this, especially at this scale.

What's most frustrating is that none of this was disclosed at booking, in the confirmation email, or clearly explained at check-in. For many people, this could easily create real financial stress or exceed credit limits.

The staff acknowledged this is a common complaint, which makes it even more surprising that it's not communicated upfront.

Again, the property is beautiful, but transparency matters. It's very hard to enjoy a stay when this much money is being taken from your account for items that haven't been purchased without clear explanation.

If you're considering staying here, I would strongly recommend asking detailed questions about their billing and hold policies in advance.

Updated: and I knew I'd get an AI generated response with an apology but no action.

findings.title: Kim L. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Had a gift card for the spa   The massage was wonderful and customer service was excellent but the pool spa needs to be updated  there is rust at the bottom of the pool.  the handles to get in and out of the pool have no covers so you burn your hand hold on to it to get in an out of the pool

findings.title: A B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The Phoenician  is still the grande dame of luxury hospitality in the valley of the sun. With impeccable grounds, multiple pools and restaurants. It is hard to find fault with this Resort.. Their culinary offerings are particularly fantastic with my favorite being J& G steakhouse . I surely missed the days when they had the best Sunday brunch buffet available. Times have changed though ! Whether you are here for a few days or  a week long stay or have an event of some kind. this resort will most likely deliver and wow you in a grand way. They also offer a remarkable afternoon tea. If you're looking for a place to pamper yourself look no further.

findings.title: Morgan A. (2/5)
findings.snippet: I was sadly disappointed. I went to visit for the day because I wanted to see if I'd like to book in the future. At the front desk, they said they are not doing room tours at this time due to full occupancy. That was understandable. So I asked if they do tours of the property. And I was told that they don't. I suppose I was hoping maybe they would encourage me to walk around or purchase a day pass to explore or something so that I could know what I would experience if I were to book a stay. Before I left, I went to use the restroom, and the toilet didn't fully work, and the soap dispenser didn't work either. I tried 5 of the dispensers, and only one worked. I left confused because I really expected the highest of quality, and I did not receive that in the short time I was there.

findings.title: Zoe F. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My friends and I attended afternoon tea today and we had the best time. We knew the price would be quite high going into this, so that was expected and well worth it for the ambiance and delicious tea and bites. Our server Wanda made our whole experience. She was lovely and friendly and on top of things. We never had an empty drink and food was cleared promptly at the appropriate time. I'm not sure our experience would have been what it was without her. I would highly recommend this experience for a group of girls looking to have quality bites with great views and vibes. We will definitely be back! Thanks again Wanda:)

findings.title: Tiffany P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My husband and I stayed here and loved it! The entire resort is a dream- from the main lobby, to the rooms to the beautiful pools!

findings.title: Kenyetta C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Our stay at The Phoenician was really nice. The property was beautiful and the views were amazing! The staff were pretty friendly. The beds and pillows were extremely comfortable. We did not want to get up, lol. There are multiple restaurants on the property. All of the food was good. No complaints. Not sure if self parking was an option, but valet was available. The pools were all warm. The property was clean. This was a great stay!

findings.title: Debbi P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful hotel and grounds!! Always the friendliest staff!!! Fabulous restaurants and amenities. Amazing pop-ups!! First time doing a Veuve Pop-up with music and small bites added!! So much fun!!!! Beautiful views!!

findings.title: Gail H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Love this resort so much! This is our go to staycation spot. The pools are great and the restaurants and bars offer so many options. The location is central to so many fun activities like shopping  and eating.

findings.title: Margalit F. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Very large clean well laid out rooms with a lot of storage spaces and comfortable beds  , beautifully manicured resort and a staff that is trained to please if anything were to go wrong. It was too cold to use the pools ( sadly) but we did eat at ALL their venues. 
Their J&G steakhouse is top of the line though pricey and their marketplace has a surprisingly addictive gelato selection. 
If you want to live it up then book your stay here .

findings.title: Kim H. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful resort I Scottsdale. We went to check out their Xmas tree lighting. Santa was there and so were some carollers. They had a veuve pop up bar, but for $43 a glass I passed. Lol.

findings.title: Alyson W. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
With a hotel of this caliber, my expectations are higher so please bear that in mind for this review (I hold them to a higher standard than for example the W or the AC hotel).

Pros:
Absolutely beautiful, well groomed property.
Staff, especially room service and valet, are great. Front desk was not quite as polished, efficient, and friendly as I would have hoped.
Gym is GREAT! Two stories with a game room, pelotons, tons of machines, overlooking tennis courts. Small nitpick: I wish they offered water bottles. They offer a water station and cups instead. 
Room service food was very good. 
Rooms are quiet/noise proofed.
Big bathtub, nice toiletries (byredo), really good water pressure.
Housekeeping went the extra mile, including chocolates for turndown.

Cons:
Gym is far away from main hotel (like a 5 min walk). I travel for work so my time is pretty crunched- if I have to allocate 10 min for my walk to and from the gym out of the 30 min I have to workout, it's annoying (a me problem).
Hotel is very far from anything else (could be a pro or a con).

findings.title: Jenn M. (4/5)
findings.snippet: It's a maze to get the right entrance, lol, or maybe it was my car taxi. There's a lot of walking, the staff are friendly and helpful, and they even helped the bellman drop me off at the right entrance. The room was nice and clean, and there was a lovely balcony with space to sit outside. The bed was okay, not very comfortable, and the pillows were lumpy. The room smelled fresh and clean. Beautiful lobby and entrance when you pull up, but it's a bit hard to get a good picture unless you pull over and get out of the car. Excellent water pressure when taking a shower, but I didn't get to enjoy any of the amenities offered

findings.title: Kirstin H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful place!! Clean and well kept. Gym and pool amazing!! Let us check in at 11am. Went to dinner there:) great food totally worth the $$ spent

findings.title: Kathryn Z. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Super disappointed in our accommodations. 

We reserved a casita for a family staycation and the room had several issues. The most problematic issue was the ac unit that cooled the living room was not working and when maintenance finally came out at 10:30pm, we were told there was nothing they could do as the compressor had been out and they hadn't fixed it yet. I'm sorry but it's very hot in AZ and to know you have a unit out and still put guest in it is just not acceptable.

The other major issue was the room was infested with insects especially ants! They were everywhere. Floors, counters, and even in our luggage. This also didn't seem to be an issue for the staff but would be for most guests.

Lastly, we were traveling with our three small children. After dinner we went to make their pull out beds and found there to be no linens, pillows or blankets to make them (we searched everywhere). After calling the front desk we were told that this had to be done by the staff and someone would be out "soon". At no time were we made aware of this practice which seems a bit ridiculous. Their process is to simply wait for guests to discover they can't make their pull out beds and then take action. It was after dinner and late for our children so this maybe something you want to let guests know at check in. They knew we were a party of 5 so could have done the math and realized we would need to use the pull out beds and sent someone before it was so late.

findings.title: Vivian H. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I'm receiving an important award soon and to thank the wonderful people who supported my nomination and helped me to get selected, I wanted to do something nice for the elders in my life. 

My culture teaches about respecting my elders, so organizing an afternoon tea here for them as a token of my gratitude felt like the right thing to do. 

Afternoon tea seating is from 2-3pm. A pianist is scheduled between 3-5pm. Some of us arrived around 2:40pm for a 3pm reservation and pianist was already playing. 

The lobby of The Phoenician is beautiful and classy. I'd definitely come back again and have a drink at the bar, enjoy the ambiance and people watch.

To the right of the lobby, that is where you check in with the hostess. We had a party of 12 (I reserved for 11), and the hostess's response to me wasn't the response I was expecting honestly. She said let me check if we can accommodate your one extra person. I was thinking to myself, "you gonna turn away a party of 12 because of one extra person?" You're gonna lose out on a decent amount of business, but ok, up to you. 

She was able to accommodate our one extra person in and led us to our table. To be honest. I didnt quite like that two seats were placed on the two ends of the table, felt a bit cramped. I've only seen one seat usually at each end of a long table. The afternoon tea area also felt a bit cramped, but the views were lovely of the balcony and outside. 

There's a summer special for afternoon tea, so it brought the cost down to a little under $100/person before taxes and gratuity. 

Also note they have very strict no show policy. If people in your party don't show, it's a $35 fee/person.

You can choose from a variety of teas and I got the coconut one, which was lovely. I enjoyed it! I love anything with coconut!

Then the finger sandwiches kept coming, first a few showed up in the first course and then more! 

Then, there were scones and the Devonshire cream was lovely. 

Last course was an assortment of small, cute and delicious desserts on a plate.

The food and tea were delicious and everyone seemed to enjoy and many of us were so stuffed we needed to take home the tray of small desserts. 

I guess my only suggestion to the hotel would be to have all the options plated on a tiered tray where people could choose from any of the above options all together vs being served in courses.

Service was attentive and friendly. Definitely would be a spot I would come back to for a special occasion!

findings.title: Brittney C. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
We were here for 4 nights, 5 days for a national dance conference.

Upon check in the staff were friendly. The staff at the marketplace, Miriam and the other nicely dressed lady were fantastic! Their responsiveness and kindness was amazing! 

As the stay went on there were several things lacking. We went 2 days without our room being serviced. I had to request it several times, it took 24 hours to fulfill my pillows and blanket request. 

The pool on day one was great, with great service. Every day after it was dismal, the pool area trashes were overflowing, garbage everywhere. I contact the hotel property to inform them the pool was water level was dangerously low. Kids were jumping in and hitting the bottom because of the lack of water. I was told it's because it's hot, but they wouldn't someone know. I'm an Az Native and never had I had water evaporating in any of my pools or staycations at a rate they stayed theirs was. The next day, the pool levels still weren't corrected. Finally by day 3 we couldn't use the pool anymore because of concerns with the low water levels. 

The area near the ballrooms were also not well maintained by housekeeping as trash was always overflowing. The bathroom trashes had paper towels spilling on the floor. The stalls had toilet paper on the floors etc. 

The bellmen and cart drivers were friendly and helpful. 

Over all I expected a lot more for the price and clout this hotel has. It was lackluster at best with service.

findings.title: R.B. P. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Went for a night for wife's birthday and a "staycation". Very expensive, not good value for the $. Should be more like $300 for a night in summer not $500. The music was too loud at the pools, not relaxing. Couldn't get service at the bar either, had to go elsewhere. Also no kids programs, even though the website said there would be. The fireworks were cool and nice to be so close to the mountain, but otherwise, would go elsewhere, especially for this price.

findings.title: Lindsay L. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Shocked by how poor my experience staying here was. From returning to the lobby an hour and a half after check-in to retrieve our bags ourselves, to some of our table's food not coming out until the rest of us were done at Mowry, to having to flag servers down 3 times at the pool for water, to not being acknowledged at the bar for a drink, to the steakhouse not willing to accommodate food allergies, to even all the listed amenities not in the room when we arrived, I would never recommend anyone pay to stay here. 

I've had MUCH better service and overall experience at the Element in south Scottsdale. Which should not even be a comparable Marriott hotel.

findings.title: Jan L. (5/5)
findings.snippet: 1This review is for Cynthia in the Phoenician Spa, where I go for my "foot pampering" pedicure visits.  Believe me when I say that my feet are super pampered.  I appreciate Cynthia's professionalism, and her congenial, friendly demeanor.  It's always an experience that I look forward too!  I, and my feet, thank you Cynthia!

findings.title: Sheldon D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The Phoenician is one of my favorite resorts. The resort is beautiful. The staff and employees are friendly and helpful.

findings.title: Noah S. (3/5)
findings.snippet: The casita was definitely not worth it. I wish we would have stayed in the main hotel. We had bugs and roaches in the casita(the hotel removed the resort fee as an apology) and our patio led out to the road, so our deluxe view was just of cars passing by. There were also food service boxes outside our neighbor's door the entire time we were there(probably attracting more bugs), no one cleaned them up the 3 days we were there. It's like the resort doesn't care about the casitas at all. The food and drinks at the hotel were very tasty, but it is a resort so everything was overpriced. The tavern had the best food at a decent price. The pools were nice and clean, the staff were very attentive, but the adult pool was in the middle of the two non adult pools, which meant that you still hear the screaming of kids the entire time. There was also no adult only jacuzzi so they were occupied by kids almost the entire time. Luckily the pools are open 24/7 so we were able to come back during the evening to enjoy the jacuzzis.

findings.title: Nayia R. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Was here for a work conference. There were over 500 people at the conference and at the hotel where everything was being held.  This hotel is really big and pretty cool. There are 4 pools and a hot tub. One of the pools is an adult only pool. The gym is huge and they have a spa. I didn't get to enjoy the spa due to being there for the conference. The service was really good and I'd book here with my family for sure.  Especially if you plan to be on the resort majority of the time.

findings.title: Chau B. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Mother's Day Brunch at the Phoenician - A Special Treat, But Pricey

We had brunch at the Phoenician for Mother's Day. The food was mostly delicious, but at $180 per person, it felt a bit overpriced. Some buffet stations felt cramped and could've been laid out better, especially with the crowd, which made it hard to fully enjoy the experience.

The caviar station was a highlight, with four options; I liked the Black Pearl best. Sushi was standard but fresh. Seafood was hit or miss--some oysters didn't seem very fresh, but the crab claws were great.

I enjoyed the roasted pork at the carving station; the New York strip was underwhelming. The smoked salmon Benedict was good, though it needed more roe (I added caviar myself and loved it). The seared scallop and carrot risotto at the sauté station were excellent. For dessert, the fruit tart was my favorite.

Great for a special occasion, but not quite worth the premium price.

findings.title: Marianne C. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Nice Hotel, luxury mmm not by today's standards. A bit tired in many areas. i'd consider paying about $500 a night inclusive of all fees, especially since this hotel seems to cater to group/conventions who we know are paying a lot less.

The room was well appointed. Lovely bathroom with tub, two sinks (yay!) and separate shower and separate toilet closet (perfection). The towels were frayed and thin. Frette slippers and robe provided. Comfy bed and pillow. Fully stocked refrigerator and pantry with prices one expects. 

The killer on room service is a 22% fee.  This is especially egregious since there is absolutely nothing near by.  [Just stayed at an exquisite Kimpton Hotel (truly luxury)  in the islands. Their total extra room service charge was $7.50 (unbelievable) and the food was not only delicious, but was very well presented!]

The room overlooked the hotel entrance with a large water fountain. The fountain is unusually loud all day until midnight; I couldn't sit on the balcony because it was so loud. There was no way I could talk to anyone on the phone with the fountain in the background either. 

Although the door to our room was facing the beautiful Camelback mountain and cactus garden, non of this could be seen from our room. A waste of a view. 

Staff seems passive aggressive. Appearing gracious, but with a sting. Odd and off putting. The only truly lovely and informative staff member, Angelica, was at the pool. A wonderful young woman. Note:  Food and drink service at the pool was extremely slow! The "club" music at the pool was quite a bit annoying. Just a hard beat all day with annoying music and lyrics. Not a fun-in-the-sun type music.  Made me rethink going for another all day at the pool.  (I did complain at the front desk and for the next couple days they toned it down.) The adult pool on one end is directly adjacent to the huge kiddy luge. Not great planning.  

Nice that there is a "food market" with any prepared food and drink you might need; open 6-6 everyday. A sundry and snack shop opened 7-10, I believe everyday (Pure Leaf iced tea $5/bottle). These are nice touches as there is nothing easily assessable close to the hotel. 

Went to the Athletic Club to do some Pilates mat work. Thought I'd wipe off the mat just to make sure. Dear God, thankfully I did. I kept cleaning, and cleaning, and cleaning. There was filthy black residue on the wipes. I got tired of cleaning. I put the mat back and warned this other young woman who was about to start a work out. 

In room ice can only be had from room service. Hugely inconvenient and annoying for an ice lover like myself, never mind the inconvenience and constant tipping issue.

All in all, it's a good hotel. Not the luxury that I was expecting.

findings.title: Melanie B. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
We usually stay at another property in the area, but decided to try somewhere different!
I want to start off by saying the staff here are phenomenal! The staff is the best asset this hotel has. It is, hands down, the best overall service we have had at a resort property. There are some members of the staff that I would like to give a shout out to for being exceptional: Rachael at Mowry and Cotton; Angelina, Maya, and Marisa at the pool; and Kira and Julie/Julia (can't remember which is correct) in the market/coffee shop.
We arrived on a Sunday afternoon and when we checked in my husband's Marriott status was acknowledged (he really doesn't care if it is!) and we got a little box of truffles and were told we were being upgraded to a king in a casita with a mountain view.We had booked a king, so the upgrade was the casita and the view. More on that coming up. 
Our room wasn't ready yet so we went to the lobby bar/restaurant and had something to eat and drink while we waited. We received a text a little while later letting us know our room was ready. A member of the staff gave us (and our luggage) a ride to our casita. 
The translation of casita is "small house" and is defined as a small self contained dwelling. What we stayed in is not a casita. It's a room in an out building. The first one we were in had either four or six rooms and the second one had eight rooms. These are two story buildings with rooms on both floors.
The first casita we had did not have a mountain view. It had a view of the side of a parking garage. We don't spend a lot of time in the room, so we just shrugged it off.  
The next day, we come back from breakfast and go to sit outside and we notice one of our windows on the slider was all taped up. My husband either called, or messaged someone in the app, and we were told that while they were mowing, a rock kicked out and broke the window and they taped it up. The inside wasn't shattered, just the outside. We felt that a call or text or note in our room or something would have been appropriate. But no. We found it on our own. At that point, my husband requested we be moved. 
Everything had to be packed up and then Luke, from the bell staff, came in a golf cart and helped my husband move everything to another not-really-a- casita. Again we were on the ground floor, but we did have a mountain view! There aren't elevators at the casitas, so it's ground floor where everyone walking by can see into your room, or you're walking up and down stairs. 
The casitas are somewhat like bad apartments. You hear everyone come and go. I could hear someone sneezing and blowing their nose. 
Our door was near the housekeeping door. We NEVER, in the week we were there, left or came back to our room when there wasn't a pile of stuff sitting there. The housekeeping buckets, rags, etc, sat there all day. Room service dishes were piled there. And all kinds of pieces of nature blew in there and went into our room when we opened the door.
Our room was nice and large and so was the bathroom. There was mold/mildew on the shower ceiling. The tile floor in our entry was chipped in a few places. We didn't use the tub, but there's something on part of it - spilled paint? I don't know. 
The grounds are beautiful and well maintained. I would maybe suggest hosing down the goose poop a little more often down by the lowest pool. It could be pretty gross.
The lobby is very nice! But the lobby restrooms? Not so much. They're old and tired looking and they're probably the first restroom most people use on the property. 
All this leads me to say that the place needs a facelift. It's just looking a little shabby and kind of tired. I wasn't feeling the "luxury".

findings.title: Tarrah M. (3/5)
findings.snippet: I was so looking forward to a quick getaway with my husband while he attended  a conference here.  The lobby is beautiful and sparkly and I was thinking the rooms would be on par.  We checked in and granted, conference rates ($350/night), but we were probably given the worst room in the place...main floor first room off the lobby next to the kitchen.  So, loud.  Small.  Bathroom was a hodge podge of renovations and very dated and not at all clean.  It had a little patio that opened onto the...check in area for the valets.  Not what I was hoping.  The man staying next door was really nice, but I could hear every word of his phone conversation.  Went to dinner, came back, and husband said this was not going to work.  So, he talked to the front desk who said there was nothing else available in that rate, but they ended up finding a room for $750/night which was much better and we moved immediately for which I was really grateful.  If my husband's company wasn't paying the tab I would have probably rebooked somewhere else tbh and yes he is a long time rewards member.  We ended up in a HUGE suite with 2 balconies overlooking the pools, directly below the steakhouse.   It was quiet and the views would have been hard to beat.  But there were drawbacks.  The bathroom is grimy and quite outdated.  For a luxury hotel I genuinely expected better.  Shower stall was tiny.  In the room there was trash by the seating area from American Airlines-those bag check tags which are quite big actually...but we traveled Delta...so it was there from the previous guest.  After 2 nights and 2 cleanings by the staff, it was still on the floor so I finally picked it all up and threw it out.   The patios were spacious and one was shaded which was lovely and even on a very windy day I could sit out and enjoy without really feeling the wind--so well protected.  Sadly, the patio is dirty-I wondered if it was stained so I wiped it up a bit and no, it wasn't, it just needed a quick wet mop and it would have been good to go.  We dined in the Mowry and Cotton for breakfast each morning and it was delicious, service was wonderful and highly recommend.  We sat outside and yes the birds were about but they really aren't a big deal--they don't bother the seated tables.  I actually enjoyed watching them and their antics.  We had cocktails and small bites at The Thirsty Camel.  We sat outside and it was beautiful and comfortable but the service took 45 mins and 3 rounds of my husband going inside to ask for service to finally take our order for 4 people.  The bar refused to take our order and  just kept repeating that someone was out there.  After they did finally get to us, service was great, drinks were delicious as was the food.  The steakhouse was yummy and service was helpful and kind.  The grounds of the Phoenician are gorgeous--very well maintained and beautifully landscaped.  The cactus garden is a real treat.  Thoroughly enjoyed walking it several times and highly recommend-some really amazing things to see growing there.  I wish I could say we would return but we won't.  The rooms are just not at all what I would consider luxury.

findings.title: Ali T. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I was here for a few nights in March and I had an enjoyable visit. Upon check-in, my room was automatically upgraded since I'm a Marriott Rewards Member- so that felt like a nice perk. My room was large and I had a nice balcony. Unfortunately, I didn't really have a room with a view. Just a big tree. 

I was here for a conference and I feel like the staff were SO accommodating. The food was good and there was a great variety to choose from. 

Hoping to be able to visit again for a non-work event!

findings.title: Neha K. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
While this is a sprawling, gorgeous resort- they lack the ethic to follow through on random charges they hit you with. I have stayed here twice and in my second  stay, I was mysteriously charged for 'honor bar' without any reason, not even itemized or provided proof for. Nothing was taken or consumed in the hotel room- but the hotel made me call multiple times until I had no choice but to dispute my credit card. An absolute headache to follow up for something they just try to cheat you with. 

The rooms are huge, parking is underground and most of the staff are great. Sort of shocking how a hotel like this won't have a full length mirror in the room that is actually usable. The only full length mirror sits behind a massive table so it is pointless. The pools are sparkling and the views are beautiful! Sometimes they give a coupon at check in for a free beer at the pub. They do upgrade folks with Marriott status which is nice.
Overall, watch your credit cards like hawks with this hotel but have a great time while you're there!

findings.title: Jay S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I absolutely suggest you stay at one of Scottsdale's many other resorts. This place is absolutely awful. I'm still on property, generally they run a shotty three star Marriot service level. rooms were not ready on time, they promised they would call or text when they were, they never texted. they couldn't get me a reservation to the restaurant here even though I'm a guest, however, when we saw the restaurant half the tables were open at the time we wanted. I tried to call the front desk four different times from my room, nobody ever picks up. The original reservation was supposed to be at 4 PM check out which I get through Amex, they forgot to put that on there. bellman were supposed to take our luggage for four hours and left it out the entire time with absolutely nobody guarding it, and it was only just luck that nobody stole the contents. Hopefully you get the idea. This is not someplace you want to stay, especially if you're spending more than $1000 a night. The real kicker, the front desk wouldn't even give me the email address of the GM. They said he was too important and it had to go through his assistant. I've stayed at fine hotels around the world, that's a first. But it's emblematic of why this place runs so poorly. It's a shame. It's a beautiful property, but terribly managed.

findings.title: Dee W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This Resort has everything you want and need right at your fingertips. From the moment I arrived the staff managed to go above and beyond to exceed my expectations. We enjoyed a lovely dinner unfortunately we weren't close to the restaurant but when we called the front desk we where told the bell boy come to our door with door to door golfcart service . J&G offered an incredible dining experience.  I felt like I was at home here and I can't recommend this Luxury resort enough.  The staff went above and beyond to ensure that all our needs were met. If you're looking for luxury accommodations at your fingertips this place is an absolute must-try!

findings.title: Rohit R. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I would like to give a specific shout out to " Mowry & Cotton" a restaurant located on the first floor. I had a simple breakfast with Kinwa and poached eggs. They made Kinwa taste good. The bowl had a mix of flavors which were distinct but blended well. Wish I had more time to taste other culinary options. I would have loved to give 4.5 stars which is not an option on yelp.

findings.title: Carrie O. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Day before arriving, (12/30) I called to confirm my stay as I had booked with AmEx. Was told by Brad the reservation was cancelled. Spent over an hour on the phone with AmEx to learn Marriott didn't have permission to cancel AND had not notified myself or AmEx. Brad was seemingly helpful, but suggested to me to "re-book" which would have been at a higher rate. I refused and AmEx resolved that issue.
Arrived the next day (12/31) at 130 and checked in. At 4 pm, the advertised checkin time, my room wasn't ready. At 4:35 I went to the front desk and was told the room wasn't ready, BUT if I wanted to move to a lower level floor they could check me in. One person, who I won't mention by name, for fear of him being punished for his honesty, told me point blank it was a lesser room than I had booked and paid for and not to move. I then asked to speak with Brad, who acted the day before as if he was in a position of authority. Brad told me the room wasn't a downgrade and if I "really wanted to check-in then I should just take the room that was available." No, thank you and you are dishonest. When I asked for my 5 pm dinner reservation to be moved, I was questioned why that would be necessary. Let's see, it's 440, I've been traveling, need to change and YOU still don't have me in a room. Reluctantly, Brad/Bryce called and moved the reservation to later.
From there we had the worst service. Waited for service EVERY single time at Mowry & Cotton. Ordered hot tea with drinks, it came out 20+ minutes later. Ordered more cream cheese for a bagel, it never was brought. Plates stacked everywhere outside from the breakfast buffet, including on our table inside, and no server to clear or clean them up for 30+ minutes. Birds flying everywhere and eating off plates because it was a mess anytime we dined outside. Felt like we were dining in a scene from the Birds movie! The bird man did what he could to keep the birds away, but nothing helps when dirty dishes are left sitting for lengthy periods!
On 1/3 the server outside at Thirsty Camel was painfully slow. Ended up going inside to get more drinks where she proceeded to make a comment about us not waiting. We waited and waited AND we were the only people outside. Glasses and plates stacked outside and not cleaned up for over an hour while we sat there. We ended up moving all the glasses to the other side of the fire pit to get them out of our way.
Amanda, at the pool, was great. She was kind, prompt. She deserves a raise.
I stayed at Phoenician Suites years ago and the service was impeccable. I convinced my boyfriend and his kids to join us this trip and was embarrassed I recommended this hotel.
I can unequivocally say the service was not 5 star, in most cases it was barely a 2. There is ZERO reason to return and pay the prices being charged and receive terrible service. Brad is in serious need of being trained!
Calling yourself a 5 star resort is like Carnival claiming to be a 5 star cruise ship. I don't cruise, but if I was, it wouldn't be on Carnival. I do enjoy 5 star resorts, but NOT this one anymore. Sadly. OH, and learned today that O had an $80 credit for breakfast through AmEx. Except their "policy" is that if you don't use the $80 then they charge you the $80 or any portion unused back to you! WTF?! Insanity.

findings.title: Matt H. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Went to the pool on the resort day pass. First, it looked like I was getting the final day bed but when I arrived the pool was empty. Made the best of the day with no one around and ordered food/drink. 
When the bill came we received an additional resort fee of $40. When we questioned the Phoenician they said we had to go through resort pass and then vice-versa. So no one took ownership of the charge and I had already paid the resort fee, so why was I charged another resort fee?!
Point is, I believe we could have just arrived without paying resort pass and then ordered poolside.

findings.title: Jennifer J. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The Phoenician is now a Marriott property with a brand spanking new gym/game room and spa and waterslide. Really love the upgrades and I can see why the Obamas and Jay Z Beyonce prefer staying here when in Scottsdale.

findings.title: Lindsay G. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Currently staying here. We have three casitas and the hotel is not a 5 star. Beautiful grounds but management doesn't seem to have their act together. We have had several issues we have had to follow up with. The casita we are in needs to be updated. Please see pics.

findings.title: Melissa F. (4/5)
findings.snippet: We loved our room with a Firetable  outside. We had a nice size suite and it was comfortable with excellent bedding and pillows. I didn't give 5 stars because the restaurant breakfast was bland. We also don't like that we couldn't access an ice machine out at the casitas. We had to wait for ice to be brought from the bar a at from our room. And the resort fee of $50 per day. They have extra events available but we had no interest in them. So we paid $100 for internet basically, and this should be free. This was an extremely expensive adventure and next time we will choose  a value hotel (not cheap just where you feel like it's fair.....we felt screwed at the Phoenician).

findings.title: Carrie U. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Staff, amazing. Rooms are clean and well appointed. Food on property is delicious. The game room for the kids is a huge hit, as was the slide! The Valet is amazing and the welcome we got was great, BUT the wifi situation sucks. 

Apparently from all the reviews online this wifi situation is an ongoing problem, so I would have expected not to have stayed in a luxury hotel without wifi during our stay- but sure enough... the wifi was not working when we were there. Or, it worked then pooped out. Good luck getting your work done on a laptop here. My advice, use your phone as a hotspot and expect everything else outside of the wifi to be great. 

Breakfast is a little bit of a mess with the buffet and service was REALLY slow. Like 20 minutes for a juice kind of slow. Also, I didn't think $80 for service charges was fair for two tables of four (we were two families split into two tables and wanted two bills, but they put everything on one bill instead of two then double charged us for the service plus a large party charge.) I wouldn't have minded paying it had they actually done something other than deliver food from the kitchen and bring juice after 20 minutes, but this was insane. We were so tired of waiting for the check at the end I didn't even bother complaining about the double charge- but just heads up, breakfast service sucks all around.

findings.title: Lacey P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Got a couples massage, over $800 leaving with some kind of chemical burn on my hands had to visit the dermatologist and waiting for them to heal still.

findings.title: Courtney B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Lovely resort with beautiful, clean amenities and kind service. I stayed for a work conference and enjoyed afternoons by the many beautiful pools. Pool service was fast and wonderful- lots of great poolside food and drink options. 
There are nearby hiking trails but none easily accessed by foot. Fortunately, there are rideshares available and bikes for rent. Lots of good restaurant options but prices are high.

findings.title: Sue H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: If you are a local (as I am), or staying at the hotel, you absolutely must enjoy a pedicure from Cynthia. She is the BEST technician I've ever experienced. The pedicure was perfect, she engaged but didn't talk the entire time, and the entire experience was a delight. My toes are gorgeous and I cannot recommend her enough!

findings.title: Amanda E. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Overcharged! Like another review, check your bill..... 

It's a nice place but the spa overcharged me for my services and what an absolute headache trying to fix it! 
It was their mistake. I was told one price and charged more. Call to fix it, and no one answers the phone and after calling a bunch of time, I finally get ahold of someone. 
Tell them about the charge and I'm on hold then on hold again and they sound like they don't know what they are doing. They tell me they have to talk to someone and call me back in a couple days? Just fix the problem! It was charged incorrectly! And when I ask questions, the girls just keeps saying the same thing over like she's reading from a script! So frustrating! 

For the price and the level pf place this is, the customer service should also be good and it has been an absolute pain trying to get someone to help me fix their mistake!

findings.title: Richard K. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Lovely hotel.  Unethical invoicing practice.   I had roughly $80 per day in Resort charges added to my check out bill.   This was not detailed when the room was booked not was it discussed when I checked in.   
Very sneaky and unethical.  Not something I expected from a Marriot property.

findings.title: Brandy J. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This place is absolutely BEAUTIFUL!!! The staff was AMAZING! Always pleasant and offering help.

My room was large, with a fridge and fully stocked bar. More than enough closet space AND drawers to mmake your stay more comfortable.  My room had a patio facing Camelback Mountain so I woke to a beautiful view every morning.

The bathroom held both a soaking tub and a roomy shower. I loved the separate little room for the toilet.

Received a wonderful m

findings.title: Alvin L. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Was in town visiting family and checked into the Phoenician for a night to use the pool / staycation. 

Property is beautiful and there were multiple pools on site (very nice pools with views of camelback mountain).

The rooms were clean and spacious as well. Stayed in a casita (some of which has a personal firepit out on the deck which can make a very romantic evening).

Resort fee comes with access to fitness classes. I was able to catch a yoga class prior to checking out and that was a nice way to start the morning - instructor was great and class is for everyone (with or without prior yoga experience).

The only area that didn't meet expectation was the service. Upon arrival / pulling up to the front of the hotel, we weren't offered any help with luggage or acknowledged by any of the staff members (not typical for a high end / luxurious property).

Overall - beautiful property and we had a good staycation.

findings.title: John S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Pay close attention to your bill.  I was charged for an honor bar bill.  What was it?  No one at the Phoenician can tell me what the charge represents.  Did they say they would remove the charge?  Twice in the last two weeks.  Have they removed the charge?  No.

I'll never go back to this establishment and I'm a Marriott Elite member.  The Phoenician is awful at customer service.

findings.title: C R. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I was excited to stay here with my friend. I was out getting food, and houskeeping (2 people) entered our room while my friend was sleeping in his pajamas. I was later told by Marriott phone representatives that they are not allowed to enter the room if we do not respond and if they see we are sleeping. Anyways, the 2 housekeeping employees ENTER the room while my friend was sleeping. My friend has anxiety and he pulled the covers over his head. They come close to his bed, POKE HIM on the shoulder twice and leave 2 water bottles near his bed. We had already gotten 4 water bottles from the front desk during check in so that nobody would enter our room. I called the front desk and they said housekeeping is not supposed to do that and that they would be calling me within 2 hours. NOBODY EVER CALLED. Then, the water would not turn cold, I called and they said it was summer and the water is warm...so a luxury resort can't have cold water? Really? Some of their rooms go for $4,000+. We used the tub and then the water would not drain. NONE OF THESE WERE ADDRESSED DURING CHECKOUT. I called Marriott and they asked Phoenician to contact me so Phoenician lied and said they called me and closed the case, even though they NEVER reached out to me in any shape or form.
 
This was supposed to be my MOST luxurious hotel experience but was my WORST customer service experience. I will never visit the Phoenician again. What an awful, incompetent hotel this is.
 
I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE TO ANYONE.
 
GOOD RIDDANCE.

findings.title: Scott L. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Did a quick summer getaway at the Phoenician during slow season.  The resort was quiet as temps are high in the summer but there's still plenty of relaxing to do during the day and fun stuff to do during the dawn and dusk periods.

Since it's slow season, there are plenty of deals.  Resort credits, free self-parking, room upgrades, etc... and best of all you get great service from the Staff who has more time to interact with you.

Spent four relaxing nights although a cricket in our room forced us to a different room half-way thru - couldn't find the constant chirper.   Day wise we went to:  the quiet, clean and well-equipped gym, lighted pickleball courts (4) with available paddles and balls, driving range with cart, bottled water, and clubs for a small fee, tennis courts, and multiple pools with food & bar service!  If needed, golf cart rides to and from the various buildings.

As for food and drink, we had drinks at the main lobby bar and poolside.  Since it was slow season, their main open-air and enclosed restaurant was undergoing renovation thus breakfast was available at the Tavern near the golf shop.  The breakfast options were unique and tasty - see pics and service was on point.

Overall, an enjoyable and relaxing stay with no crowds!  Will make this an August ritual....

findings.title: Marion W. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Alright... I'm going to sound like a spoiled kid, and own it. I've traveled A LOT, and this hotel was WAY out of my budget, but I won a giveaway (not affiliated with the hotel) for a weekend + spa treatment there and went late May 2024, so I will give my opinion as if I had paid for it, even though for free, we had an amazing time. 

1. The grounds
The hotel is on a BEAUTIFUL property. You're right by the camelback mountain and everywhere you look is beautiful, you get there and you're WOW. The hotel entrance, the pools, it's all huge and big windows, beautiful. What you expect from a Luxury collection hotel
The pools are nice and big, though on day 2 they closed the kid friendly pool for the entire day after someone had an accident. I would have been livid if I came for this and had to find another smaller pool to hang out at because it made the other pools even more crowded (especially on this holiday weekend!)

2. The rooms
That's where the disappointment starts. If I had paid for the room, it would have made me sick. I expected something amazing for the price and it was just a normal hotel room, with a big bath and some nice mirror lights. The amenities are not all that luxurious.
We traveled with our 9 months old, and the crib was horrible.. are these from the 60s or what? My baby refused to sleep in there, making the trip tougher for mama since he had to sleep in bed with me = not a resting sleep. 

3. The service
I'm so split there, we had some amazing waiters, but also some very meh experiences. I had shipped some diapers and sunscreen to the hotel (do that all the time when traveling with a baby) and it was the most complicated thing ever to get my hands on it. For a luxury hotel, it should have been waiting in my room for me. Instead I had to chase a fedex guy 2 days in a row because the office was closed. Ridiculous.

4. The food and drinks
Overpriced AF. Good food, great service, but omg...  the prices! Whatever you're paying for your stay, double that for your food. The prices by the pool are also extravagant, but that's what you get when traveling to a nice hotel. The steakhouse was a great experience though, and an excellent meal + the service was outstanding, they saw me struggling to put baby to sleep so I could enjoy my meal and not disturb anyone around, and they gifted us a bottle of champagne to take to our room + the dessert. Thank you so much to the manager there, I felt seen in a good way.

5. The spa
Super super meh experience. They spent millions on redoing the facility so yea, the facility is nice. But that's it. They made it SO DIFFICULT to book, it took weeks of back and forth and in the end there was no more room for my husband to get a facial... experience cut short. They could only fit us on the monday when we were leaving (mind you we were getting there on Friday). Our treatments were over a thousand dollar (for 2 massages and a facial, WHAT?!) so we booked a babysitter on our last day to watch our baby so we could go enjoy the spa until time to leave. I did all that through the concierge, who was really good (ps: their babysitting partner is amazing, responsive and sweet, I highly recommend using them if you go there). They refused to let us keep our room for a few extra hours ON A MONDAY, I had to call and throw a fit explaining that we had a spa reservation and I needed the room for a few extra hours (just a late check out yall...) so the sitter could watch my kid. Sounded like I asked for the favor of the century and they gave me ONE extra hour. That cut our spa visit super short, I did not get to enjoy the expensive facility, and our massages were so meh. I can get a better one for $120 back home. Facial was also super meh, didn't find it worth it at all. 

Overall, you pay for the grounds. if you like golfing, the golf looks gorgeous. The gym is nice. The rooms are meh. The pools are good. The food is expensive but good. The spa is not worth it unless you're loaded.

Have fun with that. Meanwhile, I won't be returning.

findings.title: Alex K. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Bad service staff disrespected me fallowed to my vehicle didn't feel wanted wouldn't come back to hotel want a free room for this disrespect

findings.title: Dan M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This was our third year in a row visiting this destination resort and it continues to exceed expectations. Location: Considering the fact The Phoenician Resort is located in the booming metropolis of Phoenix/Scottsdale, its proximity to Camelback mountain is one redeeming factor that makes the venue even more spectacular. Service: 10 stars. Service has always been excellent, but this year, Bryce (our check-in agent at the front desk) set the bar even higher. First, he remembered our request made 3 days earlier by phone when we asked if our Casita included a Nespresso machine. (He explained the adjacent Canyon Suites have Nespresso machines, but the Casitas do not). No worries as we could bring our travel-Nespresso machine for this 4-day trip. Yet he surprised us with a welcome card, anniversary greeting and stated, "Hey since we couldn't upgrade you to the Canyon Suites, we decided to bring a little of the Canyon suites to your Casita and included the Nespresso song on our welcome card."  Now that's a concierge-level of service if I have ever seen one. The Casita's in their own right are fabulous, spacious and first class. 3 different swimming pools, a great waterslide and 4-5 restaurants on-site mean you don't need to go anywhere off property. The fitness facility is nothing short of fabulous. The Phoenician is highly recommended and a destination you won't soon forget.

findings.title: Lorrie E. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We decided on a last minute girls trip for relaxation. The rooms have amazing balconies with couch and table setup. Great for coffee and sunrise view. The room in service was a must to give the daughter a morning to remember. The rooms are quiet and the bathroom, vanity sitting and two closets were great additions to 3 women getting ready. The adult pool area was top notch. Many great servers but Jared was my fav. He anticipated when we needed our next round. And the pool food was excellent. The slide in the kids area made me at least ten years younger. The spa experience was the key to our stress free weekend. The 80 minute massages are the key to this Phoenix rising from the ashes.

findings.title: Denise C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: LUXURY is the perfect word to describe this hotel.   From the Valet to ground maintenance personnel-everyone greets you.   The Chef's prepare delicious food and the hotel ambience is superb.  The rooms are spacious and so comfortable.   Only complaint is we only had a short stay.  We will be back.

findings.title: T. L. C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We attended the Derby Party on 5/4 and I would rate the party 5 stars.  The food and festivities were top-notch.  
Several in my party ordered non-alcoholic mojitos and they were great.  When we order a second round, we received what appeared to be virgin margaritas (sour mix with a lime but no salt).  We told our waiter how good the first round was and asked if they could remake the second round.  A few minutes later a bartender approached and said, "I understand you don't like the drinks".  I mentioned they tasted like a margarita minus the salt rim.  He insisted it was a mojito.  I then pointed out there was no mint in the drink.  He then said he "ground up" the mint and once again insisted they were mojitos.  If he had "ground" the mint there would have been flakes of mint in the drink and it would have tasted minty, which it didn't.  In short, he lied.  He was very condescending and rude.  I brought the situation to a manager  who advised they would take care of it.  We never received replacement drinks or any further dialog about the matter.  Later, one member of our party who was unaware of what had happened order another virgin mojito and received a drink like the original with mint and club soda on top of what appeared to be lime.  The issue here is not the mix up of drinks, but the aggressive nature of the bartender and the fact he lied.  I've called the hotel and left two messages and haven't received a call back.  At a 5 star hotel, you don't expect an employee to argue and lie to you and when it's brought to the management's attention they are not interested in resolving the matter.

findings.title: Andrew M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Platinum Marriott member dealing with over two hours wait
The drinks thank gd calmed my nerves waiting but gd forbid we should French fries and NOT YUKKA fries
Clearly the name fits
And gd for it we should even have normal food,
Food to help a starving belly
Where are chicken wings?
Where are French fries?
For me four seasons and ritz Carlton hence if they even exist
Don't recommend

findings.title: Maggie W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is such a wonderful resort.  The staff are the the most helpful we have ever seen, from the second you walk in the door.  Great pool area and great food at the restaurants.  Beautiful area and close to the Fashion Mall downtown.   Highly recommend.

findings.title: Iris P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: When in the desert  Staying at the Phoenician in Scottsdale was the best experience! Sitting poolside for 10 hours sipping on frozen cocktails is the life! Happy to go back and spend another 10 days at this beautiful place! They have multiple pools and the fact that it's never crowded and I can enjoy my time was a blessing! Not many kids at the resort which is a huge plus and spending our mini honeymoon here was the best choice we could've made! Thank you for making our stay amazing!!!

findings.title: Janet B. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Their tag line is "A Luxury Collection".  Sorry Phoenician, you fell WAY short! Upon our arrival at 4:30pm we were assigned room 6150 which is on the top floor and we were thanked for being Marriott members. Days prior we were contacted by customer relations and my husband let them know it was our 39th anniversary. We do A LOT of staycations in Arizona and this was a HUGE disappointment. Friday night we went to their Tavern restaurant which was a nice golf course view and the food was mediocre. Saturday morning we went off property for breakfast to one of our favorites but not before the valet brought us the wrong car ~ it was funny once they finally located our car but seriously? We did like walking around checking out a new place and the employees seem content over all. We decided to get an afternoon cocktail to be told the Thirsty Camel in the main lobby doesn't open until 2 so we hung out and at 2 a terrific server, Kelsie, did a fantastic job! She was friendly, knowledgeable and was funny when she had to explain the bar was not equipped with a blender to make any frozen concoction whatsoever. For dinner we tried Mowry & Cotton. Appeared to be a great place. Appetizers were good, our server was nice but when our food came we ended up eating separately because they way over cooked my husband's medium ribeye. Not ideal for an anniversary dinner and $283 was definitely way over priced for what was served. I had the Mowry burger which was flavorful but the fries were the same greasy ones they serve at the Tavern and not fresh. This is the one place, however, someone actually said Happy Anniversary. The Marketplace was a great little spot to grab coffee and their shining star  is definitely Kelsie at The Thirsty Camel~ she definitely worked her tail off & it was easy to see she was a standout employee. Big downfalls were the algae covered fountain that never ran and also our view for the weekend as well as the constant parade of cars in and out directly across from our balcony, also the room was older and worn and not fixed properly ~ just painted over, we had turn down service on Friday but not Saturday, had to call for towels and ice (you can't get ice yourself), cobwebs and spider  in plain sight and a gross something on the bathtub ( see photos). It was certainly not a luxury collection weekend ~ far from it. Several employees knew were experiencing problems but it seemed to be nothing out of the ordinary and we certainly have been to much better Marriotts in the area. Putting a few extra goodies on a bathroom tray doesn't make a stay luxurious ~ you can do better Marriott!!!

findings.title: Karina V. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We went here for a bachelorette and enjoyed the Afternoon Tea. Everything from start to finish was impeccable. Decor, service, and ambiance. The champagne option is wonderful and they never left our drinks empty. The tea was delicious, sandwiches, and scones were to die. The star was the desserts! We cannot wait to go back!

findings.title: Walter H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Had the opportunity to stay at The Phoenician for 3 days.  The resort is beautiful with some amazing views!  The service here is amazing and the staff couldn't be nicer!

The room was very comfortable, and had a large balcony.  Comfortable bedding and the bath towels were plush.  Definitely a great space to relax and just enjoy the setting.

The restaurants on site are also very nice.  Room service is available and was also very good.  All in all it was a great trip.

findings.title: Angela H. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I attended a 3 day retreat in January 2024. The property is lovely and clean. The conference rooms were spacious and comfortable. My interaction with the staff was pleasant. Housekeeping didn't get to my suite until after 3p. It wasn't too much of an inconvenience. The suite was nice and clean. However, the furniture layout was weird. There was a table and two chairs directly in front of the full-length mirror, which made it hard to use. The bathroom was spacious and stocked with things I may have needed. Overall, I was pleased with my stay. I would definitely return so I could experience more of the resort. I spent most of the time in the conference rooms. The grounds were a lovely backdrop to the beautiful sunrises and sunsets I was able to witness.

findings.title: Gigi S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: my girlfriends and I had a great stay here! excellent food, lovely staff, and really amazing service. would 100% go back again!

findings.title: Sharon G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Where do I even begin! The grounds are beautiful, however we did encounter 1 homeless person charging their phone in the pathway down to the spa. There's so much room explore on the grounds, just tie up those sneakers and go for a walk.
The staff was from around the country and all super friendly and it's so close to popular sites but tucked away you don't realize the big city is a stones throw away. We'll be back!

findings.title: Michael B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We have had high tea at the Phoenician now a number of times and my wife has gone every year for many years.  We went this year again and it really is a delightful experience.  The ambiance is so comforting and the service is impeccable.  We have had Wanda and actually request her because she is so sweet.  They are all very wonderful servers but we just have taken to her from many years ago.

This is a special event and is ongoing but fun even more so around the holidays.  

You will get the classic finger foods and as much as you want.  This includes scones and amazing deserts and the f course your choice f amazing teas served in beautiful tea-ware!  And my favorite - bottomless champagne- often Perrier and Jouet!  

While the price is not for the faint of heart at about $450, for a great experience, it is truly a treat.  I highly recommend doing this at least once!

findings.title: Keegan K. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I'm not sure luxury is the word to describe this resort. I would have to say it's comfortable, doable and clean.

findings.title: Nikki D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Definitely a luxury collection resort everything has top-notch. The properties is stunning so much to do and the service is superb. One of our favorite places to stay whenever we are in town everything from the Pickleball to the tennis courts to the swimming pools and the multiple restaurants they have everything you need!!

findings.title: Linda T. (1/5)
findings.snippet: The description "luxury" needs to be removed from the description. With the price tag... $26 to park .... $70. For a dirty martini, a shot of Japanese whiskey & two diet cokes.... $80 buffet with 20% gratuity... now $96 a person, I would expect top shelf service. Our cutlery was dumped on the table. The buffet was small with few options... the food was adequate but not the quality I would expect. When we were ready for the second course we were told to keep our dirty cutlery.... We ordered four cups of coffee with cream and sugar.... One spoon to share! Save your money, don't eat a celebratory meal here.

findings.title: Rachel B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Came here for a family vacation after having had a previous pleasant experience at the Phoenician, we wanted to also share this experience with our kids. We booked two rooms, for four nights and our rooms were located on the second floor. Upon packing our luggage we discovered a GIANT cockroach--imagine the horror on my face! I have 4 luggage bags potentially full of roach eggs, I've had 18 month old, 11 and 12 year old, and my husband and I potentially lying with these roaches at night! We immediately contacted the manager, who did not seem too suprised by this -- and had more of an "oops" attitude towards the situation. The manager, Devin, offered us a 300$ comp for our stay. Mind you, I have spent 2000$ in JUST food and drinks while on this trip, not to mention the nightly rooms. I feel disregarded as a customer, I am mortified and disgusted which says a lot considering this is suppose to be upwards of a 5 star hotel---I have seen better in motels. Will not be coming back here.

findings.title: Daniel C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I never write hotel reviews but the service here is horrendous 

Staff is just not helpful with requests, have to ask for everything several times, rude concierge and front desk

Was told all restaurants are closed and I have to order room service then see a couple eating at a restaurant ten feet from me 20 mins later 

It's crazy. I have traveled a lot and stayed at some of the nicest hotels in the world as well as many mid tier and lower range. Staff vibe and treatment is of paramount importance and although the property has pretty areas and a nice 24/7 jacuzzi, the service (or lack thereof) makes it not worth it

findings.title: Dustin C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Okay, what's not to love about visiting The Phoenician in December, with record temps in the 80's?!?!
As soon as we arrived, you could tell the staff took pride in being kind, accommodating and making sure the stay was above expectations.   The groundskeepers have done a wonderful job making the landscaping look stunning.  The tennis courts and pickle ball courts were top notch!  The fitness center was spotless, and had a ton of fitness equipment.  The rooms were spacious and well taken care of.  
We are at the Phoenician Tavern, and the service and food was fantastic.  We also spent a lot of time at the Thirsty Camel.  Great bourbon selections, and delicious wings and appetizers!  
Overall,

findings.title: Jason K. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Gorgeous place. So big you could get lost. Golfers dream. Staff and service are excellent.
They have casting available and worked great. Yet my intern at times on my devices lagged. Big rooms with a great sitting area and work space.

findings.title: Jeff P. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Thanksgiving Brunch?? Don't bother!  Yes this is the famous Phoenician resort but unfortunately they know it and simply behave in an elitist manner that implies they don't need your business.  When inquiring about Thanksgiving brunch, no one bothers to call you back or answer any questions. You can't get a simple straight answer such as "We are unfortunately booked"   

Even the manager's response below is fake. It's a cut and paste that he applies to every 1 star review. The apathy can be seen even there. That's how this place runs. 

If you want world class service, go to the Royal Palms next door. The hotel is well managed and run. They pick up the phone and treat you like a guest. I've dined at the Royal Palms for Thanksgiving 3 years in a row  and it's been a wonderful experience. We were going to try the Phoenician for a change and the absolutes horrible service made me recognize and appreciate the Royal Palms. The manager at the Phoenician needs to train his or her staff better on etiquette and basic professionalism.  They could start by training the staff to answer the phone and be courteous.

There are so many better options for Thanksgiving brunch in Phoenix Scottsdale and Paradise Valley.  Don't waste your effort here. They obviously don't want your business IMHO

findings.title: Rajiv K. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Pretty spacious hotel with a number of pools in the middle. Huge golf course and spa attached, which I didn't get to visit. Amazing foodie options throughout. Spacious resort both with rooms and common areas. I was here for a work event and think it's a great event space. I could also see myself coming back to just visit and enjoy the amenities. I'm

findings.title: Chad B. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Online reviews are a tricky beast. With all the AI out there it is quite difficult to discern if you are reading a real experience from a real human. This I can assure you is genuine and mainly intended as a word of caution so no one else has to suffer the experience my wife and I endured at the Phoenician in September of 2023. 

This review has nothing to do with the room quality or amenities or facilities, those are all quite nice and frankly should be for the nightly rate you are paying. This review ties directly to the staff and their lack of care for their guests. 

We were there for a weekend with family and friends attending a wedding. On the day of the wedding my wife went to the pool for one hour by herself. She got her towels and set her things down on a chair. She then received a phone call that she took and spoke for 15 minutes next to the pool with her back turned to the chair. At this time someone grabbed all of her things including her purse and sandals. When she turned back around and realized her things were gone she immediately alerted the staff including waitresses and the towel clerk who had been working the area. This pool probably had 20 guests at the pool at this time, not a lot of activity. All the staff had the same lethargic response, "I am sorry maam, there is nothing we can do." 

Now let me be crystal clear, we are not ascribing blame directly to the hotel. They certainly cannot be responsible for all guests' belongings at all times and my wife made a costly error in judgment, although an unconscious one, she never should have turned her back to her items. 

We immediately shut down credit cards but saw that the culprit already tried to charge $2K+ at Neiman Marcus just down the street, so now we had validation that this was no accident or misplaced items. There was one gentleman that worked the hotel security, I believe his name was Thomas, and he was the only one that took any ownership of the issue and showed an ounce of empathy towards our predicament. The extent of effort from the rest of management at the Phoenician was to blink, stand still and continue to say "I am sorry, there is nothing we can do." One gentleman who worked at the front desk (I wish I had his name) even had the nerve to tell us, "Things get stolen here all the time" as if they had as much control over this as the weather. Further, if that statement is true, maybe an examination of security protocols might be a priority. 

Rather than attend our wedding we spent the reception filling out a police report. We knew the chances of recovery were slim and the financial loss was significant ($500+) but not catastrophic. I can hear the critics whispering, "first world problems." The point is there is an absolute dearth of security at this resort. I can't list all the shortcomings but here are a few: There are no cameras anywhere on the three pool decks (at least that is what we were told), All gates to the pools remain wide open at all times. I have stayed at resorts who charge half as much as the phonecian and they still require a room key to access the pools. The parking lot entry attendant showed no enforcement as far as which cars were allowed on property. We were waived through, never asked for a name or room number.
