If I was a thief I couldn't ask for a more vulnerable environment. 

Here is the kicker. 7 hours after the purse was first stolen another charge was attempted on our canceled credit card BACK ON THE PHOENICIAN property. We thought this was our chance, how many establishments are even open at 10 PM to accept payment on the property? Less than five we thought. We alerted hotel management immediately and again the blank stares, the nonchalance, complete and utter deflection, "I am sorry, we can't track that." How easy would it have been upon our initial claim to tell their staff "If you run a credit card that is denied then alert security immediately." With today's tech and ubiquitous communication that is such an easy catch. You would think at $700/night there might be a modicum of effort or assistance for their guests. 

We were routed to some off-sight Marriott risk assessor that did not respond to us for three weeks only to tell us "our investigation results in no compensation to the guest." I can only imagine the depths they went into that investigation. 

Moral of the Story: Don't take anything valuable to the pool 

Second Moral of the Story: Don't rely on the staff. Their customer service extends as far as reading a script, over and over again. They are sorry, but there is nothing they can do, ahem, willing to do.

findings.title: Rae C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My family and I came here to celebrate our 10th wedding anniversary. We brought our little furbaby for the experience and she was treated so good! 

Listen, I will tell you the real deal and BAABYYYY!!! This place is expensive but worth every penny. Every restaurant was on point!!!! The food, ambiance and service here is AMAZINGGGGGG!!! It was a one-time experience as we'd like to see other parts of Arizona.

findings.title: Jillian T. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Join the afternoon tea service and I gotta say, Arizona knows how to do it well. The service here is impeccable. We had Sabrina (Gal Gadot's doppelgänger) assisting us and she did not miss a beat. 

Full tea service includes 3-course plated meal for $100.

Starting off with the White Coconut Creme tea which tasted great by itself, with sugar or with milk. The dynamic of the flavor changed each time I added in a different component. 

Not to mention, unlimited tea sandwiches! I really enjoyed the asparagus+parma ham, the soft poached lobster salad and the lemon+thyme chicken salad. 

By the time I got to the scones course, I was already more than halfway full. Then came the last course, the desserts in which I was bursting at the seams and had to box up and take home.

The team even sent us off with a tin of their peppermint tea. Nothing short of an amazing experience.

findings.title: Alana P. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We had a wonderful stay at the Phoenician!
We stayed in a casita with a lovely view of the pool and pond. Our spacious suite was updated and very comfortable.Where to begin with the exceptional staff?! The Valet, front desk all superb! Every staff member we met asked if there was anything they could do to make our stay even better! 
Now for the best part we ate dinner at Mowry and Cotton. We arrived early and the host gave us a little tour and history of the Praying Monk.
Our server was so helpful in helping us make decisions on a fabulous menu. The fresh salmon ( flown in) was perfectly cooked. I could have licked the plate on the cheesecake! I really can't say enough on how much we enjoyed this resort! I highly recommend!

findings.title: Happy G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is really a 4.5 star resort. The resort itself is a little dated but maintained immaculately. Meanwhile, the drinks and food were amazing! I usually assume the F&B at a place of this size will be average, nothing offensive, nothing outstanding. That was far from the case here. From a perfect iced latte at the coffee shop to the wonderful breakfast that was shockingly accurate despite multiple substitutions and requests to the gyros, guac and fantastic cocktails by the pool and the cocktails in the lobby bar... Everything was fantastic and reasonably priced given the location. The gym was also top of the line. I would definitely stay here again.

findings.title: Lidia M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I decided to do a staycation for my birthday. I've always wanted to go to The Phoenician and I'm glad I finally got the opportunity. From start to end, my stay was amazing. I requested an early check-in and when I arrived I was so happy my room was ready. The room was amazing. It was just myself and my boyfriend, but the room was very spacious. After unpacking we decided to go to the pool. There is a separate adults only pool which I appreciated. I will say, my only complaint was that the service at pool was a bit slow and we did have to wait some time to get our order taken and brought to us. We also had dinner at J&G which is inside the resort. After dinner we went to the bar in the lounge and our bartender was amazing and made some of the best drinks I've had. The resort is beautiful, but what made my stay amazing was the customer service. If you have the opportunity to stay at this resort I would highly recommend it.

findings.title: Karen R. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Went here for a work event recently &, after the build-up of so many people saying how amazing the place is, I wasn't too impressed. Maybe it's just the area we were in, but it was shabby & old-fashioned looking. Also, in the ballroom we were in, the carpet was brown & they had wires running across 2 areas that were held down w brown tape, so you couldn't really see them. And people couldn't. All day, people were tripping over them, including me. One of the ladies was walking back from getting her lunch and went crashing down! Landed face first on the ground. Her soup splashed up into her hair. It was terrible. Maybe you want to rethink how you cover wires.

Gave a 4th star because the buffet lunch was fantastic.

findings.title: Ashley H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Great 18 hole golf course with great options or cafes and restaurants for family with babies!! If you are near paradise valley, a great place to come and enjoy food & spa. Great pool for kids

findings.title: David M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Absolutely beautiful hotel. Completely luxurious with wonderful pools and restaurants. The service is second to none. Kawai the bartender is just a delightful goddess of happiness.  This hotel and their staff is all upside.

findings.title: lisa T. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
If you are looking for a great family staycation, I would go elsewhere.  I spent a whole week looking at reviews to pick our Father's Day staycation.  Unfortunately this resort missed the mark in almost every category.  Our room 4066 - overlooked a concrete jungle.  The air conditioner made such an awful squealing noise at night that we could not sleep.  We ended up having to turn off the AC and sweat it out so our kids could sleep.  
We made the most of our time by the pool but it was definitely lacking in the fun family staycation vibe that is found at so many of the other resorts we have tried in the area. The kids activities offered were mostly for extra fees (crafts, decorating sweets, build a bear) and unfortunately did not interest my children.  (Ages 8 and 10)
On a positive note since I am a Marriott Bonvoy silver elite member,  I did receive early check in and late check out!!  However for over $400/night, I did have higher expectations for our stay.  The competition is tough in the area and this wasn't worth the money.

findings.title: Marcus G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Excellent stay here over the weekend. Rooms were spacious, golf course was fantastic. Thank you so much and especially to Javier at the front desk for helping us with our accommodations!

findings.title: Mary M. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Very disappointing. Had to call room service every day to have our room serviced and clean towels. No turn down service at night, which I thought would be normal at a luxury resort. Also, bed sheets were not changed after 5 nights of stay. I've had better service at a Comfort Inn.

findings.title: Brett S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This hotel is in major need of maintenance and customer service. The first issue I had was the toilet seat was broken. It took them 3 hours to come and fix it as the front desk stated they had numerous maintenance calls. I didn't get that resolved until almost 2am. The next issue is their shower was broken. Water barely came out, which is not the worst part of it. The worst part is the fact that they had a loose handle and the screw was so loose that it came out. I almost stepped on a screw while I was showering at a 5 diamond hotel. This place should be no more than a 2 diamond. Lastly, I visited their pool in the evening to notice that everyone had maintenance issues. There was tile missing everywhere and the areas it was missing, the objects were sharp. I came close to cutting myself several times against the wall so I left the pool area. AAA and Forbes, you need to revisit this place and downgrade them.

findings.title: Tim M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is one of the best resorts I have stayed in the last 5 years. The amenities were outstanding, the rooms were perfect, and the food was next level. It is a must stay in Scottsdale, Arizona.

findings.title: Nick C. (3/5)
findings.snippet: This used to be my favorite staycation spot in the valley. It's a nice property with super friendly staff and secluded so it has a true resort feel. Unfortunately, their prices have gone way up and it's just not worth the value.  It's a $300-$400 a night hotel at best.  It's literally cheaper for me to fly to California and stay at an oceanfront property, so that's what I've been doing instead. I hope they bring their prices back down again because it is a nice spot.

findings.title: Kevina M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Dear The Phoenician management.....Your staff is simply the best. I am so so moved and touched by the gestures of kindness. Hannah at the front desk went above and beyond ....Hannah at the pool is sooo sweet too telling us where to go to lunch and dinner. And Christine at the pool ...above and beyond sweet and pure class. I've been coming to this hotel since I was a little girl....wonderful memories. Anyway....I cannot thank you enough for your customer service. We will be back! God Bless you all!:-) Xoxo

findings.title: Erica H. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I do really like this hotel, but it's a bit overpriced. For over 1k per night, our room had views of the parking lot and was pretty far from the pool. The outside of the hotel feels very 70's ish, but Inside the rooms and the lobby are lovely and look updated. 

Pros:
Friendly/nice staff
Huge, clean bathroom
Spacious room
Several dining options 
Several seating options at the pool
Warm pool
Attentive pool staff for food
Decent breakfast at Morrow and Cotton 
Golf cart service around the property 

Cons: 
Terrible pillows- my head was flat on the mattress they were so soft 
Mediocre food at the pool (not a fan of Greek food-wish it was regular "bar food")
Mediocre food at the Tavern (friends burger was straight up raw) 
Property is so spread out, so you can't forget anything in your room after going to the pool
Only saw one hot tub (filled with little kids and no parents)

Some things I would suggest is:
Add a water station in the lobby-with to go cups
Offer complimentary coffee on weekends (saw it Thursday only)

findings.title: Erin S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: When it comes to the reservations desk, ask for Javier and trust me, he's the best! He fixed a mixup on my reservation right away, was appropriately apologetic and was incredibly professional!  We are now comfortably situated in our proper room (ie: what we paid for) and it's clean, comfy and has a great view of the pool! I'm so grateful to Javier for getting our vacation back on track! Kudos to him!!

findings.title: Sherry W. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Overpriced, understaffed and in need of updating!
Rooms where $1200 a night.  We waited 6 hours to get our room and didn't end up with the room that we booked.  Room was average.  Smudges on walls and dings, nicks on furniture.  Wall behind sink in bathroom was greasy with dirt.  Water pressure was super low.   We said something at front desk but nothing happened.
Cabana service was hard to find....short staffed.  We walked back into the lobby after a night downtown and couldn't find anyone at desk or anyone at all on first floor.  Where is everyone???
Spa was lovely although services are super overpriced.   Massage was $330...a simple manicure (no gel or acylic), just a shaping and polish was $150.    Crazy prices.   
Bar inside lobby was lovely, although tough to find the one server who was so busy so ran around so much and was very flustered.

findings.title: Jack S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Had a great experience here. You get what you pay for - and it is well worth it! Very kind and attentive staff who will go out of their way to know your name and help you out. Beautiful property and landscaping with breathtaking views. Everything is super clean and well maintained. Our room was spacious with a humongous bathroom equipped with a bidet, 2 sinks on opposite sides, a large closet, and a shower with a bench in it. Beds were made both days, and a quick walk outside to our fire table (which unfortunately didn't work, but we were to lazy to call to get fixed), as well as patio with views of the mountain just added to the great experience we had. Tons of dining options, as well as stuff to do around the property. Loved the large hot tub, and the other pools were well designed. Would highly recommend staying here. Wish we would've been comped for parking because our room wasn't ready yet (weren't given parking passes), and had to pay for it to golf. Other than that, 5/5 stay.

findings.title: Sarah S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We stayed here last year for my birthday for our second time and it truly blew me away. The grounds are exceptional and they have the most beautiful cactus garden that you should not miss! It's free and pretty big. Walking through first thing in the morning with our coffee in hand was our favorite. 

We also loved the pool. There was fast and kind poolside service with a great selection of snacks and drinks. Loooved the guacamole. 

Also we deeply love anywhere that gives you free slippers (and a robe to hangout in your room in). So this place was 10/10 for us. 

If you're local, try to go in the off season! Sometimes they offer better deals than usual.

findings.title: Manny G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Wow! Thank You! Every year we celebrate my wife's Birthday month. This years celebration ended with a weeks stay. There are no words for the hospitality and professionalism that was extended to us. From the valets and porters who greeted us daily to the Front desk staff ( Clarence is the man)and Restaurant and Bar staff. The room and views are exceptional. Daily room service leaves the room looking and feeling fresh. The grounds are immaculately kept. It was nicely decorated for the Holidays not overly done just enough to remind you that its Christmas. The resort has several dining and Bar options that are very good. The golfing is Top notch and the Spa is nice. Luxury does come at a price so I get it if not everyone's experience is the same although if you have any issues the staff that is staff is customer service driven and will make it right. Until next time ( in the very near Future ). Cant wait to come back.

findings.title: MoShai G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This review is strictly for the Holiday Tea Experience which I thoroughly enjoyed! 

My friend and I decided to do Holiday Tea at the Phoenician and start a holiday tradition. It was a great time! I arrived early so sat at the bar and had a dirty martini! One of the best I have ever had! The bartender was great and it was wonderful listening to the pianist while waiting for my friends to arrive. 

The Holiday Tea Experience was amazing 

- The hostess was pleasant and so nice. 
- I love we get a photo in front of the tree with tea cup ornaments 
- The staff was amazing! 
- My friends and I all got the Royal Tea which including our choice of tea and Standard Bubbly and the four courses - lite bites with pickled deviled eggs (yummy) the pastries were delish too

Overall, the experience was worth every penny and cant wait to return!

findings.title: Gabriel W. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We arrived for a conference and ended up at the last room on the furthest corner of the hotel. Worst view of an HVAC Unit on a roof you could imagine, two double beds when we asked for a king, and just paid $110 for a really bad burger and chicken sandwich. I won't be spending much time in the room... ugh!

We've had pretty bad luck in the past but I don't think this is all our luck, I think this whole wing could use an update, kind of musty!

findings.title: Nicholas P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We took my in-laws to The Phoenician for the Holiday Afternoon Tea. It was an amazing experience and they loved it! We opted for the royal tea which came with bottomless good champagne.  First, they took a family photo in front of a cute little Christmas tree adorned in tea cups. Then we were seated at a table next to the window with wonderful views of the surrounding area. Once seated, we had a selection of 19 different teas and a full pot of tea was provided to each person (I opted for coffee).  The first course is finger sandwiches. The deviled egg, lobster sandwich, and salmon sandwich were the best, but everything was honestly good. Next up were two scones, one buttermilk and one cranberry nut. On the table were Devonshire cream, strawberry preserve, and lemon curd, all of which were delicious on the scones. The last course was a plate of pastries of all different varieties. My favorite was the mango and lemon ones.  Overall the staff was incredible, the views amazing, and food delicious. Could not ask for a better experience!

findings.title: Amy C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We stayed here for five nights for our anniversary. We had a lovely room on the backside of the property. We were initially disappointed our suite upgrades didn't happen, but we were happy with our room. The grounds are beautiful. Lots to do on the property and a short uber ride to the mall and shopping area. We ate at all the restaurants on the property. The only complaint I have about the restaurants is the pool menu is extremely limited. I had a hard time finding something to eat while at the pool.  We had breakfast at mowry and cotton every morning with no complaints. The staff there were awesome. We had a special anniversary dinner there one night and had a great meal. The pools were fun and there are plenty of lounge chairs.  The pool staff are very attentive. All the staff at the Phoenician were great. We enjoyed the gym and the game room during our stay. Thank you for a great week!

findings.title: Liz J. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The hotel itself is beautiful. There are more intimate courtyard areas that were beautifully lit, as well as lots of space down by the pool. The entrance itself is quite something with the large fountain and great for photo ops (if you're into that sort of thing). The rooms were also very spacious and clean. 

I wish I could remember the bar tender's name at the main hotel bar because he was great. He gave us excellent recommendations and made some custom mixed drinks for us that were delicious.

One member of our group got a little inebriated during our stay and the hotel staff were very discrete when helping us get them from the taxi back to their room, which we were very thankful for. The professionalism here is impeccable. Additionally, we were staying at the hotel at the same time as a group of a-list athletes and I felt the staff treated our group with the same respect as them and did not favour them over us in any obvious way. Very rare to find nowadays!

Finally, a few of us used the spa and I can honestly say the facial I had there was the best facial I have ever had. Considering I spent eleven years between LA and Vegas that should tell you just how good it was. I really wish I could remember the girl's name (she was brunette and I'd guess early 20s). Fantastic hotel and experience.

findings.title: Malisa R. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I've heard such great things about The Phoenician, so I was surprised when I arrived. Don't get me wrong, this hotel is nice, but a little dated. For the price, I was anticipating the hotel to be a little more luxurious. 

Once I entered the grounds, my Uber had to twirl around to get to the front. Everyone I encountered was so nice and friendly. Marriott does a great job with hiring friendly people! 

This resort is giant! I was happy that my hotel room was not too far from the lobby and didn't require a ride to get there. 

This property is huge. I was super impressed with the gorgeous gym and the amenities. There is a Drybar on site! Plus, the restaurants on site were really good too. Just be mindful of the hours they are open. 

My hotel room was large, clean, but a little dated. No complaints, just a standard room. I did have a nice view of the mountains. 

Would I pick this hotel again? There are nicer Marriott locations for the price point in the Scottsdale area. Camelback is my all time favorite Marriott. Also, JW Desert Ridge is about 30 mins away, but is a stunning hotel.

findings.title: Denise H. (3/5)
findings.snippet: BEWARE! They DON'T tell you upon check-in that they are going to hold a certain amount of $$$ from your bank acct!  I saw the charge online and thought someone had gotten a hold of my bank card!  Plus we couldn't sit out in our patio because the cushion on the chase lounge looked like someone had a bloody nose or something.  It would've been nice to sit out there.  It was gross!  Other than those (2) things... it was a lovely experience*

findings.title: Danielle J. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Stayed here for 4 nights this past weekend. Lovely place, great rooms. Spacious, and decent view. All great amenities within the room. Only downside was one day our room was never cleaned despite us being gone all day. No big deal but was surprised bc they had come in and out the other days so stealth! The balcony was lovely and not too hot despite the high temps.

The pools were great and perfect temps. I highly recommend the two restaurants on the pool level! Mowry and Cotton for breakfast and the pool side Mediterranean place for lunch (so good are thee twice!)

The staff couldn't have been nicer! I will also say, it was my first time seeing such high tech elevators and i was amazed at how quick they were and also how we never were in an elevator with others! Oh, and the valet was the fastest I've ever seen at any place I have ever stayed. Amazing! 

Hope to stay here again someday!

findings.title: Sasha N. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This is mainly for Afternoon Tea.

The Phoenician is my all time favorite afternoon tea spot in Arizona. We love Wanda (the senior tea matron) like family and seeing her again after all this time, exchanging hugs and hearing that they were shut down for a while during Covid broke my heart! She's truly what makes this place extra special and we're so grateful she and the rest of the tea staff were able to endure, return and keep the tea service at the Phoenician running at its very best. They truly go out of their way to make everyone feel special and their regulars absolutely adore them, myself included!

The tea selection is huge, the sandwiches are tasty, scones come with all the expected toppings and are so buttery and the sweets/deserts are divine! They also take into consideration any dietary needs (my husband is a vegetarian and has no issues with options for any course). I love to go on my birthday; there's always extra treats for the birthday celebrant. To get the full experience I highly recommend upgrading to the Royal or for an extra special treat the Grand Royal tea!

The atmosphere is nice and posh without any stuffiness or pretention. Seating is comfy, the views outside of the grounds are gorgeous and the piano music played during the experience really adds to the ambiance of the entire setting.

If you're ever in the Phoenix area and love afternoon tea you must stop in. Tell Wanda I sent you.

findings.title: Brendon P. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The Phoenician is an excellent resort located in an area close to both the hearts of Phoenix and Scottsdale. The poolside service was spectacular, then resort and hotel were comfortable enough. The gym is a little far from the main resort, but it is well equipped. 

The AC started leaking towards the end of my stay, which may explain why it was not as cool as it could have been, but the room was still comfortable enough to get a good nights rest. I would come back again.

findings.title: Rick G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I thought it apropos for my 500th Yelp review of an establishment visited very, very, very often for both day visits and staycations, special events, occaisions, and culminating in some incredible memories - our absolute fave combined resort, spa and restos in the Valley.  Having the opportunity to regularly stay over many accommodations across and occasionally outside the country, not a professional hotel reviewer by any means, and not a regular business traveler - but as a primarily pleasure and needs wanderer, I have developed as what I believe is my concise method for scoring the worthiness of each hotel visited.  A little exception for this establishment is necessary though, since my wife and I enjoy staycating here very often and find the amenities, eateries and then some, very satisfying and enjoyable. The Phoenician spa lives up to its hoopla from massages to aromatherapy. For swimming and lounging in the sun the Phoenician has its main pools, lazy river or the Spa Pools. For contemplating a valley view while imbibing some of the best The Valley can offer The Thirsty Camel Bar has its cool, modern and relaxing inside, or the outside patio with live music and firepits. Or you can select being more recluse in the Phoenician Tavern! If you want an upscale yet casual dinner there's Mowry & Cotton, which has been our only disenchantment to date at the Phoenician. They have gift shops with above average quality items, for adults and children alike. The poolside Kalio Kabobery Mediterranean offers an above average menu. Get your morning coffee and then some at the Marketplace Coffee House. If you your into Hi-Tea or Afternoon Tea you can't go wrong with our fave Valley Tea,  Afternoon Tea & Champagne offering in the English tradition, with tasty selections of Finger Sandwiches, Fresh Baked Scones, not to mention the pastries, along with some incredible tea selections. Love it! Combining the aforementioned with my criteria are as follows and the results are: 1) ease of access to and from public or private ground transportation [Score:4.5]; 2) convenient and safe parking [Score:5.0]; 3) access, accuracy and convenience of check in and check out [Score:5.0]; 4) atmosphere, ambience, public facilities, lounging areas and access to an office center and Wi-Fi access [Score:5.0]; 5) overall customer service - including but not limited to Hospitality, Support Services, Concierge knowledge, communication, attitude and demeanor of staff [Score:5.0]; 6) quality, cleanliness, value, convenience, amenities (i.e., ironing board, iron, TV, charging access, phone, et.al.) and comfort of rooms, beds, room safe and/or valet services [Score:5.0]; Taking all the aforementioned categories in a scale of 1 star to 5 stars with 1 being the worst and 5 being the best a hotel can be!  This hotel rates a: 4.9. If you have an opportunity to experience the Grifin Club you will most definitely appreciate the upcharge, and being a Member of Marriott's Bonvoy goes a long, long way! Great work staff and management, kudos and congrats for work well done. We'll just keep coming back!

findings.title: Natalie W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We spent a weekend here for an Anniversary trip. The views are amazing and the pools are the perfect temperature! The staff is so friendly and helpful.  The spa is wonderful and relaxing and the restaurants are fantastic. The menus are well thought out and creative. Fantastic flavors! We'll be back again.

findings.title: Julie A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: It is a beautiful property and the staff and incredibly kind and helpful-worth the money. I will definitely stay here again

findings.title: Todd I. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Place is great, but every store, every restaurant, and all but one bar closes at 4-5. Pretty ridiculous when flying here for a vacation without a car

findings.title: Jennifer G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Absolutely loved staying at The Phoenician last weekend for a girls getaway! Very impressed with the grounds and comfort of the room. Food at Mowry & Cotton was delicious, as were the food and drinks at the pool bar. Special shoutout to Ireland at the front desk who checked us in - she was so sweet and helpful! She made us feel instantly welcome and we really enjoyed her positivity and kindness. Thank you Ireland and The Phoenician for a wonderful stay. Can't wait to come back!

findings.title: Letty G. (3/5)
findings.snippet: I've had the privilege of staying at many wonderful hotels. Looking forward to the Phoenician, I didn't know what to expect. So far it's been disappointing. Even the presentation of the towels in the bathroom was not what i would expect, especially from a luxury resort.

findings.title: Philip J. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Our stay was great until I woke up to use the bathroom in the middle of the night and there was a 3 inch cockroach running around the toilet. I was horrified at the sight and killed it with a towel. I was literally sweating and my heart was racing as I was trying to kill it because it kept racing off. I called the front desk who sent someone up to dispose of the dead insect. I could not sleep the rest of the night not knowing if there were more, how it got in, if another would crawl in bed with me, etc. The next morning there was no follow up from management, as if nothing happened. I called to the front desk and they seemed indifferent and told me that the resort butts up to the mountain and this is not uncommon, and they can't contract with pest control because guests might have a reaction to the chemical spray? I insisted to speak to a manager and spoke to Natalie who was very sweet and reversed the $45 or so resort fee as compensation, and sent engineering up to the room to assess the bathroom. I got tired of waiting for engineering, as my whole morning was spent dealing with this, so I used the public bathroom on property and don't know what, if anything, engineering found as no one followed up with me after. Besides this issue the stay was great, and we loved the property and restaurants, but I don't think these people put themselves in my shoes and thought what this was like for a family with small kids to discover such a large roach during their trip. They didn't offer a different room or anything besides the waived resort fee. This was not a small bug as you can see from the picture and they really need to contract with some pest control service.

findings.title: Faith D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Treat yourself.

The atmosphere has a modern, classic, traditional, luxurious feel. Very clean, polished, and manicured.

You'll get your steps in for sure! It's a huge resort and spread out - even if it is packed, you'll find spaces to allow yourself some privacy, distance, and peace. The elevators cater specifically to you - so you don't have to worry about making multiple stops or sharing the elevator with others. 

I recently stayed here with my young daughter and got to experience The Phoenician from a young family perspective. I loved it! They offered daily crafts (one paid, one complimentary) and a decorating time (pretzel or cookie). My daughter loved it! And it made for a nice structure for the day - getting a break from pool time. If you have toddlers, this is ideal. There is a large and very toddler friendly splash pad next to the main pool. If you have young kids, also ideal! There is a slide and a tree house that your children will love! Lots of green space to play tag and run around. We didn't make it to the fitness center and so we didn't check out the game room. I imagine it is ideal for older kids. There is so much to explore! During the winter months I imagine you'd spend all of your time outside - riding bikes, walking the garden. 

We ordered room service for breakfast and it was top notch. My daughter was thrilled, "We don't even have to leave our room!" The pancakes were fluffy, plentiful condiments, bacon was crispy, and my huevos rancheros were savory and seasoned well. We didn't wait long and the delivery staff was very courteous and polite. 

The restaurant (Mowry and Cotton) was great! Perfect misters to stay on the patio (minus the birds - but a guy with a hawk walks through occasionally to scare them away). The Marketplace was well stocked and quick to get a scoop of ice cream or a latte. The poolside service was convenient - compared to other resorts' poolside drinks, theirs seemed a bit weaker. 

It is also very convenient to order from Door Dash. I met the delivery person outside the lobby - so many great nearby restaurants to choose from. 

The spa is lovely. The moment you walk in the entry, you feel relaxed. I didn't get a treatment, but imagine this being a perfect escape to getaway from any life stressors. 

The customer service was excellent. Each employee seemed attentive, upbeat, kind, and relaxed. Hands down why you want to book your next overnight here.

findings.title: Felicia G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is a great place to stay. The rooms are beautiful, and there are plenty amenities and things to do without having to leave the resort! The guest service is absolutely top tier, especially from Vanessa at the front desk, Cameron by the pool, and Dwi at the marketplace. I plan to be back!

findings.title: Cemil A. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
This isn't 5 stars.  Not even close.  Just charging more doesn't make a facility 5 stars.  Live and learn.  The up-charging here is really absurd.  Won't be back.  You can read all the other reviews that would already say the same but in more detail.  'View' was of a rooftop with probably 100 cigarette butts within 10 ft. Overall this property has good potential, feels mismanaged.

To the room service delivery folks and valet guys, you are the best part.  Down to earth, polite and seemingly hard working.  Thank you for that! 

Can't wait to get back to Mexico.

findings.title: Andre G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We are dedicated Marriott customer's, so when we had the opportunity to visit this beauty, we took it. The spa was fabulous. And with awe inspiring pool views, it does not disappoint.

findings.title: C M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I had an enjoyable visit to this beautiful resort during Christmas 2015. I had a second floor casita with a lovely view of a garden area. I enjoyed eating at the restaurant on the second floor above the golf club. The wait staff remembered how I enjoyed dining near the fireplace. I  also utilized the spa and had a delightful hot stone massage. 

My room was simply gorgeous. My king size bed was comfortable and cookies were placed in the room on Christmas Eve. Most nights my curtains were drawn. The bathroom was huge and amazing! The shower was enormous and my bathroom had a water closet with a bidet, large tub, plantation shutters, and an awesome vanity. 
 
The Phoenician is just a few miles from downtown Scottsdale. It took me about 20 minutes to drive to the airport. The staff members were professional and personable. 

I can't wait to return since it's been awhile. Hopefully by next year I will plan a relaxing getaway with a few close friends.

findings.title: Roslyn W. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
My experience at the Phoenician Resort:

I have been coming to the Phoenician for several years. I have never had an experience like I did tonight. I pulled up to the hotel and there was a man there to valet the cars. The Phoenician always has someone to valet your car. The man that was valeting for the evening just stood outside the booth and looked at me. I waited patiently because I assumed that he was waiting for another valet person to come. After five minutes passed, he walked toward the passenger side, I was preparing to roll down the window and before getting to the car, he turned around and went in the back of the valet station. He stayed in the back of the valet station until another car pulled up. He immediately came out and proceeded to help the lady get out of her vehicle. I got out of my car once I realized that I was actually overlooked, disregarded and not acknowledged. I asked him why he didn't come to my car and he lied and said I wouldn't open the car for him. I spoke to the manager and he told me that he will take my keys to the same man that refused to take my keys initially. He apologized and appeared to be unsure how to handle the situation. He asked me if I wanted a drink. I told him that what I want is for the tape to be viewed and for him to reprimand the valet guy. I don't want this to happen to anyone else. I am a women of color and I am hoping that this was not done for that reason.

findings.title: Addy G. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I was looking for something low-key, relaxing, and fun for my family and I to do for my birthday. We live in Queen Creek so we were looking for a good spot for a staycation. I never liked the idea of staycation, why spend your money where you live? It's not really a wise investment considering you're not having a new adventure? However, the way things have been going for me recently, that's all I wanted. I wanted to pack up the family, but not have to worry about the anxiety of going to an airport, flight delays, "flightmares," etc. We decided upon the Phoenician as I am a Marriott ambassador and it is part of the luxury collection of Marriott. I used my points for a two night stay with my husband and one year old. They upgraded us to a beautiful room on the ground floor called the Casita. It had a beautiful garden and fire pit outside but the room itself was very small. Typically we have much larger rooms. As an ambassador I get a certain amount of suite nights where I can put in a request to get upgraded to a suite. Anytime I've ever used that it's always been accepted, but this time around it wasn't. Too bad because I've had a horrible year and I really wanted that for my stay here. It's also difficult with my one-year-old because he sleeps much better with his own space and when we have a suite he will have his own room. What was cool is that we didn't have to park in any parking lot. We had our own parks parking spot right there outside of our room. It also only cost about $14 a night which isn't bad for a resort. You do have to pay resort fees which I believe are $49 a night and include the regular resort fee type things like activities, etc.. The concierge was absolutely lovely. They have a whole team of people and we checked in with them often to make reservations, ask questions, etc.
We ate at Cotton & Mowry the first night we were there and that was delicious. I will do a separate review on the restaurants.. The second night we dined at J&G Steakhouse. That's not open on Mondays and Tuesdays. It was very fancy and very fun to celebrate my birthday dinner there. I made myself a massage appointment for the first day we got there. I was so happy I did that. It was one of the best spa experiences I've ever had and I already cannot wait to go back. The massage itself was amazing, my massage therapist is named Zach. He was great. What I really loved about this experience was the amenities.. They had a steam room, a sauna, a large hot tub. A gigantic and beautiful quiet room, a locker room, showers, everything you would want and more. They serve tea, snacks, different flavored waters, it was so relaxing and so fun. They also have a rooftop pool. You can chill there, order off the menu, they have a bar and they also have fun nonalcoholic drinks. You can also rent a cabana while you're there. You do not need to be a hotel guest in order to use the spa. Although, you do need to book a service in order to use the amenities, meaning they don't let you pay just to use the amenities. They also have a great gift shop on your way out if you're looking to spend some extra money as everything is very expensive. On the day of my birthday we rented a cabana for $325. We were at a very quiet pool and there were only a few people who rented a cabana and they all had families as well so it was very kid friendly. It was great to have a private spot to keep us out of the sun, however it was still very hot there. They don't have any kind of cooling system or misters in there. Just the shade. They have a TV, they give you a choice of a complimentary champagne or a food item as well as a fully stocked refrigerator with water, Gatorade, etc. You get your own personal server who comes in and wait on you. I thought the price of the cabana was pretty high in comparison to what we actually got, but it definitely made the day more fun and more private. There are three pools there on site. There's a big splash pad for the kids, there is a pool restaurant, and of course the opportunity to rent cabanas. The food was really good at the pool. We ordered fish tacos, and as our complimentary item we got chips and salsa with guacamole, we also ordered the hummus tray. The drinks were just OK. Honestly, my son's banana smoothie was probably the most delicious thing. I ordered a beer and a vodka drink and my husband ordered a beer and a margarita but the liquor drinks were very weak. The same person who waits on you also makes the drinks. It was a nice day.. Normally at Marriotts  when they know you are celebrating a birthday, they send something, a letter, card, food tray, or wine to the room, they really didn't do anything like that. I thought in terms of hospitality, that was lacking. Otherwise, I definitely recommend staying here. It's a beautiful resort. They also have an athletic club and a golf course that I did not take advantage of but that looked beautiful.

findings.title: Sally P. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
WOW. What  a horrible experience trying to book dinner for 13 people and no one calling me back after I spoke to someone today who cared less about my son getting married.  We took our dinner business to another place "Steak 44" which is a better dinning experience and certainly a better experience overall. 

I thought, at least they won't hate me for trying to book a party of 13-15 two weeks out with an added suite and spa day! 

We had still hoped to book my son and his new wife in a suite & spa day however, that didn't work out either.  After being transferred three times I was connected to a person who spoke over me and basically didn't really care about anything I was saying.

 I was transferred yet again to another boy who was pretentious, disrespectful,NASTY and incompetent . I HOPE he reads this  review and while he might laugh .... he doesn't own this business and he might as well stealing cash from this establishment with his pretentious demeanor.

We have worked really hard traveling for business to achieve Marriott "Titanium" status to be treated like garbage is pretty sad and clearly what  led me to write this review. I will NEVER take my business here and would
 recommend you don't either. I have also contacted Westin/ Marriott to report such unprofessionalism.  Absolutely gross experience  and thankful it didn't work out. 

Hopefully they will respond as they have my contact number. Maybe they would like to apologize? NAH... I'm feeling confident they will decline from that and just post a swift and nasty response and I'm okay with that:)

findings.title: Jake G. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Our stay at the Phoenician was underwhelming to say the least. It was a nice hotel, and the restaurants were excellent even for the price. They unfortunately did not have a couple amenities available when we went. However the reason for my review is a pet peeve of mine, Cockroaches. I definitely wouldn't have expected a resort like the Phoenician to have cockroaches in the room. My spouse is very afraid of bugs to say the least, and that cut our stay a little abruptly as this was the early morning before checkout. Will probably be trying other places in town to staycation..

findings.title: John K. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Parking is a little bit of a mess after checking in somehow your card is supposed to open the gate.
It didn't then said to press button for ticket.

Check in was polite and decent.
The layout of the property is poor.  Park go up two escalarers try to find hidden life. One goes to one set of rooms and so on.

If you are used to huge property would not be an issue.  Is slightly more complex than the palazzo towers in Las Vegas.

Room is typical Fairfield style with small desk a bed but very nice bathroom.

Bathroom has tub and separate shower.

Is ok would expect it to be in the high one to low two hundred night range compred to similar experience.

Is not a bad property but do not less probably price tag fool expectations.

findings.title: Vanessa B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My husband and I were in town for a vacation thanks to his company, Emerson. We spent 5 nights in this beautiful resort and this place is first class all the way. The amenities are everything you would expect for a five star resort. The restaurants are fantastic, there are three pool levels, a spa, gym, game room, cacti garden, etc. The staff here were wonderful and service was top notch! All in all the best resort I've ever been to!

findings.title: Jessica S. (4/5)
findings.snippet: We had another pleasant stay here with friends who came to town. There is something for everyone here. We are not super fancy, but we have a lot of history here. Service here is over the top more so than ever. They go above and beyond to accommodate their guests. So much better than pre-renovation though we do miss the pre-renovation room pricing. They have put so much into the property and for our friends into golf the course is well manicured. Pricing on food at a resort I really never have a qualm about as we are always guests enjoying the amenities, the beautiful grounds, especially the heated pools. All these perks come at a cost. I feel I am just helping as a consumer. That is just how we feel. Exceptional service and kindness from everyone is worth it to us. A good staff and let me tell you there are a lot of people who have been happy employees here for many many years along with keeping enough staff and the cost of running comes at a price.  enjoying the amenities, the beautiful grounds, especially the heated pools. All these perks come at a cost. I feel I am just helping as a consumer. That is just how we feel. Spring is in the air. Make reservations as far ahead as possible for dining as they book fast. Right now 3 weeks out. Keep in touch with the resort by phone for any scheduled up and coming holiday events. If we didn't have so many food allergies I totally would LOVE to take the girls to their Afternoon Tea. Kids are welcome! Tea, finger sandwiches, and beautiful desserts!

findings.title: Reyn R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Lovely place. The employees are very kind and helpful, the grounds are very clean and the service is wonderful.

findings.title: Amanda K. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Came for spring training and ended up getting 3 rooms for 3 nights amongst our group. Check in was easy and quick, Valet was awesome, every attendant was professional, quick and kind. We went to the bar and that was another great experience. 

Our rooms were spacious. They were nice and clean and comfortable. Loved the balcony, we spent a lot of time enjoying the seating area out there.  Went to the pools to take the kids, nice and clean out there as well and the wait staff was very attentive.

Overall great experience, will definitely be back for our next visit to AZ.

findings.title: Thomas S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I have been here many times and have defended it to my wife who has always been like warm on this destination. The most unfortunate thing is that I'm here for another 5 nights. 

Service is something I expect when I come to a place like this and it is so sorely lacking. From the valet, to the check in experience, to the overall lack of helpfulness- things are going down hill. Now I really don't think I'm an unreasonable but I do have high expectations but it took three phone calls and three different people putting me on indefinite hold to simply get some wine glasses and a wine opener. A pretty simple request In my humble opinion.  What an ordeal. I was on hold two separate occasions and no one ever reconnected with me....And I waited!

Now I know good help is hard to find and with this "quit culture" I'm sure it is even worse for a place like the Phoenician but it was frustrating indeed. I even asked to speak with a manager and was again placed on hold.....indefinitely. 

So end of story the glasses finally came. After much stress and angst. Just not what you want when you are paying $600-$1000 per night. 

I know they can do better but this was not one of their best. This is not the Ritz Carlton experience I would expect.

findings.title: Marie K. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I had an awesome 3-day weekend here as part of a corporate event. The service was excellent at the steakhouse, shops, and pool. The waterslide was a huge hit for all! 
The grounds are gorgeous and meticulously maintained. The premises is filled with desert-friendly flowers and cacti. 
I would highly recommend this hotel for anyone visiting Phoenix/Scottsdale.

findings.title: Ps S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: DISGUSTINGLY DIRTY! I just returned from 5 days at the Phoenician with group event of 10 rooms and Presidential Suite. The suite was filthy. We called three times for the floor to be cleaned with no success. Crawling babies had black hands, feet and knees. Then an older child went through the drapes to get to the patio and her face came out black with what appeared to be soot. I emailed the manager (with photo proof) and asked for someone to contact me about cleaning and never heard from them. DO NOT go to this property!!

findings.title: Sarah M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We enjoyed our stay here recently. The hotel grounds are expansive and include multiple pools, a large standalone fitness facility, a cactus garden to walk through, and a nice spa. 

We had a nice room and could see cute bunnies outside most evenings (looking out from the ground floor porch.) Despite virus precautions, it was a relaxing and very enjoyable stay overall. 

The spa was very nicely appointed, and I really enjoyed my massage. Breakfast at the restaurant was very tasty. 

The only part that fell a little flat was service in the lobby bar. It was hard to get anyone to come by and take your order on a couple of different occasions.

findings.title: Christine T. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My stay here was a birthday celebration treat for me.  While I expected to get lost at a massive property, it felt quaint and nostalgic. They have redone it in a way that it feels like old Scottsdale, but completely luxurious.  The food was fantastic. The service was impeccable. It was a true pleasure to turn a milestone at your beautiful property.  See you again!

findings.title: Teresa L. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I intended to book $1200 in services at the spa, however, she was to impatient to wait and discuss the options.  I am going elsewhere!!!!!!

findings.title: V M. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Great property- on-site dining service is not "luxury" hotel level.  Some kids got welcome stuffed animal gifts while others did not.  Mischarges on my folio upon check out and dealing with it a few days later...

findings.title: B C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
With ~400 Bonvoy nights and stays at over a half dozen properties in the luxury collection portfolio, this by far the worst property and experience. I would avoid and suggest elsewhere should you stay in Scottsdale (you can get much better for far less). Specifically,
- Am lifetime gold elite
- Checked in on the app as early as available - apprx 24 hrs before arrival 
- Had booked and reconfirmed King room
- Requested early check in

When I arrived not only was there no early check-in (which understand it's only if available) but then they also put us in a room with two queens, see attached photo for our "view". This hotel's avg. rate is somewhere around $800 I believe. There was tremendous turnover the day we checked in so I am certain they could've found us a king sized room or even a better view (not to mention try for an upgrade, again, part of gold status, but of course also only if available). They didn't even try. Hospitality is dead 

Went to the restaurant while waiting for the room to be ready. Couldn't even get any server to grab a second beer. I get that everyone is short staffed and trying, but again, you're paying for "luxury" and this ain't it.

findings.title: C N. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Spent a few days enjoying Arizona at the Phoenician Suites. This place is all about customer service. Beautiful setting. Wonderful breakfast buffet. Quiet suites with very comfortable beds. Big thank you to everyone who made our stay a relaxing getaway.

findings.title: Tommy R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This place is LEGIT. If you are staying in Scottsdale I highly recommend. It is such a beautiful hotel and the whole property is amazing. Pools are great for kids. The gym is really nice. The game room is great for kids. The restaurants are great we will definitely be staying here when we come back next time.

findings.title: Nunya B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Wow.  I grew up coming here and my recent visit was horrifying.  No hot water in my first room, hot water BARELY worked at the second room and in the second room the sealing agents used on the door were so poor the wind howled like an awful ghost sound effect.  The bar was serving drinks and yet there was no food available on the entire property.  Yes, I'm talking no snack food, no restaurants open and the best recommendation was Uber eats.  As if 10 PM were too late to keep a snack shack open.  The mawyry cotton has gone horrifyingly down in quality since my last visit.  Over salted, under portioned, and overall awful.  Meanwhile the only solution we have gotten for all of this is being moved to the arguably worse room with no apology.  Severely disappointed and may not return.

findings.title: David C. (2/5)
findings.snippet: 4 pm means 4 pm . Got here at 11:30 requesting an early check in for our 30th anniversary. Went to the work out facility that is very nice and had lunch but 3.5 hours later still no room only to find out that they have a similar room ready but since nobody has stayed in it for 2 days somebody from housekeeping needs to go by and make sure it's ready to go . Could t this have been done hours ago? Beautiful place and they are probably short staffed like most other businesses because there is not much incentive to work nowadays but communication is key to help things along . Thanks

findings.title: Liam B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I'm attending a healthcare conference at this 5 star resort. I went to check in and was placed in a room with King bed and Mountain View. I walk in and there are towels all over the floor, bed not made, I realize it hasn't been cleaned yet.  Not good Covid protocol, but hey mistakes happen, no big deal. I call down and let them know, so they send a guy up and move me to a room with two queen beds and a view of the roof equipment. I was thinking, hmmm, for my trouble I get a downgrade?  Call front desk and just get the run around, no logical or creative solutions. I asked if I could just wait for the room they gave me 1st to be cleaned and they said no, I'd have to check out and then get back in line and get 1st available. I'm sure they are short staffed so I just said I was disappointed in how they handled the mistake, not that one was made, just how they handled it. What makes a 5 star resort 5 star is how you take care of people after a mistake. I rarely if ever leave a bad Yelp review, but this warrants a 1 star review.  Have to live up to 5 star if you use it in all your marketing.  Disappointed.

findings.title: Mrs V. (1/5)
findings.snippet: A "luxury" resort where my door lock wasn't working so someone drunk walked into my room in a middle of the night and vomited all over my bathroom. A security team confirmed the locks weren't working properly. They gave me some points and offered a cabana. I couldn't utilize it, so I asked them to get me in to the spa for a facial (much cheaper than a cabana), but now they are saying they won't cover it. I'm traumatized over what happened, I couldn't eat the following day I was so nauseous. Last night I woke up like 10 times checking in panic if my door is locked and they won't pay for a stupid facial? So if you want a hotel that is negligent with their guests safety and then couldn't care less how you were traumatized by their negligence, that's a place for you

findings.title: John T. (2/5)
findings.snippet: This is not a 5 star resort. Can't get any "hot" food at restaurants between 2-4p unless room service. The highly rated thirsty camel bar waited 30 min to get shrimp that wasn't fresh. Staff is nice but room, while large had a shower that a $125 a night hotel would have. Our suite was over $1000 a night. Nothing like a Four seasons or Ritz, actually after being here 3 hrs I'm looking to check out and find another hotel. I'm not a diva with high expectations or concerned about price but just expected more.

findings.title: Elma B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We've done a few staycations here and every time it has been great. The resort and rooms are high end and very clean. Great restaurant options on site and one of the top spas in AZ. We will try to come back every year.

findings.title: Alex O. (5/5)
findings.snippet: A fantastic place to stay in Scottsdale! Very beautiful when we rolled up to the front very late at night after our late flight. We were quickly checked in and had our questions answered. Our room was comfortable and spacious. We fell asleep quickly. Being that I arrived late at night, I could not see the landscape outside my window/balcony. I woke up to such a gorgeous, sunny view of Camelback Mountain. Absolutely breathtaking! We grabbed breakfast at Mowry & Cotton. The staff was so polite and kind! The food was great. My biggest overall takeaway is how nice, polite, personable, and engaging the staff at The Phoenician are. I just really enjoyed them all so much. They made our stay so much better just by being so sweet. I loved the property and amenities so much. There really isn't a reason to leave the resort, but of course we did to explore the town. I loved our stay and would happily stay again.

findings.title: Chelsea S. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Some things at this resort let me down and made me feel like this wasn't a five star hotel, this included things like small difficulties in my room, some poorly made food, etc. But let me tell you what made this resort stand out. The service. The pool servers were incredible (Berkeley and Cecilia), super attentive and quick. The pool helper, the person who puts your towels down and brings you ice for you water stood out by far. I had a few experiences with different people but Nathan went above and beyond. He always adjusted my umbrella, my water pitcher never went warm, and he was always offering new ideas on how to enjoy my trip - like putting a towel on the edge of the pool to read a book! No other person on the property made sure my experience was this amazing.

findings.title: Jesse R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This place is absolutely incredible . We Just got back from spending 4 nights here and I don't think I would stay anywhere else in the Scottsdale area. The grounds are immaculate and the views are unreal. The staff was great . I want to specifically mention Genaro from the pool staff . He was absolutely incredible. He made our stay amazing. Thank you Genaro!! You will not get better service anywhere. The resort has a bunch of food options as well as the lobby bar which has great drinks and great bartenders there. Another mention is the gym. It's a very big gym and it's super clean. Has everything you need for a great workout. I want to also mention the gym attendant. I can't remember his name, but he was extremely friendly. We went to the gym each morning and could not be happier with the experience. Overall a great resort !!

findings.title: Pauline G. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Don't waste your money. It's literally worse than motel 6 . First of all the pictures don't resemble actual rooms.  
On my first day there a shard of glass on the chaise pierced my vein.  
2nd night the roof started leaking 
Final night cockroaches were coming in under the front door . 

When I brought this to their attention I was met with such an attitude. 
They automatically charge 22 percent for tip . No exceptions and they ask for further tip . 

You must pay 15 dollars a day for WiFi and there's a 45 dollar a day resort fee ( in case you want to do yoga and other ridiculous things ) 

They double charge your card and you must wait 5-7 business days for it to come off ( still waiting ) 

It was the worst experience I've ever had in a hotel . Go to the Omni or camelback inn. Don't get suckered in by other reviews. This place is awful . 

I asked them twice to come and look at the leak.  Both times ignored. I saved up for this trip and literally wasted almost 2,500 dollars

findings.title: Paige J. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
A group of us from the East Coast who desperately needed a break from COVID, the daily grind, our bushiness, and regular life, decided to go to Scottsdale for a week-long vacation.  Our group of couples celebrating 25 plus years of marriage each, comprised of a VA school principal, a FedEx Director, a DHS Executive, a NY Business owner and other professionals hit the JACKPOT with this resort.

Everyone in our group felt as if we were far-far away from the United States. The resort is beautiful, simply beautiful, well-kept, peaceful, and comforting. 

The rooms are huge.  You have your choice of views - facing the mountain, the pools, or the fancy entrance with a fountain.  

There are trails, tennis, bike riding, a golfing range, a full golf course, yoga, valet parking, underground self parking,  the Market Cafe that serves their signature non-alcoholic drink "The Phoenician" (black tea/lemonade with Prickly Pear juice), which became a morning staple.

The Spa... prepare to spend your entire day there, you won't want to leave.  Steam Room, Sauna, Whirlpool, the Quite Room, the Rooftop Pool and the amazing massage that will leave you sleeping on the massage table long after your service is over.

Lastly, the customer service was impeccable.  We're all very well traveled individuals and the Phoenician is the Nordstrom of hotels/resorts and more than deserves it's 5 star rating.  Shout out to @Rachel-Front Desk @Hannah-Front Desk @Doug-Valet @Ed-Security @Moira @Mr. Vinciguerra

findings.title: Jamie H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This place is 5 star. The restaurants, the pools, the customer service. We used the athletic center. Truly it's a luxury resort for a reason. We will be back.

findings.title: Jenny C. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Disappointed in my stay this weekend. Every single pool was HOT- something was broken or their water isn't aerated because it was stagnant and pretty awful. You could not cool down. Several other couples poolside were cancelling and going elsewhere. One couple said last year it wasn't like this, but the resort refused to acknowledge anything was wrong. Sad to say I can't trust this wouldn't happen again/ so I can't refer the resort to my friends knowing their entire weekend could be ruined by every pool being too warm to swim in. I really wish they would have at least acknowledged their was a problem. We paid good money and it felt wasted.

findings.title: Glenn M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Never written a Yelp review before, mostly because I have never felt strongly enough one way or the other to go through the trouble. However, my fiancé and I had such a positive experience on our recent say at the Phoenician, I felt compelled to share with the class. Similar to other five diamond resorts, there is not a lot to complain about - sure you could nit-pick a few things here or there, but they more than make up for it with other luxury service and amenities. Namely, and the reason for me writing this review, the service we received at the pool by a saint named Gennaro. 

If our stay at The Phoenician was a beautiful bonfire, Gennaro was gasoline. He took our trip to a whole other level. On our first day we had a cabana to celebrate a friends birthday and Gennaro showed up to take care of us. Before we even had our first round of drinks he had used his friendly and genuine personality to form personal connections with all of us. We thought, "maybe this was like, the red carpet package that comes with the cabana", or "maybe we were his only customers", but boy were we wrong. After meeting Gennaro, he looked out for us the next 4 days of our stay like we were family, and truly made us feel special. I'm not going to give away all his secrets online, but it was hard to leave. 

If you are ever looking for a fail-safe way have a good time and feel like you are living your best life, call The Phoenician and tell them you want to book your stay when Gennaro is working. You won't regret it.

findings.title: Cyndi B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
For years I have heard of this property from friends and clients that have been going for years. The property is large and spread out, but access is very easy with golf carts that arrive when you request them.
The spa is world renowned and "huge." The vibe is special and intended for a full day experience. The Canyon Suites with a spa focus vacation would not disappoint anyone wanting a special disconnect of pampering.
Many restaurants to choose from, we tried The Tavern and Mowry & Cotton. There was retail sprinkled in as well, R&R is a fun store.
The multiple pools were a highlight. High touch of ice water by the pool staff was very appreciated.
Joanna Paulsel was a joy and her long history with the property put an impressive cap on the reputation and experience on my visit. There are many long time employees which says a lot for the owners and management.

findings.title: Tianna T. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Went fir a girls weekend and Stayed for 3 nights.,  rooms are spacious and hotel is very clean. Staff was very friendly and always available even at the poolside. Went to the spa for a massage which was great as well. The gym was really nice with brand new machines. The only downside was the pool was a little warm. Couldn't really cool off that much from the heat but you still couldn't get me out of it! Definitely would stay again.

findings.title: Ralph A. (3/5)
findings.snippet: We had a good time just visiting the bar on top overlooking the pool. The views weren't what I thought but not bad. We got a couple drinks and appetizers and they were not cheap. Wish we could have stayed at the resort but they were booked up.

findings.title: Wynn Y. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
"The Luxury Collection" .....Yeah, If your standards are set low low low low".  More akin to an average apartment complex.  Every time we'd walk back to the room, my husband and I commented how  we felt like we were reliving our newlywed days of living in a cheap apartment complex on the wrong side of the tracks just trying to make ends meet.   Not exactly the vibe we were going for since we are here to celebrate our 30th anniversary, but it was fun reminiscing about how  far we've come in three decades.  

This resort is Nothing fabulous, grand or luxurious.  
The room could've been a Holiday Inn next to a busy freeway-sans the traffic. 
That's fine if we weren't paying $600 a night.  

Steak Restaurant atmosphere was ok. We went up for an appetizer and drinks. Decided not to stay for dinner. 
Tried the Maury and Cotton restaurant. 
What in tar - hill  is going on with those hideous, ill- fitting uniforms the poor waitstaff have to wear???   Slouchy shirts with weird unkept suspenders?  
It took over an hour to get a steak and hamburger, which was too raw to eat. Finally drove a few blocks down to Mastros for dinner. 
I am writing this review at 10am as we are driving over to the Westin Kierland for the second night of our anniversary celebration-staycation. I just can't justify spending two nights here.  
The first night was spent reliving our newlywed days, 
hopefully tonight we will be celebrating how far we've come....and for a third of the price..

findings.title: Austin R. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Probably my favorite hotels! I've stayed here several times in the winter and summer. Was recently here in June 2020. Pretty busy for summer but I think everyone wanted to get out and travel with COVID pretty much gone. The hotels location is amazing.

Amazing views from the rooms and of course the pools! The pools here are so nice, even if it is 115 out. Most importantly, I LOVE that they are open 24/7. Going for a swim at midnight when no one is around and the sun is not glaring down is perfect. Not many hotels I've been to have this unfortunately. The slide is really fun. Yes, I was the only adult on it that day haha. 

My only negative with my last stay was the house keeping. We stayed for almost a week and they never replaced towels or toiletries like shampoo. We had to call room service who was very quick at bringing it but shouldn't have to do that. 

Other than that, it's an amazing resort. The cactus garden is amazing to see with Camelback Mountain right behind. Looking forward to come back soon.

findings.title: Bill S. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Had dinner at Mowry and Cotton the other day and was underwhelmed for sure. Service was slow and seemed disinterested. Had salmon and a steak and the bill was north of $150. While I understand the prices are normally high at a resort of their reputation it was still on the high side for the quality of the food and overall service. Save your money and go to Scottsdale there are numerous other options which provide superior food and service. Won't be back.

findings.title: Evan A. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Came here at the end of February and had a nice stay. 

Hotel itself is large, personally things tend to get lots with large resorts, not a lot of personal service but everyone was very nice. Seemed short staffed, know that's been an issue for a lot of hospitality in general. 

The check in was easy, room upgrade if available when I booked with on AMEX website. The room was ok, loved the large bathroom but the room itself was meh. The decor was gray and felt a little cold. The upgrade was a top floor overlooking the cactus garden and the mountain side. Thought it wasn't that great of a view but it was quite which was nice. 

The pool was great, during the week a lot less people and Friday/ Saturday were a little hectic with every seat filling up quickly. 

Not sure if this is the best option in Scottsdale for myself. Not as 5 start as I thought it would be.

findings.title: Cecilia O. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We came here for afternoon tea  for our birthday celebration.  From the welcoming environment to the staff. The afternoon tea was amazing, the service provided was exceptional service. Sabrina and Natalie were amazing, top notch. The decadent desserts and finger foods so many flavors that accent eachother very well.

findings.title: Shirley T. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Very disappointing due to terrible service.  The property itself is lovely, but the service was definitely lacking.  We arrived early and dropped our bags with the valet and went to eat lunch.  Lunch at the golf course restaurant was "ok" - wouldn't choose to eat there again.  Wandered around waiting for the call that our room was ready - nothing.  At 4pm, we went to the front desk and were told, "Oh, yes - your room is ready."  (Seriously - no call?) 
 Ninety minutes and two phone calls to finally get our luggage delivered to the room.  No housekeeping service (we were not told that there wouldn't be any and they were obviously cleaning other rooms with people staying in them.)   Called guest services and asked for a towel refresh at a minimum.  Four hours later - called again.  An hour after that we finally got towels.  Asked where we could get ice and was snootily told, "This is a 5 star hotel.  WE bring you the ice."  Great - no ice showed up for 90 minutes so my husband went to the bar to get some.  It finally arrived an hour AFTER that.  
The pool area was crowded (we went in April) and the service at the pool slow.  
Bottom line:  You're paying 5 star prices and getting 1 star service.

findings.title: LV Guy Y. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Stayed at the property around May 1, 2021 for 4 nights and i am from CA, the property is very beautiful, but i would like to point out a few things about this property, so depending what u are looking for from a 5 star facility:
it is a local water hole for the well-to-dos of Scottsdale, i saw more Ferrari/Lamborghini than in Vegas, the Camel Longe was a place for the fashionable folks of the town to see and to be seen....... so it is not a serene and exclusive place.......the "beautiful" people are generally VERY dressed up for the occasion.
there was not enough fine dining "capacity" for hotel guests, their steakhouse, J&G was outstanding , but was full every night and i was not able to get a reservation.  Again, i think the reservations were taken mostly by the locals......i walked in half an hour before close to wait for a table, lottery...
the service, for the Camel Lounge, was below average, but it may be due the lack of staff caused by the Pandemic as well as how busy the bar is generally....
the pool was so packed, like a pool in a Vegas hotel.
the spa was beautiful, but my wife was not able to book a treatment, and we were there for 4 nights!!! again, like i said earlier, the property caters to the locals.....
the tennis courts: i am a tennis player, and the courts are BEAUTIFUL!  Almost worth the trip....

if u are looking for peace and quiet,  i suggest the RITZ C in Tucson, i am staying there now for 5 nights.......

findings.title: Sean M. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Overall, I would not recommend this resort. While the property does have some strong points, I found that the overall feel of the resort does not live up the standards of a "5 star" resort or the price they charge for a room. The property in general was fantastic, but I felt like the food, service, and amenities were severely lacking. See my full review here, I hit yelp's text limit. 

https://www.flyertalk.com/forum/33276932-post240.html

Room:
Luckily, I was able to book with points (at 70K a night) and used a SNA, which allowed me to upgrade to a 1,150 sq ft, 1 Bedroom Casita Suite with kitchenette on the second floor. When choosing between the Casita suites, I would highly recommend booking the 2nd floor as it provides you a spectacular view of the pool and surrounding fountains. P2 and I really enjoyed having meals on our balcony and this was one of the highlights of our stay. The ground floor does provide you with a larger patio and fire pit, but given the heat - I doubt you would find much use for the fire pit. I found that the quality of our rooms were fantastic, with the largest non-jacuzzi tub I have ever seen. We actually thought it may have been too big (if that was such a thing) as it was difficult to get in and out without slipping on the marble. 

Facilities:
Another strong point of this property, as their resort grounds and overall facilities were spectacular. A large portion of their hotel is outdoors with lush green grass, and carefully maintained shrubs and desert plants. The property is HUGE, and taking a stroll through it was enjoyable. We saw a variety of animals roaming the property, ranging from a family of ducks, "song" birds, and even hares! It was straight out of a Disney movie - you can tell the animals enjoyed the greenery compared to the vast Arizonian desert. There are picnic tables and benches sprawled throughout the interconnecting walkways, providing more locations to sit and relax.

Dining: 
Definitely property's weakest point, by far. The breakfast options at the Mowry and Cotton were pitiful. Between the two mornings, we tried the breakfast BLT with tater tots (6/10), Chorizo breakfast burrito (3/10), and lemon french toast  (2/10). Overall, all these items were $20 and very mediocre. If the price was cheaper, I still don't think I would order it again if I had the option to eat it back at home - that's how bad it was. The welcome breakfast amenity was $18.99 for you and a guest. Not as great as I've seen at the other Luxury Collection hotel I stayed at, but that's a pretty small sample size.

The breakfast BLT was the only thing was close to acceptable - however they chose to skimp out and provide tater tots instead of standard has browns or breakfast potatoes. You heard me right, a five star resort was serving tater tots as part of an adult entree for breakfast. This was certainly one of the things that left a strong negative impression. Even the best tater tots are still... just tater tots. In addition, their chicken and waffles (a favorite of mine) was not even fried chicken, but chicken tenders. Talk about watering down their brand name... The breakfast burrito was mushy and the flavor was homogenous with little Chorizo. It did not come with a side of tater tots so it was $20 for a small amount of food. The lemon french toast was whatever, and did not look like the stock photos they had online - and it was also missing the vanilla curd that was part of the description. I could've made better french toast at home... 

With the negative impression we had from the first breakfast, we did not feel like giving their dinner options a chance and chose to order take out to be enjoyed on our balcony.

The food options were grossly underwhelming. Glancing at the lunch and dinner items, nothing looked special or noteworthy, and was just standard American faire. I make it an effort to enjoy dinner on-resort at the nicer places I stay at, but here - there was absolutely no way considering the experience we had during our first breakfast. During our stay at the US Grant in San Diego, a Luxury Collection Hotel that I highly recommend, we had a fantastic breakfast that I would be eager to eat again when I'm back in the area. It is insane how the quality of food can vary so greatly with the Luxury Collection. If I was the chef and menu curator at the Phoenician, I would be embarrassed of myself. I would have rather eaten breakfast at Denny's. I don't think I can stress how disappointing the breakfast was.

findings.title: Lisa H. (5/5)
