findings.snippet: Beautiful resort to relax. The pool is a perfect temperature to soak all day, rooms are upscale, clean and large. The restaurants offer a great selection and beautiful views of the mountains and resort.

findings.title: A C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We stayed at the Canyon Suites at the Phoenician and loved it!  The room was spacious and offered a closed sleeping area to the rest of the suite.  Our balcony overlooked the pool and mountain and offered a great spot to watch the sunset.  The resort was not overcrowded during our stay making it easy to find pool chairs.  Sharon at the Canyon Suites pool was spectacular!  She was spot on with service and really made our trip extra special.  Jay at the front desk went above and beyond to confirm car, restaurant and spa reservations.  Highly recommend this location to "get-away".  Look forward to visiting again.

findings.title: Michael C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is a great spa had awesome there last month went to book again and now have to be a resort guest on weekends very disappointing

findings.title: Carole C. (1/5)
findings.snippet: We have been loyal to the Phonecian for years, but I had skipped a substantial amount of years and in the meantime Maria took over. This place should not be qualified as a luxury experience. It is a beautiful property with lots of restaurants, but it is totally overrun with yuppies and tons of children. We feel like we are staying at a Disney resort.  Additionally some of the things that are wrong is there was no soap, the refrigerator didn't work, they haven't taken the coffee out of the rooms. You can call for room service for these things but you stay on hold for five minutes at least because they evidently Cut down on their help. No more turn down service, no more laundry or dry cleaning, it takes at least 20 minutes to get a cocktail. The food in the restaurants is 4 to 5 times higher than anywhere else, but it is good. Basically if you can stay at a good quality hotel you'll be way better off sitting here. This place just specializes in taking your cash!  And it's not that it's inexpensive. Our room was over 1000 a night plus 40 for luxury and 40 for parking the car. Buyer beware

findings.title: Andrea N. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Incredibly disappointing. I'm currently still here --  because of a storm my flight tomorrow had to be moved to Monday -- but I'm checking out and going to another resort because the service here is mostly horrible. 

First, I booked a garden casita so I'm paying a premium price for what I thought would look like the website... a room with a terrace near grass. I didn't expect a fancy pool view, just some grass. It's called a garden casita! Instead I'm overlooking a road. I called and asked about a different room as soon as we checked in but didn't get a call back until the next evening. And, can't really get through to the front desk without being on hold for ten minutes or more. Tried the app which worked for a minute but still no follow up.

We've been here for two days now and no housekeeping. When we first checked in the towel in our room was stained. I had to call today to get someone to come switch out towels.

The weather sucks so I was really counting on service to save this trip. Nope. We ate at Mowry & Cotton twice and both times it seemed like they couldn't be bothered. One waitress hurried us through our lunch dropping the check off after one drink. I made a dinner reservation asking for a table with a heater and we were seated at the single table without a heater. So we asked to be moved inside and then barely got service. Once we got our meal no check back and had to wait to get our check. So bizarre.

We went on the cactus walk this morning. Nice garbage overflowing from can - see photo.

The two bright spots were service at Thirsty Camel and Heather's service at the pool. 

Not enough to save it though. I can't believe I spent thousands on this for our wedding anniversary. I've had better experiences at a $130/night Clarion. 

I guess they've given me a $150 credit. I've worked in hospitality and I'm not the kind of person that just complains to get free stuff. However $150 doesn't really offset the investment I made for our anniversary and this experience honestly sucked. Unless you are coming here for a conference and your company is footing the bill I can't imagine why anyone would come here. I could have gone to an all-inclusive in Mexico for this price. I will never come back here.

findings.title: Gerald J. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Visit to the Phoenician was relaxing.. 
Downside was It was much too crowded at the pool for me and spacing on seating at Mowry could've been much better. 
The pandemic is not over yet.

findings.title: Jenna K. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Note: I'm a current guest staying here & writing this 5 min into getting to my room & I would be giving 0 stars, but the property is gorgeous & half the employees were great/helpful.

I was SO excited to check in here, especially because we haven't traveled since COVID. We came to Arizona for a quick, weekend business trip. Driving in, first impressions were beautiful, huge property! Customer service upon checking in was awesome. We have been up since 4am traveling, so when our room was finally ready, we couldn't wait to get into it! Upon arrival to our room, I realized it was not what I booked. For some reason that was never explained, they changed my room without me knowing. I booked a Deluxe Casita w/ 1 King Bed & Garden View. I chose this specific room type because I brought my dog & it offered extra space unlike your typical hotel room. I also called not once, but twice to let them know I would be needing a pet friendly room & I was also told that I would be getting a ground floor unit. Now, I don't mind a different view or if I get stuck with an extra bed or even if the room wasn't ready yet. However, none of those things happened. Instead, I checked in, received my keys & got to my room which was not a Deluxe Casita, in fact it wasn't a casita at all. They downsized/changed me to a regular guest room. If I wouldn't have called to see what happened, I would have been charged for the Casita. Now I do want to mention AFTER I called to see if they would get me in the correct room I booked, they then offered a $75 off per night due to them not having a Casita available. So although I booked a Casita & called twice before, I still was not put in the correct unit. Very frustrating & honestly disappointing considering the price per night. If I wanted a hotel room I would have booked elsewhere, but we chose The Phoenician for the Casita's. Safe to say we won't be returning. So unfortunate considering how much we were looking forward to staying here.

findings.title: Sam M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Had a nice stay here. Beautiful hotel and garden. Very clean room and great customer service here.

findings.title: Melinda B. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Our stay in January was great; the room, spa, fitness center and pool were excellent as were the staff.
The trouble came after I got home and realized that I had left my iPad in the room.  It had been a week by the time that I called because I only use it for travel.  I spoke with several hotel staff members over a weeks timeframe and nobody really seemed all that concerned with helping me.  I finally called Apple to have the track my iPad; it was last located at the Phoenician but my Apple ID was inactivated on the machine.  
Not sure if it was a member of the staff or guest but instead of turning it in, they made my iPad theirs.  My fault, I left it but it would have been far less frustrating if anyone was willing to help me.
Won't return; cannot trust that my jewelry or other expensive items wouldn't be taken next time.

findings.title: Sunil T. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful resort, conveniently located near the mall, restaurants and trails in a Scottsdale.  It's a bit dated but still well kept.  The staff is courteous and helpful.  The coffee shop is convenient, and breakfast at Mowry and Cotton was wonderful (I had the hash with salsa verde and coffee).  The tennis courts are amazing, though you do need your own tennis balls or need to purchase them from the athletic center (rackets are free).  They also have a beautiful garden/small trail area.

findings.title: J. B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: One of the nicest resorts I've ever stayed at. There are multiple pools on multiple levels, including an adults-only pool (thank god), where the attendants all help you out with towels and water, as well as food and beverage orders from the kebab restaurant. The poolside food absolutely exceed my expectations. The grounds were gorgeously maintained and lovely to walk around. The rooms were quite spacious, well cleaned, and modern. The lobby bar and outdoor patio were both beautiful spaces to enjoy a tasty cocktail, and had amazing views.

findings.title: Mike W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Great place they upgraded us for being our anniversary and we will definitely back what a fantastic view we had over the whole weekend !

findings.title: Judith T. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I felt alarmed at the lack of strict and forcefully enforced PPE protocols. What makes it more shockingly is I experienced this fear at a five star hotel. 

Lobbies shoulder to shoulder, a check in process that is packed should have been conducted outside.   Bars packed no air circulation or open doors to the patio. Surly waiters huffing when I asked for water with no ice his mask slipping below his nose. 

A gym filled with people. A receptionist that does nothing. No wipe downs of equipment no air circulation no staff insuring people are wearing masks correctly I had to ask that the wipes in the garbage can be emptied as it was overflowing. 

I've attached our upgraded Motel six room with one sink, cheap looking furniture and my view of the golf course if I squinted I may have seen a sandtrap.  One tiny bar of soap also included in images. 

What was even more troubling was overhearing a guest who was black and his checkin experience. It was clearly outright racism his comparing his experience after the white couple before him were greeted cheerfully and provide an overview of the hotel. 

While the grounds are immaculate the interiors are grounds for dismissal.

findings.title: Danielle B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Completely dissatisfied with this resort. Our entire experience from the minute we got there to the minute we left was not good. We booked through aahotels.com which misled you greatly on what resort view meant. The room we got was overlooking a roof and they called that resort view. We had to pay more to get the Mountain View for the two days we were there. The restaurant experience was horrendous. They didn't tell you that you had to make reservations so we had to go off the resort for the first nights dinner meal. Then we made reservations for the second night and we still had to wait 30 to 45 minutes and for some reason because we complained of the wait when the restaurant was completely open and had many tables available they put us in a back room and closed the door like we were in time out. They gave us a drink menu that had nothing in it. Yes management came but that was not the point. Overall we were totally dissatisfied with the amount we had to pay to stay at this resort.

findings.title: Christina S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Mowry & Cotton excellent breakfast. I had an AWESOME server Rachael she was friendly extra attentive. She gets 2 Thumbs up.

findings.title: Jason H. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Great property that is in need of a reno as both the styling and the decorating is a bit 1990's.

Other than that, its a sprawling resort with an incredible tennis club, they have good service, large rooms and its competitively priced.

findings.title: Ahna E. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Highly recommend this hotel and if you wanted to be treated by the best see Chris at the bar, he is so friendly and loving and will always take care of you unlike the other bartenders

findings.title: teri s. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We had Austin serve us at the mowry and cotton 
He was awesome 
Professional and very attentive 
Thank you Austin

findings.title: Tyler Z. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We stayed at the Phoenician for 6 days, 5 nights during COVID. To say we were impressed is an understatement. The hotel takes their COVID protocol very seriously, and we really appreciated that. 

We stayed in a king bed, pool view room. Our view was so nice and we had a pretty good sized balcony. The room was clean and the bathroom was a great size for a hotel bathroom. 

What really stood out to us though throughout our entire trip was the service. If you needed something, the staff would make it happen. The pool service was absolutely phenomenal. The staff would literally wrap your chair in towels for you, give you extra towels, and constantly make sure you had ice water in a pitcher. We were so impressed. 

The only thing that was a bit confusing is that we were told the only restaurants on the property that were open was the tavern and Mowry and cotton. However, we saw the steakhouse open and people sitting outside eating. Maybe it changed while we were there but we would have loved to try it. 

I would recommend this hotel to anyone. Worth the price.

findings.title: Lisa W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed here for a couple of weeks! Super impressed with the customer service and amenities. Very clean, great for kids,  and super good food! Ate here a lot, but the hotel is also conveniently located near restaurants, shopping, museums and grocery stores. They also have exclusive Byredo shampoo and conditioner!! Definitely recommend.

findings.title: William H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Driving in with the original Phoenician entryway with the perfectly manicured landscaping with massive fountains and flowers, you realize that you have arrived to a world class resort. The valet is quickly to welcome you while dropping off the car. Step back and realize the sculpture perfectly placed between buildings bringing your eye back to the mountian side. Walking into a the lobby there are several places to check in, see the concierge and the lobby bar. The food in the different restaurants are wonderful. Mowry and Cotton has a outdoor patio that you can sit and see out to the whole property and pool area. I'd highly suggest the turkey cuban. 

If you're from Chicago, NYC, Europe, Asia or just a neighbor for lunch, you will instantly appreciate and enjoy your choice for coming.

findings.title: Drai V. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Old hotel - most of the rooms don't even face the mountain - pool feels like a 2 star Vegas property and the rooms are expensive. Should have booked the sanctuary instead... the restaurants aren't good either... look at elsewhere to relax and enjoy.

findings.title: Daniel M. (3/5)
findings.snippet: This luxury (read: overpriced) hotel gets a meh. I'll give the benefit of the doubt that COVID has impacted their business, but really, in October/November they should really have it figured out by now.  And while they state they adhere to strict guidelines during the pandemic (facemask requirements and temperature checks), that must be for the staff as countless guests (and this place is relatively empty) ignore mask requirement signs, there are no temperature checks, and high touch areas go ignored throughout the facility. Disregarding that, this place offers no amenities or luxury that would distinguish it from any other Marriott property and you'd be better served staying at a Courtyard and buying a day pass for spa treatments or tee-times at other venues.

findings.title: Sara H. (1/5)
findings.snippet: My husband and I stayed at The Phoenician for a "staycation" for 1 night about a week ago. It was our first chance since Covid to have some alone time without our girls for the evening. We live in town and like to stay at the nice resorts to support our local community. This was our first time here and can say we were very disappointed. We arrived and decided to stay in one of the casitas due to the proximity to the pool and the fact we could park our car out front. When we drove up to our room, there was no parking in either parts of the casita parking and several cars were "double-parked" so we had to search around for self parking which was a long distance to our room. We were lugging our luggage down the road by the golf course and past several buildings before we got to our room. If I had known parking was like this, we would have valet parked and stayed in the main hotel. We went to the pools where every seat was occupied so we decided to have lunch at the hotel first. We were told they were at 97% occupancy which was evident by the crowds. After lunch, we were able to locate lounge chairs. It took about 15 mins for someone to take our drink order and then another 40 minutes for our drink to arrive. It was less than desired customer experience for a high end resort where we paid over $600 for the night. Later that evening we returned to the hotel after being out and went to have a drink at the main lobby bar at 9:30. It was completely packed and a lively scene. We sat at the bar and ordered drinks. We asked what our options were to order food and we were told there were no options other than chips and dip at the bar. Given the hotel was so full and packed with people, I found that odd to have no food options at 9:30pm at a large resort with that sort of occupancy. So we ordered delivery and when I mentioned to my husband that I needed to grab the food from the lobby, the bartender eavesdropped on our conversation and said she would put our drinks in to go cups and gave us our check. We never said we were closing out and we had no intention of eating the food until later when we returned to our room. When we asked why she closed our bill, she said no outside food was allowed (yet, there were no options at the hotel). She completely made assumptions and listened in on our conversation instead of asking us what we would like to do. Our evening was basically cut short and we felt like we had no option but to go back to our room and end our evening out. Overall, it was poor service from beginning to end and really feel I was ripped off for the amount of money we paid to stay there.

findings.title: Cecilia M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We enjoyed our stay. Some insight, it's $33 a day for valet, you can come and go as many times as you please after you agree to the fee. $15 a day for WiFi, which allows you to cast from your device onto your hotel room TV. We used this feature for Netflix and Hulu. The cactus garden was my favorite. The spa was fully booked and you must call ahead in advance to schedule a massage. The concierge desk does a fabulous job at recommending restaurant & activities. The resort is very luxurious and beautiful! We will definitely be coming back! This place has 4 restaurants.

findings.title: Luis B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I proposed to my fiancée here and they went above and beyond to make the experience unique and memorable. The entire organization went above and beyond even during a current pandemic. They were wearing masks and have multiple safeguards in place. The customers do not respect it as much as it is communicated and highlighted throughout the resort but the resort is trying.

Best resort in Arizona!

findings.title: Gabi M. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We recently enjoyed a family staycation at the Phoenician resort.  It's less than a mile from our house, but we needed to "get away," as we've been spending so much time at home due to the Covid-19 pandemic. It was a very expensive 24+ hours, but it was memorable and fun for all.

We went with another family and booked casitas near one another.  It was busier than expected at the resort, but supposedly not at full capacity due to precautions.  We did notice that all staff were masked up and professional.  Pool service was great, as was the service at The Tavern restaurant, but Cotton and Mowry for breakfast Sunday morning was beyond slow... especially with a handful of hangry kids and adults!  

Even so, we had a great time and we would all go again in a heartbeat.  From the waterslide which never gets old and the splash pad for younger / little guests, to an adult-only pool, and some insane views of Camelback Mountain, there is something for everyone at the Phoenician.  I hope to stay longer next time to take advantage of more amenities or perhaps plan a spa day soon.

findings.title: Megan M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
What an amazing resort!!!!!! This place is not only beautiful but very clean and spacious. We were blown away by our stay, the staff was absolutely amazing also. They have taken all the steps at the resort to make sure guests feel safe and comfortable. Hand sanitizer bottles on every corner on the hotel, by elevators, by entry ways, etc. Masks are required as well. We were nervous to vacation due to covid19 and this resort went above and beyond to where we felt extremely comfortable. 

This resort has some amazing pools, 9 of them! The fitness center is the best we've ever seen on the resort. Tons of tennis courts, amazing golf course, etc. We will be back!

findings.title: Michael S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: What more can I say besides WOW! This place is know to be very high end and upscale, came here for my wife's birthday and boy did they deliver. The check in was top notch, rooms are spacious and had a great pool view. Amenities are top notch and service from everyone was outstanding. One knock was their limited number of restaurants open due to Covid but we were told they will be slowly re-opening. Great relaxing stay, can't wait to do it again.

findings.title: Vanessa M. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Nope nope nope. Never again. I'm sorry, COVID cannot be the excuse for a bad experience. I was super excited for this staycation, and unfortunately many things went wrong. We were promised a resort credit and when I asked about the credit I was told that I was misinformed, $150! Then upon booking I was told the game room was open and upon check in no game room was open. No housekeeping services unless it's requested. Upon booking I was told the spa closed at 6pm, I booked a massage at 4, giving me enough time to relax on the rooftop and when my massage was over we had to pack up and leave because spa closed at 5! The lack of communication was so unprofessional. Sorry never again.

findings.title: Audrey N. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I'll start by saying the hotel was beautiful & clean and most employees we interacted with were kind. So they get some points for that. 

However, I stayed there on August 29 for my wedding night. I called the front desk at 10am that morning and asked for the possibility of a 3pm check in (regular check in is 4pm) as the wedding started at 4:30pm and my husband wanted to check us in before arriving at the nearby venue. I would have understood if not but the front desk concierge on the phone was very kind and said not a problem and she was moving us to the priority check in list, she was recently engaged and was so excited for us! She said I'll put you on the 11am clean list so you'll be good to go this afternoon when he comes by. Fast forward to 3pm, my husband arrives to check in and get dressed before the big night and the front desk VERY rudely explains our room isn't ready and acts as if we're insane to think it would be. I'm going to mention at this point it's 40 minutes before a typical check in - and I was your priority check in? You can't find a clean room to let my husband get ready for our wedding in? If there was a chance we couldn't check in, the lady should have mentioned that in the morning. Or at the very least the staff could have been nice and we would have received it better. They were rude and cold. Then it gets better because this same rude employee insists my husband gives them a card for a room we aren't even allowed to check into at this time. Why? You aren't letting us into the room anyways. All in all, less than stellar customer service upon arrival. We came back at midnight and the front desk was far nicer but said we already checked in that afternoon even though we never received keys or a call from the earlier employee. So again, it was unorganized and embarrassing for a hotel that prides itself in customer service. Luckily, our day went smoothly and we ignored annoying errors and miscommunication by the hotel. 

But honestly I'm not surprised because every time I spoke to this hotel leading up to the day there was inconsistency in customer service. They forgot to respond to messages and promised to reach out with updates and never did. Yikes. Would not recommend- it felt that they will not go out of their way for you and could care less about you - even on your wedding day.... Next time I'll stay at one of the other 5 hotels on Camelback for a better experience.

findings.title: Brennan P. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The Phoenician is a well-manicured hotel with a beautiful golf course and pool views. We stayed in late August for 4 nights dueinf COVID. Their COVID procedures are mostly impressive, except for a few blunders at the pool. I witnessed a pool attendant get asked by a pushy guest if she could "just move the cones so their whole family could sit together" and watched as the staff person nervously obliged. What's the point of the social distance cones if you're going to allow guests to ignore them? 

The resort is touted as 5-star but has less than 5 star feel/service/amenities. We were celebrating three big occasions this trip but no special treatment or congratulations was had. That's okay, but the other 5-star resorts in the area are known for things like this. Additionally, the resort has only one sit-down restaurant open right now and one bar (understandable), but they stop serving food at 9pm. So, there was nowhere to grab a drink or snack or dessert after about 8:30p. Breakfast is only offered on site at The Marketplace (small coffee/snack shop) and the one restaurant. The restaurant waffle was served very cold with bottled cold syrup ($17, of course.) service at The Tavern was just as cold-waitress seemed exhausted and annoyed with life. 

We found it pretty annoying/disappointing that on two days around 3pm we couldn't find the attendant who rents out the bicycles, so we couldn't rent them. Also the game room and gym are closed for covid, housekeeping is per request only, but the resort still imposes a high daily resort amenity fee. 

We were overall a little disappointed in the low energy, disappointing food, and lack of programming on site. Would not call it 5-star by any stretch. But, it's a pretty place to visit if service and value are not at the top of your priority list.

findings.title: Jared E. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
This review comes with the caveat that the resort is not operating as normal due to the virus.

We booked a "grand deluxe pool view room" which is the highest room category (other than suites). Due to the pandemic only every other room is occupied, and they are also allowing 24 hours to clean them. So, our first night there was not a pool view room available. The resort was able to get us into the proper room the next day, and also offered some amenities/lower price for the trouble which I really appreciated. This was more than fair and they went above and beyond service wise to make up for this--so as far as customer service goes they do an outstanding job to make sure guests are satisfied. 

I just can't quite give the hotel five stars--it's just not a five star hotel in my opinion and experience. The pool experience is unparalleled--fantastic service, plenty of towels and chairs, and many different pools to choose from. The adult pool is huge--and having an adult pool is really important to us when choosing hotels.

We had breakfast and food at the pool. The food was fine--it was good. Nothing crave worthy though to mention. The pool service was great.

As far as the rooms go--the king size beds seemed small to me. The sheets didn't seem up to par with a 5-star hotel. They advertise Frette linens, but they didn't seem like Frette to me, they were thin and rough, and reminded me more of standard marriott polyester sheets. There was nothing five star about the bed--and if you look forward to a big, cushy hotel bed with amazing linens you won't find it here.

The hotel has undergone a substantial renovation/redecorating. The color scheme is very dark gray--which I get is in vogue right now, but it was too dark, and too dramatic for a desert resort feel. The rooms were sparse, and they belonged in a NY or DC hotel. Nothing about the rooms stood out to me as worth the money. Institutional is how I would describe them. There is no refrigerator or microwave. There is a mini bar that has ostensibly been emptied due to the pandemic to minimize touch points, so we used that to keep water in--but it doesn't get very cold. They removed the coffee amenities, but when we called they brought a bag of pods and accessories to us almost immediately. Surprisingly, they are still using keurigs--the same model you'll find in any cheap hotel. I've not been in a high end hotel (Ritz/Park Hyatt, etc) in a while that isn't doing nespresso or illy coffee. They also ought to be offering a coffee coupon or something due to the pandemic to get a morning coffee from their market--that would be nice gesture considering.

The views from most rooms really didn't seem like they'd be great--and even after being moved the second day I wasn't that impressed with the room. Many rooms appear to have a view of nothing--which is unfortunate given the super high cost to stay at this hotel. Even in the summer rates for the pool view grand deluxe room were north of $300+fees/taxes. 

The room had a small sofa that seemed cheap. The patio furniture was way under par for a hotel of this caliber. The cushioning was badly soiled and needed deep cleaning or replaced. They could do much better on that end.

But, this isn't really a hotel where you're spending a lot of time in your room--it's just that you're spending a lot of money on it, so it should be up to par with hotels in the same category. This hotel had a lot of character before the renovation, and it's too bad they didn't keep some of that. The hotel now looks and feels like every other hotel--and we weren't paying to stay at every other hotel, we were paying to stay at the Phoenician.

I would stay here again to spend a couple days at the pools--if the price was right. However, other than the pools and the amazing staff all around at this hotel, it's just not impressive enough, at least during the pandemic, to justify the prices.

findings.title: Kate S. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I stayed here for 3 nights this past weekend. First, the good: 

-The resort is huge and rooms are spacious. 
-The customer service we received was amazing. Bartenders, pool attendants, etc were all very attentive.
-We loved the food at The Tavern and enjoyed hanging at the Thirsty Camel each night. 
-Pool was great (for the most part) and the food at the pool was really good and arrived very quickly which is rare for most hotel pools
-Hotel seemed to take proper COVID precautions which was much appreciated

The bad:
-We were very disappointed with the pool drinks. We tried a few different types of drinks on several different days (prickly pear margarita, watermelon margarita, vodka lemonade, etc) and they were the weakest drinks we have had in a long time. I'm not saying I need to get drunk off one drink but every drink we ordered tasted non-alcoholic and made you feel as if they are measuring half an ounce of liquor or less per drink. Very disappointing when our drinks ranged from $16-22 each. We finally gave up on drinking at the pool, it it seemed like a complete waste of money.
-The pool music was extremely loud several days to where it was impossible to focus on reading or talking to anyone else. We are two women in our mid 30's who like to have a good time but even for us it was way too much. The music just didn't seem to go with the pool vibe which was mostly couples relaxing and families playing with their kids. It was bizarre and made it hard to fully relax. Even with headphones in you could still hear it
-The bathroom in our hotel room (double queen) was huge which was a plus but we noticed it didn't have any sort of AC vents or venthood/fans in the bathroom. Even though our bedroom was a cool 68-70 degrees the bathroom was hot at all times. The smaller room that the toilet was in was incredibly warm, even when in there in the middle of the night. I'm assuming the hotel is so old that the bathroom vents were never built but this just seemed a bit absurd for a room this pricey not to have any bathroom air circulation. We also felt since there is no maid service that the bathroom should have been better stocked. One roll of toilet paper and one box of kleenex isn't enough for a 3 night stay. When we called for more toilet paper and asked for a couple more rolls they only brought us one. Just a few minor suggestions for any management that might be reading this

findings.title: Veronika Z. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We stayed her for 2 nights recently. Our room was pretty far from the pool and it was considered an upgrade. It was at least a 10 minute trek in 115 degree heat. The hotel didn't seem that busy (it's COVID) so I wish we were closer. The rooms were honestly whatever - reminded me of a typical Hilton/Hyatt - no frills.

The pool area was very good & had terrific service. This resort is extremely family & pet friendly.

A few items I think they can improve on are: the tavern restaurant (the breakfast wasn't great - definitely not 5 star worthy) and upon check-out the folio that I was handed didn't match the charge on my credit card. It ended up being double - when I called they said "sometimes that happens." Also the resort fees for tennis courts, putting green & bicycle rentals seem ridiculous in over 100 degree heat.

findings.title: Sarah C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I highly recommend this hotel. It has beautiful grounds, pools and rooms. We felt very safe visiting during Covid. Everyone properly wore their masks. The highlight of our trip was having Rich serve us at the Mother of Pearl cabana. He was so attentive bringing us water, food, and fresh towels. He properly wore his mask and gloves. We felt every indulged and safe. A big thank you to Rich!!

findings.title: Dan S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Arrived tonight hoping for a great staycation.  Paid for the highest upgraded room with a pool view. 

The first room we walked into was the second to last room on one wing with just a sliver of a pool view. To top that, the room was completely torn down and not even the sheets had been placed on the bed. 

Went back to concierge and they gave us a second room.  Sadly, this was a downgraded room on the lower level with just a view of the back of the pool restaraunt. 

When we turned on the bathroom sink to wash our hands, the master bath tub started filling with brown water that had dirt or some other grim particles coming out with it. 

Went back to the concierge and was told maintenance could come check it out. We didn't have any other rooms to choose from. 

Now two hours later, about to miss being able to eat at a restaraunt because they close in thirty minutes, maintenance is still in the room running grinders and other mechanical equipment to clean out plumbing lines.  

I went back to concierge and they were rather flippant about it and offered me a refund if I wanted to leave. 

I left. 

I'd recommend the Hyatt at Gainey ... they helped us out and the room is amazing.

findings.title: Christine V. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The Phoenician is so incredibly beautiful! The grounds are well kept, the golf course is gorgeous and the amenities are awesome! We stayed for a few days and absolutely loved it here! With your resort fee, you get a free movie each day, tennis racket and equipment rental and a few other things which is great for someone who likes to stay active and venture around. This property is massive and tons of fun for someone like me who gets bored and hates to feel confined. They have a cactus garden that is very well maintained and very zen, I loved getting my breakfast and coffee from the Market Cafe downstairs and walking through the garden - such a great start to the day!

The gym is very high end and very clean. Tons of Peleton bikes facing a huge open window with a great view, top notch machines, dumbells and cardio equipment. Things were spaced out due to COVID but it didn't affect the experience. The only bummer was the movement room was closed but it's understandable. Located below the gym is the game room with Shuffle board, pool, ping pong, arcade games, etc. Sadly, that was closed as well. Hopefully it'll be open when we come back.

Now, on to my absolute favorite thing, THE POOL! It was so relaxing and open 24/7 (we have never been somewhere with a 24 hour pool). We went for a midnight dip and ended up getting a cabana for the rest all of the days we were there. Service is excellent and Rich is the man! He's on top of it, funny, friendly and extremely attentive! Of all the people we met there, Rich was the one we missed the most when we left. If you want a delicious drink to sip on when you're in the pool - go for the Strawberry Lemonade (it has alcohol so it's not your regular strawberry lemonade - sip it slow cause it creeps up on you). There are several pools and it's kind of a split tri level set up. One is dedicated to adults, the others are for all ages and there's a splash zone! I still think the Mother of Pearl pool is the best!

We can't wait to come back for a visit! Please make sure you tip all the staff well - they work extremely hard and they go above and beyond!

*DUE TO COVID* 
There was no housekeeping, no game room, less artwork and decorative items, no valet, no reservations for lounge chairs and one less day the golf course was open. Trust me, it did not hinder our experience at all.

findings.title: John D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I'd say more like a 4.5 star rating. 

My wife and I stayed at the Phoenician for 8 nights recently. We used the Phoenician as our headquarters while we made small road trips throughout our stay (Saguaro National Park and Tucson one day, Sedona/Red Rock Canyon one day, Grand Canyon another day, and had a great time exploring Phoenix and Scottsdale in between). Along with our excursions, we had plenty enough time to enjoy our time on the resort. Unfortunately due to the Covid 19 stuff some of the resorts amenities were not available to us. Such as room service, daily room cleaning, a restaurant, and modified hours on bar. 

The resort is beautifully maintained and landscaped. Truly a little oasis in the desert. They have about five pools to enjoy a pool bar and wait staff at the pool areas to serve drinks and pool snacks. It was pretty quite during our stay and we had plenty of space to ourselves. We do wish the bar was open later and the music was better. Music really was crappy (sort of like a light dance or house music that was on a playlist cause same songs over and over). Drinks were quite good and the bar staff were friendly at the pool. 

We ate twice at the resorts Tavern. Once for breakfast which was ok for the price point and once for dinner and drinks. Again dinner was ok. During our dinner we were able to enjoy the live music which included two singing piano players singing mostly classics. They were entertaining bit because the crowd was sparse it was hard for them to muster up the crowd too much. The hotel bar is also nice. It overlooks the pool grounds and they make good drinks and it has a more dressy casual vibe. 

My favorite part of the resort was their own cactus garden on the grounds. It's small but certainly great for a nice walk to enjoy the local flora. Very beautiful. 

The resorts has some shops on premises but again the prices are so high on the goods they sell I'd be surprised if they make much money. 

There is a ton to do on resort as well as the immediate area. We found so many cool restaurants and coffee shops near by and was so pleasantly surprised by how consistently good restaurants in Scottsdale are. 

Wasn't too happy with $20.00 daily parking fees and resorts fees ($40-50 daily). 

All in all we had a great time and were happy with choosing the Phoenician as our home base. The staff are very welcoming and helpful. We'd certainly come back.

findings.title: Ryan T. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Last week I booked the Executive Suite for 2 nights for an interview shoot for a client. The day before we checked in, I popped over to the resort to see if myself and one of the crew members could have a look at the room for shooting purposes. We were told, in a rude manor by a lady at the front desk, that the room was not available to be viewed at that moment but we could come back upon check in to view the room. We agreed and returned the next day with our gear.

Upon checkin, the room was extremely bland with stains on the carpet, Oreo crumbs left underneath and on the couch and broken blinds. Ignoring this, as time was ticking before the interviewee was due to arrive, I asked the front desk clerk if there was a possibility of attaining anything visually pleasing such as, a plant or any type of decorative material to add some color to our shot. You would think that a hotel, offering an "Executive Suite" upwards of $700.00/night would accommodate accordingly. We were told that plants or decorative material was not possible but, they could deliver a couple small succulents. Busy with setting up and after the interviewee had arrived, we were still awaiting the succulents. We decided it was too late to add these succulents to the shot and to roll the cameras. At that time, 2 hours had passed.

I found the staff to be robotic, far from friendly and poorly trained in their mannerisms when dealing with customers. You would think that a room would be neat, everything in tact and for the staff to at least be warm and friendly when purchasing a room for $700/night.

I would never recommend The Phoenician to anyone for any reason. This was an unpleasant experience.

findings.title: B B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
3 nights of luxury! Professional and friendly staff. Kaylee at the front desk helped us find our ideal upgrade room and very helpful at providing us information. The hotel location is perfect, next to camel back mountain and Scottsdale. Amenities are limited (pools and golf only). Rooms were clean and spacious.
Tavern and Marketplace have excellent food selection (and coffee!), too bad the Steakhouse was still closed. If I already had an excellent experience with limited amenities/dining options, what more if they are fully operational?! Will definitely comeback and stay here longer!

findings.title: Michael M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My absolute favorite golf course and resort + spa. The best views, excellent service, and unmatched experiences. Whither you are hanging out by the pool, checking out the resorts vast amenities, or swinging away on their luxury golf course, you truly cannot lose. 
Highly worth the time.

findings.title: Ally D. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I am writing this review towards what I hope is the end of the COVID-19 pandemic. I had a trip planned after the Phoenician had been open for a couple weeks and I had scheduled the trip a couple weeks out- I was going there to help a friend with something. I have to say this establishment is disgraceful. During this pandemic, there have been many companies that have struggled to provide service and that is understandable. But, the Phoenician here has decided to take advantage of this chaos to employ poor customer service and bad business practices, and I will not forget- shame on them. A few days before my stay they sent an e-mail that went to my junk mail that they were cancelling the reservation due to the pandemic and they were closing again. Now, Phoenician is owned by Marriott and all the other hotels in the area are open safely. I am 100% sure they decided to cancel because they weren't getting the same higher rates they thought they might so they cancelled on everyone and closed their hotel- without even calling people! Of course they recommended you book at another hotel in the area, also owned by Marriott, which now had skyrocketed rates. If I didn't call for another reason I would have traveled there and had no idea I had no where to stay. I will not be booking at another one of their Marriott resorts like they hoped and now I am left to scramble and find decent priced lodging with all the others that had their reservations suddenly cancelled due to "safety concerns". Which the same supposed concerns were clearly not an issue for other hotels owned by the same company immediately next door. I would also like to add they gave no rate guarantee and did not even offer for the other hotels give the same rate. I expressed my angst at the unfairness of the situation to a person named Nicole there and she could not have been more argumentative and unhelpful and implied that they have no obligation to call and that I should do better about checking my junk mail. This all was clearly a poor move on their part to try to boost earnings at other hotels in the area and carried out in a very disorganized manner.

findings.title: Meg C. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
This is the view from our balcony. The noise is unbearable. Even worse during the day. So very disappointing! To come all this way to celebrate not one but two 60th birthdays. 
Management unwil

findings.title: Chen W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Gorgeous resort. Every time I stay here, I'm pleased. This is my go-to hotel when I'm in Phoenix. The afternoon tea service is better than the hotels I've frequented in London...even forces me to drink with my little pinky out. The pool is a sanctuary of beauty in every way, especially the perfect bodies...I mean, drink servers...everywhere. Great hotel rooms, comfort, fabulous service. Class-act in every way. (Wish I could say the same for myself, hehe)  ;)

findings.title: Gianna D. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Such an amazing hotel experience. The Phoenician is a perfect luxurious escape. If you're headed to Scottsdale, want to pool, spa, and splurge, this is your place. This place is NOT trendy but instead a classy getaway with stunning views of Camleback Mountain.

findings.title: Tanga S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Its crazy how a 5 star hotel can be so filthy and dirty! 
Public restrooms were very dirty and there was no toilet paper.  Not only that but my bed had BEDBUGS! Hotel staff should spend more money to keep bed bugs away and to hire good cleaning staff. Resort is beautiful but i will never stay here again. If hotel looks like this i can imagine how food is made!!!

findings.title: Dave P. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Nice resort but watch your bill!! There was a porterage charge for $14 even though the bellman never touched our bags.

findings.title: Sara H. (1/5)
findings.snippet: My friends were coming in town from the East Coast to visit me and cheer me up, as my husband was leaving for work until October (at the earliest). Being that we have six kids between us I thought we all could use a "mommy break" for a night. Our plan was to stay the night and then we had a daybed booked for the next day to lay by the pool and relax. We had to cancel early next morning and leave the resort for a medical emergency and when I called to check out and explained our situation the woman told me they completely understood and told me she would send me a day pass so we could come back two days later before my friends left (barring everything was okay). Because why wouldn't they understand and offer me that? I paid for the casita for the night, three massages, and food and drinks, and didn't even get to enjoy the pool. Well after our emergency was in the clear I called the hotel to ask to reserve a daybed again and mentioned that I had never received my day pass in the email as promised. Bottom line I was bounced around to three different people telling me they don't do day passes. Now I really don't care what your policy is or isn't BUT if one of your employees tells me I can come back with the hotels full understanding that emergencies happen, I expect decent customer service and for that promise to be upheld. Andrew, who showed no empathy whatsoever, made me make another reservation for that night (EVEN THOUGH WE COULDN'T STAY THAT NIGHT BECAUSE I HAVE THREE CHILDREN) and rebook a whole other room because it is hotel policy that you need a reservation to make charges to. So I begrudgingly did it (now I'm in for twice the money with half the stay) because I wanted to show my friends a good time that was promised to us. WELL this "policy" was proven wrong when we finally got out to the pool and my friend walked right up to the bar and the nice bartender told her "no I don't need your hotel room" and let my friend charge things to her credit card. I am extremely upset with this standard of customer service, especially with my husband being a titanium elite Marriott member. Luckily for this hotel, Hannah P. was a gift from above that day and turned my day around by immediately saying "what can I do to help" and was completely attentive and respectful the whole day. Extremely disappointed still as the hotel has made no attempt to contact us.

findings.title: Jennifer R. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
The service is disgraceful. We had a family emergency and had to leave a day early from our stay. When we checked out, they said they would give us a day pass to come back and enjoy the missed day. We arrive back days later to get the day pass, and Andrew claims there is no recollection of this agreement and they won't offer that. He said that it was a mistake we were told that, yet he did NOTHING to fix the mistake.  Granted we have a titanium elite membership, have endless bookings with Marriott in the past 13 months alone. You think they'd at least fix their own mistake instead of just lying and not rectify the situation. Instead of trying to fix their mistake, they said the only way we can enjoy day amenities a is to BOOK AN ENTIRELY NEW ROOM WHEN WE ARENT EVEN STAYING OVERNIGHT.  It's unreal to me that this 'elite' of a resort has made zero effort to make customer service a priority.  Make eye contact next time Andrew and own up to the huge error on y'all part Instead of being a jerk and just not give a damn with a woman crying on the phone to you about her frustration.

On the total opposite end of the spectrum, Hannah who works the poolside service was PHENOMENAL. She was such a delight and attentive to us the entire day

findings.title: Robin H. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Came here for a luxurious experience. The rooms were nothing but basic. Almost relatable to a motel 6, but paying nearly 700/night. Was lied to about the late check out time and was told it was impossible to stay another night even though there were rooms available when we looked online. The concierge was rude when she told us we had to get out immediately.

findings.title: James H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: A few friends and I were in town visiting for a convention.  We decided to stay here as it appeared in a good location and close to everything we would need.  This spot did not disappoint.  The restaurants at the hotel were on point as well as the hotel service.  Will definitely come back in the future.

findings.title: Monica K. (1/5)
findings.snippet: My friends and I booked a trip in November for arrival January 23rd - 26th.  We expressed numerous times to the staff at the Phoenician that this was a double birthday trip as well as a tennis trip.  A week prior to the trip, I called and booked 3 tennis classes, Friday the Live-ball class at 10:00, and Saturday two classes, the Stroke of the Day and the Live-ball class.  I asked about reserving the tennis courts for 2 hours each day (we had two rooms and you are given an hour for each room included in your daily resort fee) but was told that they hardly ever book up and we could get a court whenever we wanted it for.  On Friday morning, I received a "text" from the tennis instructor, Ivan Rodriguez, and he apologized but there was a resort wide tennis tournament that weekend and we would not be having any classes.  REALLY?  As this was a planned tennis trip from the beginning.  We flew in from Fayetteville, AR to play tennis this weekend.  I then tried calling Ivan and he did not answer my call.  I texted for him to call me but never heard from him.  We then went to the tennis facility to speak to Ivan in person.  He said that he would try and do his best to work something out for us.  About 2 hours later, I received a text from Ivan offering lunch at the Phoenician Tavern comped and he would have us a court from 3:00-4:00 and a lesson comped on him from 4:00-5:00.  That was great news, at least we got 2 of the 3 hours of tennis that we planned to play..  We left at 5 with Ivan telling us that he would comp any tennis for the rest of our trip and would get with us later.  I texted him again Saturday morning at 8 to ask about getting a court for us to play on.  3 hours later, I texted him again, as he had not responded.  He then texted back and offered us 1 hour at a neighboring tennis court later that afternoon "if" we had transportation.    We declined as we did not have transportation and the time he was offering did not work for us as in the 3 hours it took for him to respond, we made other plans.  We NEVER heard back from Ivan again.  We did not get any tennis time in on Saturday or Sunday!  As we were eating at the Tavern, which overlooks the golf course, my friends and I wondered, what would happen if we had been 4 men that booked a golf trip here?  And, a week ahead, we booked our tee time for 10:00 on Friday, and again on Saturday.  However, the golf pro "texted" us an hour before our tee time to advise that there was a resort wide golf tournament and we would be unable to get on the golf course the entire length of our visit.  Do you think that would ever happen?  NO, I do not believe it would.  I have been home now for 2 days and I am still APPALLED that we spent so much money for a tennis trip where the tennis was pretty much non-existent.  I would not recommend staying at this place at all!!!!!   We should have had everything we wanted comped and offered a free stay on another weekend where we could have played tennis.

findings.title: Nohelia J. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I come with my husband  for his Anual meeting 2020. We love the hotel and the service. The people here is very nice and helpful. Thank you!  We love  it!!!

findings.title: Manda Bear B. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
4.5 stars

Beautiful place, golf course, multiple pools, spa, multiply restaurants, they design to keep you on the resort and not leaving it to go anywhere else!

We enjoyed the pool. Loved the walk around the golf course. Great food & service at the J&G steakhouse & got to watch the beautiful sunset over the mountain. 

We also enjoy the Marketplace coffee shop/bistro a lot.

The room itself was simple, nothing special, a little dated for a Category 7 Marriott Bonvoy! We got upgrade to the one facing the Cactus Garden Camelback Mountain Trail. Which was nice but my allergy was bad!  

We hated the pillows, too soft and flatted! The shower pressure was really weak, I understand it's the desert so they save water!

I enjoyed the bathtub a lot though! 

Long walk from the lobby to our room! You can cut shorter walk by using the stairs! 

A few other restaurants here is nothing special, limited menu, no Asian food nor anything interesting or modern! 

The service here is great. From the bellmen to the Tavern, from Anthony at the Marketplace to Rasa and Austin & the GM at the J&G Steakhouse. 

But little thing here and there not luxurious as you would find at a Four Seasons, Pennisula or St. Regis. Or even some of the other Luxury Collections hotel worldwide! At category 7, we expected a little more nicer touch.

findings.title: Little Black Dress W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Really enjoyed our stay. simple, beautiful, elegant. Staff were non-intrusive but always had my drinks refilled, towels on pool chairs and a clean room. Loved it! Thanks for being our desert oasis!

findings.title: Karina G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My daughter in law took me to the Phoenician for afternoon tea service. It was beautiful. The service was top notch, so friendly, attentive, and made us feel special every time they came to our table. 

The tea selection is wonderful, your herbals, greens, and black teas. I chose the orange spice, and my daughter in law got the jasmine pearl, we shared each one, they both were delightful! 

The first course of adorable finger sandwiches consisted of cucumber, asparagus, lox, chicken salad, and egg salad. 
All the sandwiches were so tasty! Your server will return with the sandwich tray, just in case you want seconds! 

The second course: The Devonshire cream, strawberry preserves, and lemon curd were all delicious! Served with a cranberry and plan biscuits. The biscuits were so delicious, they were buttery, flavorful, tender melt in your mouth! 

Lastly, the third and final course offerings, was a sweet ending to our amazing tea! Chocolate covered strawberries, selection of mousse's, biscotti, and petite cakes! 

I'll definitely be back for this lovely tea service! 
A great way to treat a special guest, or celebrate a special occasion!

findings.title: Anna T. (2/5)
findings.snippet: So many better places to stay in the Valley.  Did a two night stint during my two-week holiday to visit family in the Phoenix area for Christmas (lodging elsewhere, thankfully for the remainder).  Booked direct, ended up in a room that I can only imagine is single purpose for meeting planners (3094) running conferences as it is the at the end of the hallway past the meeting rooms (creepy vibe to start-and even weirder there is no 3093 although there is a door you pass) and then the territorial view was ....wait for it...a direct view of the loading dock and HVAC system which, it gets better, vents the kitchen exhaust and blows out the bacon/hamburger etc. cooking air for half the day.  It was comical.  They gave us NO warning that is where our family of four would be enjoying our time to relax together over the holiday.  To add insult to injury they have this scammy "free breakfast for two" offer that I booked and when I checked in the front desk staff said it was a $65 credit to be used in the restaurants (which we stayed and ate on property for the duration of our stay).  I just received an adjusted folio clawing backing the portion of the daily $65 credit that wasn't used @ breakfast!?!?  I guess breakfast by the pool didn't count, who knew!? And it certainly didn't work the way explained at check in, feels like a bait and switch getting a second adjusted folio the day after check out with these adjustments.  I did enjoy the pool with the kids but that was about it.  Will be skipping this property for the spring visit.  I hope they stop putting room 3094 in general inventory or build a wall with a garden trellis to make the view manageable (and make sure guests staying in that room love the smell of bacon and hamburgers lol). #notluxury

findings.title: Sunil R. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I was here for a conference and had a good stay. The rooms were well equipped and the hotel itself is beautiful. There is a lot of good hiking in the area depending on the time of the year of course. The gym was huge and even had Peloton. There is an entertainment center under the gym with ping pong, pool etc too.

findings.title: Sara E. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
One of my favorite parts of vacation in warm areas is staying at luxurious resorts. As such, I was REALLY looking forward to my stay at the Phoenician, planned to happen perfectly timed after family left from the holidays. However, our stay at the Phoenician was really underwhelming.

The hotel itself is absolutely beautiful, and you definitely know you're in a luxury resort when you get there. 

However, the entire stay was incredibly impersonal. From other resorts I've stayed at, they really put in the effort to make your stay phenomenal, and the Phoenician did not even put in the barest of efforts to do that. Here are some examples:

Check-in was quick, but there was absolutely no mention of anything the resort had to offer. Also nothing special with having Marriott status. No water or other beverages in the lobby... I can't remember any resort I've stayed at not having that available. This is the theme for the stay.

The room was not thoroughly cleaned prior to check-in: there were noticeable large cobwebs  in the room that I noticed immediately after walking into the room, and the guide book had dirty pages in it that were put back in out of order, upside down, etc. (this is something rather small but not very what you'd expect at a true luxury resort).

The coffee option in the room is Keurig with terrible coffee and paper cups. I'd definitely expect something better from this price point, such as Nespresso and ceramic mugs.

Whatever, I decided I would try to make the resort fee worth it and figure out what is included in the resort fee.

It was very difficult to find out when and where yoga classes were. The gentleman at the fitness center did not have a schedule. I did make it to one yoga class after finally figuring out they were in the spa, and the class itself was wonderful. That was the one resort amenity I was able to try.

Although advertised, I was unable to make a reservation for the Cocktail Mixology class as the hostess at Mowry & Cotton stayed that reservations needed to be made 24+ hours in advance (not stated anywhere). Additionally, we tried going to the Epicurean Moment which is advertised as happening daily, but we were told that they were not having it this week because "we are getting waffle cone batter next week." So this is what my resort fee is going to. Cool.

The pools at the resort are all outside, and there is only one hot tub. It was too cold out to go swimming or even lay on a chaise lounges, but the only indoor pool is located in the spa, and guess what, you have the privilege of paying $30 to access that as a resort guest.

All in all, our stay here was one big series of transactions and did not feel like a luxury, welcoming experience. If it wasn't such a pricey place that's pegged as luxury, it might have earned more stars. Next time I'm in Scottsdale, I will give a truly luxury resort a try.

findings.title: Michael W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This was one of the nicest hotels I have visited with the best service I have ever experienced within the USA.  Service is definitely their forte. No more needs to be said.

findings.title: John X. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The Phonecian, Luxury collection resort has been on my bucket list for a while. Located in Scottsdale Arizona, its a very exclusive luxurious resort with plenty of amenities, beautiful views, great dining, and amazing rooms. It will be about a 30 min drive from the airport, but not far from many places in Scottsdale if you do want to leave.


There's a guard shack to get in, though it can't be hard since ubers get in all the time. You drive to the end for reception, passing by a massive sports complex on the left (which I didn't get toenjoy but looked amazing). Reception is in a beautiful lobby overlooking the resort that compares closely to any Ritz, St. Regis, or other 5 star property. Think swanky furniture, mood lighting, and luxury touches. Check-in was quick and easy, and off I went to my Casitas suite (thank you suite night awards).


The suite was absolutely amazing with a kitchenette, dining table, living room with plenty of seating, 2 Full Baths (seriously, with 2 sets of soaking tubs and showers), and a humongous master bedroom thats bigger then most hotel rooms. Patios overlooking the pool complex completes the room. Frette slippers were just some of the finer touches you don't see even at most 5 star resorts. 


The pool complex was amazing as well, and since this was winter not crowded at all. If you're in the casitas you will have to walk through them to get to the main complex again (highly recommend dining at Mowry & Cotton)


This is not a cheap property, but worth every penny. Needs to be on everyones bucket list.

findings.title: Trinh P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This resort is gorgeous! Truly paradise when I was here in mid-May for a work trip. The room I stayed in was the Casita guestroom with the King sized bed. Clean and beautiful, my favorite part of the room was the back where there was a lovely patio for you to get some fresh air and lounge around indirectly under the sun. Scottsdale is hot! It reached the 100s when I was there but our patio was in the shade so it was perfect. There was a gym and restaurant in walking distance - if  you do not want to walk you can call for a golf cart service and they pick you up from your room. Probably one of the best resorts I stayed at so far.

findings.title: Zach H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Beautiful!  I am just getting around to write about my labor day stay-cation here.  The staff dealt with the extra crowd with ease.  The service everywhere we went was fantastic and done with a smile.  The pool was nice and relaxing.  Having separate pools for the kids makes the adult pool much more enjoyable.  

I will be back.  This is a great place to relax and spend a nice weekend.

findings.title: Mark G. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Well I don't think I will stay here again . Beautiful property, but guest accommodations and service are weak at best. This is not a luxury hotel, it's more like a typical Marriott . This may sound harsh,  but I rarely write reviews and usually don't complain , but just felt this was needed .

This is my second year attempting to spend my Anniversary at this property. Last year my wife and I  came for the first time and stayed at the canyon suites . We were very specific that we wanted a golf course /city view room . I order champagne and strawberries to be delivered on arrival. On arrival we had no champagne  and a view of a rock , the exact opposite of what we were promised . We were eventually given the correct room after complaining and champagne was delivered the following day when we were gone ??We then went to spa which was marginal at best - we were assured the inexperienced therapist were new and would be replaced . 

This year our son is attending ASU and parents weekend fell on our anniversary and we thought we would give it one more try . Same plans , champagne and a view room , but this time we thought we would stay at the regular Phoenician hotel and booked a " view suite" . We were again assured we would have a view over the pool and city . Again no champagne and our view is of a giant air conditioning unit and roof top . This time nothing can be done and we are stuck paying $900 for a shitty room and not the room we were promised  . Just returned from spa again same crappy therapists. Just a "sorry you are disappointed and would you like charge the $400 treatment to your room". Don't get me wrong it's a nice facility , but staff with very poor and inexperienced therapists. 

So needless to say this is my last stay !! And this is the way they treat their bonvoy platinum members!! 

Beware!

findings.title: Dana R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We are here for a conference and the staff here was amazing.  Everything was smooth from check in to check out.      Beautiful resort and awesome food.    The cactus garden was a pleasant surprise to walk thru.    Being the first time to Arizona, we were pleasantly surprised to be able to see so many different varieties of cacti in one area.

findings.title: Andrea B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We've stayed here 2 nights and I spent all day yesterday at the spa. This place is perfect. All the staff are ready to help at s moment's notice and the cleanliness of everything is . I had the 2 hour full body scrub/mud/ massage and the 90 minute facial.  Best experience ever. Breakfast both days was great and we were visited by their resident hawk and handler too (Calvin). Loved it. 
I only have one request for change.  It REALLY bothers me that they have chosen to give business to a cruel, dehumanizing, child enslaving/trafficking and America hating company like Nike.  They put their entire outdoor staff in that horrible clothing.  It's like a putrid cancer pimple on the face of the Venus de Milo. 
Come on Phoenician, you can do better than this.  Buy American.  Your customers do.

findings.title: Kara F. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Gorgeous. Superb customer service.  The pools and rooms are extremely clean and beautiful. We will definitely return soon!

findings.title: Chris C. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Interesting stay at this resort and perhaps I was expecting too much. Check in was a total joke. I had to repeat myself so many times that I had to write things down on a piece of paper and show it to the lady. I got to the point of frustration that I almost wanted to simply walk out; literally 15 minutes to get checked in and I was the only person there. They rooms are ok but nothing special. The room service food was actually quite good and that's a sad commentary when that is what I will take away from my stay. Wanted to try and obtain a little later check out time and I was told to call back the next morning to inquire if that could or would be accommodated. That helps. Not. Anyway, there are more than enough options in the area and I am here for business quite a lot these days. One and done with this place. On to the next. My advice... maybe this was a great place a decade or two ago... not now. Enough said.

findings.title: Jon H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
"Under certain circumstances there are few hours in life more agreeable than the hour dedicated to the ceremony known as afternoon tea"

-Henry James

It feels sinful to have this much pleasure. The beautiful place setting of dishes, magnificent decor, gorgeous surroundings, all in a comfortable manner. Yes, I could live here. Ah, if only. The Phoenician Resort is a perfect setting for afternoon tea. Its majestic views of mountains and valley all lend to its splendor. 

Seating began promptly at 2pm Sunday afternoon. The hostess Miss Lillian effortlessly guides awaiting patrons eager to begin the afternoon tea journey. A delicious journey of 3 courses plus champagne if you so choose. 
I chose! Perrier Jouet please. Our servers and now friends Miss Wanda and Miss Natalie were absolute true gems! They made the experience here more heavenly. 

First course of amazing finger sandwiches were delicate and refined. No bread crust please! (Please see photo) 
Fillings for such included: Salmon, Cream Cheese, Tuna, Egg Salad, and a Canapé topped with a twisted cucumber slice. All well crafted and delish! 
2 pots of brewing tea: Darjeeling with milk and Peppermint. Did I mention the Perrier Jouet? Yummy!
2 types of Scones: Plain and Cranberries. Top them  off with Lemon Curd, or Jam and of course plenty of whipped creme fraiche!!! Who knew? I knew! 
Finished it off with a tray of chocolate treats to die for! 

I must say that we did not leave hungry. Everyone was offered an abundance of the first course which is my favorite. That being said, our journey complete, it was easy to Uber out. Please see the photos and feel free to drool. As I pen this, I'm drooling remembering all we had.
Valet parking is available and self parking is free for 3 hours. Either way, its a win. 

As always, thank you for reading. =)

findings.title: christy m. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Full tea is lovely and well done. Felt a bit rushed at times.  Food was fabulous and plentiful.  View is lovely and pianist is perfection!

findings.title: Rachel O. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Raul is an amazing bartender.  Great customer service, very friendly, and extremely knowledgable in the art of making drinks.

findings.title: William W. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Amazing Resort!  The staff at all levels and areas make you feel like a celebrity. From the valets, room attendants, Reception, and pool attendants... everyone is on point. We've stayed at several high end resorts in Phoenix and the Phoenician is a class above. 

Stayed in a casita with an vies if the waterfall garden, do relaxing and enjoyed the sound. Pool area luxury at its best. Like the adult only pool available. 

Beautiful grounds. Highly recommend.

findings.title: Becki H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Just returned from the best getaway! Goodness the Phoenician surely doesn't disappoint! I have been to very few places that have the customer service skills these ladies and gents shower you with, if you have a problem they have a solution! In fact you don't even have to have a problem and they still make you feel like they've came up with a solution. My husband and I went out for a hike one morning, we returned and while walking down the hallway to our room the kindest man said "mam, can I get you some ice and a few bottles of water" 
then offered to deliver it to our room. Seriously, we stayed here for 5 days and experienced this kind of service multiple times a day. The rooms are clean, the food was great, accommodations couldn't be beat, the views were amazing and you already know how I feel about the service. Just book your stay and enjoy!

findings.title: Ruchi S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
There was a SNAKE IN MY ROOM, and I had to deal with the snake myself. The management did not care to change my room, alert other guests or make up for my inconvenience. I sent a written complaint last week and the management does not seem to care at all. Here is the full sequence of events:

- I dealt with the snake myself, while the room-service staff stood dumbfound. On top of that, no hotel staff cared to look for the snake as it escaped! None of my neighbors were alerted about the presence of a snake in that wing.

- I was not offered to change or upgrade the room. I had to ask for a room change. The receptionist replied to my request by saying, "would you come collect the keys from the lobby, or should I send it to you?"

- Hotel management just offered to cover my resort fee for my troubles. This is neither adequate nor helpful.

- at the check-out, the front desk manager asked me, "please do not write any email to customer service, instead reach out to the hotel staff for any further discussion."

- finally, when I reached out to the Marriott Bonvoy customer service, they looped me back to the front desk staff at The Phoenician. (These were the people who didn't care at all in the first place). I have not received any response since then, and it has been about a week since I flagged the concern.

findings.title: Charles C. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
My wife and I enjoyed our recent stay at the Phoenician.  We had been talking about staying here for awhile and were not disappointed.  The hotel grounds are stunning.  It really has a lot going on and is a massive property.

They have a lot of shops and places to explore which was fun.  You really have everything that you need on the property if you didn't want to leave.

The pools were fantastic.  We explored them late night and had a great time swimming without anyone bothering us.  

The room was well appointed and also quite spacious.  The bathroom had a nice tub and the dual vanity was a nice touch.  The beds were also comfortable.

The one thing that was irritating is that it is almost impossible to find any ice near the room we where at.  My wife ended up hiking quite a distance to finally get some ice. That could be improved.  

All-in-all, this was a nice experience.

findings.title: Celia J. (1/5)
findings.snippet: We stopped by on Thursday to look at the resort. We were on vacation at a nearby resort and wanted to see this place as a potential possibility our next trip.  You can either valet your car or park in their garage ($8.00 zero to 30 minutes)! We parked in the garage and went to the lobby and the young woman at the check in desk was like " we can't take reservations here... you can only do it on line" . We explained that we were staying nearby and wanted to see this place as a possible new place to stay next time.  I asked her to validate our parking ticket cause I knew were not staying long but she said " no, we don't do that-- only if you eat in our restaurants ". She handed us a map and said "go look around " and that was it. We will never stay there! No one seemed to care and we stayed less than 15 minutes and paid 8.00 to park.

findings.title: Lateefah C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Hiked camelback with Alan from the Phoenician today. Great guy, very patient, goes at the speed of the group and won't pressure you if you want to stop anywhere on the trail and let the rest of the group go ahead (like I did LOL). If you're new to the trail or even if you've done it a ton of times and you would just like some company, I suggest going with Alan since he can acclimate to whatever fitness level you're at.

findings.title: Jed S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
They should change their slogan to, "We'll leave a light on for you." because they've hit a new low in unaccommodating accommodations.
The food was terrible. Rotten fruit plates, stale english muffins, and wilted, slimy lettuce. The rooms, we had 2, had mold on the ceilings in the bathroom, the decor is dark and depressing. They nickle and dime you for everything. 20 bucks a day to park at their business, 50 bucks to "rent" a single lounge chair by the pool when the few public chairs are gone. They got rid of the wonderful koi in the pond and replaced them with fake, plastic swans and sterile, chlorinated water. The staff seemed depressed and overworked. There are too many nice resorts in Phoenix to stay at this over priced Motel 6.

findings.title: Casey B. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Compared to other 4 or 5 star resorts I've stayed at recently this place is terrible. It was for my boyfriend and I's 3 year anniversary, wrote that in the notes, and nothing special at all was done for us upon arrival. All other resorts have surprised us with swan towels or roses, or chocolate covered strawberries. 
In addition, I paid an extra 50 bucks for a Garden View suite, and the only view we ended up with was the concrete street below and a big noisy tree filled with hundreds of pigeons who kept us up all night. The opposite of any kind of view worth paying extra for. 
To add, after a short hour dust storm, the staff strapped down all pool chairs. 5 hours later way after the storm passed, all the cushions were still removed from the pool area, and there was a ton of leaves in the hot tub, leaving our attempt at a calm night by the hot tub time impossible. We even tried just hanging by the outdoor fire pit, and that was not even functional! 
To top everything off, we ate dinner at the Tavern on the resort, I had a simple fried chicken appetizer, and had to send it back because the chicken was slimy, undercooked, and gross. And the next Morning, I threw up for 6 HOURS because I had food poisoning from the chicken! 
Terrible terrible terrible experience. Oh last thing, we didn't park our car overnight and was still charged for it, they canceled the events at the resort, and still charged for them. I would never ever stay there again.
