Like I said I didn't stay long but my short stay was just the relaxation and vibe I needed. I can't wait to revisit.

findings.title: Cara T. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We did a crazy thing and visited ARIZONA Phoenician in the summer! We met some friends there that stayed the night and had a birthday gathering.

It was perfect weather, not too hot in the upper 90's and this hotel has the HEAT under control - they had misters that make it feel like a 70 degree day which allowed us to eat outside, enjoy the pool & time with our friends.

The renovations are just improving on perfection. The water structures and slide for the kids was a huge plus- they had such fun. 

The best part of this hotel is the CUSTOMER SERVICE. Everyone we encountered was gracious and you can tell they have a priority to treat the customer right. 

We will be back for our own "staycation" with our family in the future. Can't wait! Thank you Phoenician for our amazing day !

findings.title: S C. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Can a hotel penalize you for not checking out on time when it's taken 90 minutes to get your brunch? The service here is AWFUL and our food was cold. Was the same all day yesterday... sat at the bar (with only 3 other guests) for 10 min before the bartender even acknowledged us... was 20 min before we finally got our drinks.  In both scenarios I had to actually ask if we had a server- only to learn it was the one standings in front of us.  If nothing else, "I'll be right with you" goes a long way.  Hospitality 101. How is the a luxury's resort?

findings.title: Erin S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We have stayed at seven different SPG hotels in the Phoenix area over the last 6 months and this one is our favorite resort style hotel by far ( the downtown Westin is our favorite non resort hotel). The Phoenician has been remodeled, is clean , bright and homey feeling. The bed is of course heavenly and staff are super helpful and friendly. There are multiple pools including one for adults and a small water park area for kids. The fitness center is amazing , there is tennis , golf, and hiking (camelback is the backyard of the hotel ). Parking is underground and convenient to the hotel. Location in general is also great with easy access to so many things !

findings.title: Rachel B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The service at the Suites (at The Phoenician) was the best I've ever had. Personal, helpful, and detail oriented. It made for an amazing luxe and relaxing weekend with girlfriends. Tom was particularly kind and helpful in prepping us to hike Camel Back. Cody drove us where we needed. It was truly amazing.

findings.title: Cesar R. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Had a wonderful stay while hosting a multiple day event at the resort. 

Absolutely love her mid-century modern look of the exterior as well as the updates made to the event spaces.

Staff was very attentive, friendly and knowledgeable

My room was huge and had a great view of the pool. 

There are a few few restaurants on property my favorite being Mowry & Cotton. You most definitely eat there while at the hotel. 

Beautiful pools and a brand new spa center. 

Will definitely be back.

findings.title: Sarah J. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Had a great weekend there! Supreme customer service, beautiful pools, great food. Restaurant closes a bit too early for the weekend, but it's not far from other restaurants. The staff is friendly and efficient. I will definitely be back!

findings.title: Raphy S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I just got home from this amazing Resort... We had an amazing time here. The staff were so friendly, every time you'd leave your room housekeeping is right behind you to go clean up your room. Service here was excellent. Overall had an unbelievable stay. Would definitely come back here. 
Who ever is doubting this hotel, DONT!!!... It is a 10 star resort.

findings.title: Victor L. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The epitome of luxury!! 

The Phoenician and their amazing Guest Experience Team, specifically Shanielle Tara Jones, set the highest standards of luxury I've ever seen. The facilities are BRAND new. The food is greeatttt, and the rooms are super spacious. Belinda from the BRAND NEW fitness center does an outstanding job at making sure everyone is taken care of. Definitely will be back.

findings.title: K J. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This review is for the spa only. I purchased a Groupon for a 50-minute massage and WOW; it was amazing! The spa was recently renovated and, no joke, it is the most beautiful spa I have been to - and I've visited most of the high-end resort spas in the valley. The large locker room had plush robes, vanities, everything you need to get cleaned up (hair dryers, deodorant, etc), nice showers, and a separate changing area. The waiting room was large and pretty. Attached to the waiting room is a relaxation area, complete with your own private pod to rest on a cozy chaise with a soft blanket and sip on one of the many tea selections. This was my favorite spot! The steam room was large with dim lighting so you don't feel too exposed. I get overheated easily and was pleasantly surprised that it was warm but not hot. I spent 10-15 minutes in there relaxing and inhaling the eucalyptus scent. Usually I can't last 5 mins! The sauna was spacious as well and very pleasant. The hot tub was huge! I don't enjoy feeling like I'm sharing a bath with someone, so I appreciated its large size. The whole spa was just gorgeous. 

I started the day with the complimentary Guided Meditation class. Go to this class! It was the perfect way to relax and shut my brain off before my massage. I felt bad because I was the only person who attended (the summer is usually slow for AZ resorts and I went on a Sunday). But rather than cancel the class, the instructor made me a comfy makeshift chaise to rest on and gave me a 1-on-1 guided meditation session. She was so sweet and the whole experience was wonderful. 

Then it was time for the massage. My therapist's name was Jennifer and she was so sweet and personable. The massage was only scheduled for 50 minutes (about 40-45 hands-on) but she was excellent. Most basic massages are light and, while relaxing, don't get out the knots. Jennifer was able to do both in a short amount of time! One of the best massages I've ever had! 

I am already planning my next visit to the Phoenician spa. Can't wait to go back!

findings.title: Meredith S. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We came to The Phoenician for a staycation/babymoon. We stayed Saturday-Monday. Thank you for the Sparkling Apple Cider, candy, and the stuffed animal. 

Room Accommodations:
Our room location was great. We enjoyed the quiet room, atmosphere, and comfy bed. All I would suggest to have a hand shower, the water pressure was not that strong.

Mowry & Cotton:
We ate here for breakfast on Sunday at 10am. We had the worst service of all time! The waitress took our order. We received our drinks and food right away. Then we sat for 25 minutes with no refill of either water or Orange Juice. The restaurant was not busy at all, only 4 tables were full. After this experience eating on property we decided to go off property for our meals. I was appalled with the service being a high end Resort. 

Pool:
We spent a long day at the pool Sunday. The pool attendants and waitress (Hannah) were very helpful and attentive. They all made sure we had cold pitcher of water to keep hydrated. The food was great. Thank you for all your hard work on a hot summer day!

I would definitely come back to stay here.

findings.title: Lu L. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This is the best afternoon tea I've had in town (Much better than the tea at The Biltmore)! You feel pampered the moment you get seated - live piano playing right next to us, gorgeous view of the trees and mountains outside, and elegant tableware in front of you. The waiter brings in three courses (finger sandwiches, scones, and tea pastries) separately on plates, and he/she will place them on your plate. 

All finger sandwiches were amazing - the bread was moist and the fillings had their own characters. I loved the one with asparagus, garlic herb mousse and aged Parma ham. The freshness of asparagus was balanced with the creaminess of the mousse, adding on top the rich flavor from the Parma ham. And you can feel different layers and nuances in flavor in one bite. 

Ok, the highlight was the scones (as always). I have to say that the scones didn't fail me this time. They were not too sweet, very soft and moist inside, with the golden color outside. The strawberry preserves were super natural that you could see the whole strawberry inside. And they go really well with the buttery scones by adding a bit acidity to the palette. Yum! 

By the time we got to the pastry course, we were already so full. Pastries were all really good. The coffee opera cake, fruit tart, and  chocolate dipped strawberries were outstanding. 

Overall, we had a great experience here. Will definitely come back for the great food and ambiance.

findings.title: Jonathan M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Phoenician is uber luxury and excellent service.  There was one gentleman who showed us to our banquet event by the name of Jonathan who was awesome.  Love the food at J and G.  Will return!

findings.title: Liss C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Resort is wonderful- Review is on a few exceptional folks and tips to the rooms and drinks & room service 

Anthony - Doorman: One is the nicest, most professional doormen I have ever encountered at a resort, assisting with my car, luggage and parking.  Anthony- you started my stay off stupendously!

Ryan - Checking in was quick to please getting me in to a room with a beautiful view of the massive multiple level pool.

Edgar- Mowry & Cotton Bartender 
Made a wonderful "Old orchard cocktail ($15, pricy but worth it)- Cucumber vodka, refreshing with a splash of champagne 

Room service: OMG toast! They bring you your OWN TOASTER to toast your bread so it's hot right when you want to eat. I have never ever had that level of service before, not even at a four seasons has a toaster been brought to me. Well played Phoenician! Greek yogurt and fruit was fresh and wonderful.

Coffee in your room: It's on a pullout drawer! Fantastic- convenient, yet easy to have out of your way quickly. 

Remodel: It's beautiful- they have done an exceptional job, modern fixtures, large rooms, huge bath tubes and the cleaning staff leave the rooms absolutely spotless.

findings.title: Adam B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: So depressing.  I raved about this hotel my entire life.  Stayed many times. I never thought of voicing my opinion until staying at the Westin Riverwalk in San Antonio this weekend. This Westin hotel is the beauty and class that the Phoenician once was, before it was remodeled into a millennial catering 'hot spot.'  I went there this last November and was horrified to see the destruction.  The elegance was removed and in its place was a horrid interior of Ikea like, typical Scottsdale, millennial 20something D-baggery styling.  The marble fountain, gone.  The elegant fireplace and tapestries replaced with flat panels. The beautiful front desk gone, replaced by kiosks and glamour girls.  Where the elegant Christmas tree once stood, of course a long bar.  It was travesty after travesty.  The elegance is gone and lost forever. Depressing.

findings.title: Greg S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful, picturesque, classy, elegant, as good as it gets.  No more REALLY needs to be said, but I will still mention the immaculately clean guest room, the attentive but never rushed service at the pool and restaurants, the serene and contemplative vibe in the air and the seamless blending of the hotel grounds as a part of Camelback mountain. Frank Lloyd Wright could not have done a better job of combining the landscape with the property.  The renovations, the chandeliers, the ballrooms, the fountain.....it all made me feel like a pampered prince on a royal honeymoon....and the price never once felt exorbitant in the least for the quality received.  This property deserves it's five-star AAA rating and we will return, as well as recommend.

findings.title: Emily W. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This WAS supposed to be a relaxing memorial weekend getaway. I scheduled a room a week and half in advance. Arriving on Saturday and departure was set for Sunday. I paid for the early arrival which was to be at ten in the morning. However, Saturday morning I called and informed the gentleman who answered that we would be arriving around 3:00pm instead of 10:00am. He stated that there would be no problem with us arriving at that time and that the room would be ready for us. We arrived at 3:00 and was told the room was not ready but to give them an hour. I checked at 4:00, still not ready. Went back at 4:45 and was told that it would be another 45 mins. REALLY?? This was gonna be our first visit there. And never could even get our casita. So, last time going there. Waste of time just to see there lobby. Thanks A LOT!!!

findings.title: Jennifer S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful hotel. By far the best place to stay whether you're coming into town or need a staycation. Top notch dining and must try the brunch. Beautiful views of the golf course while dining. The spa is beautiful. Everyone is so respectful and polite. The food is amazing. Morning walks around the resort you'll see bunnies everywhere!!

findings.title: Mary G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Been coming here for years, always the best service, nicest employees, and a great time.
It's a bit pricy, and by that I mean it is super expensive. My family loves to come here, but unfortunately it can only be on special occasion because of the pricing of everything. Beautiful facility, great for taking family photos, Christmas card pictures, wedding pictures, graduation pictures, etc. I would definitely recommend this place... if you are rich. I think you would really like it. Has activities for the entire family! All the pools are at a great temperature, and the slide is warm! Come on down to the Phoenician in Phoenix, Arizona!!

findings.title: Bruce M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Writing this review on my last night of a five day stay at the Phoenician. Great service and accommodations. Comfortable big bedrooms with refurbished bathrooms!! Far walk to the pool but I find it good exercise. Rooms in the upper wings best views are of the gorgeous cactus gardens and Camelback back mountain. Make sure to take out the resort bikes and climb the trail up the hump right behind the hotel. Couldn't have had a better time in Phoenix. Jean George Steakhouse is so chic and the steaks are to die for good!!!

findings.title: Danielle B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Husband stayed here back in February. Someone made an unauthorized charge of nearly $300 at one of the stores inside the hotel and charged it to his room. Apparently from the looks of other reviews, this isn't a new thing. Guests beware-we are still dealing with this months later and it's a pain in the ***. Maybe look into why Dianne, the employee at Accents authorized a charge? This place sucks.

findings.title: Aj K. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Brunch at the Phoenician was great. We ordered the plated $39/person brunch and it was top notch.  

If you don't like something, let them know. They will replace it!

findings.title: a t. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Not worth the money to stay at this place. Overall nice and  clean, resort but not worth the money.
Highlight is that all lower end staff are very friendly and always say hello.
Front end reception, management just listen with a nice smile and don't do anything to fix a problem. It's funny, just because you speak well as a receptionist, and say "I'm sorry" you expect it to be OK with customers.
Luckily I did not have to pay for my stay here.

findings.title: Sue Ann F. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We revisited the Phoenician during Spring Break 2018.  We were disappointed to say the least in how the resort was not up to the standards that we had experienced in the past.   I would like to start off by saying the staff were all polite but feel that many of the issues I am about to mention were not directly related to them but to higher management.   To begin with the redone pool is poorly managed.  There are signs everywhere stating that "No Reserved Seating" is allowed but when we TRIED to find a chair we were repeatedly directed away by pool staff that we could not sit there because they were 'reserved' ???
  The pool was so extremely crowded it was nearly impossible to find a seat EVERYDAY we were there...timing did not matter.  Towels were on chairs the entire day (Probably were kids playing in the pool) and pool staff did not remove them.  Once again, MANAGEMENT does not enforce the do not reserve policy.
The room cleaning was very untimely where we would get service done at 3:45pm everyday.  It was always when we were returning from the pool/activities to get ready for dinner and had to sit on the patio untli they were finished.   Not sure why staff could not mix it up and begin at alternating ends of hallway.
The logistics of the resort was difficult.  Just to access our room you had to take 2 elevators and if you self-parked (For $14/day) you additionally took an escalator.  the only alternative was to walk through valet parking. In addition, the fitness center was a long trudge down the hill and the facility was very small for the size of the resort.
Lastly, there was no mention prior to our arrival of construction and NO GOLF!  Bad Management!!!
Unfortunately, until new management we will not be back to the Phoenician...there are too many beautiful resorts in this town.

findings.title: B B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: i spent easter at this hotel  every year for 28 years. i have watched how this hotel went from a high class hotel to a standard chain hotel. food quality such a disappointment. Low end. As i checked in at the hotel march 30 2018. i was given a king bed room. i showed the hotel manager my reservation that was made by american express 7 months ago that i was paying for 2 queens and a pull out  for my children. she stated they were fully committed, that they could not give us the room we booked. Her name was Emily. She was very nice. She told me that due to the inconvenience she would give us 2 rooms 2 king beds next to each other not joining. for the same price i was booked at. I stated i did not want to pay for 2 rooms , emily stated i would only pay for 1 room. so 1/1 of my family stayed in one room and i staying in the other room with the smaller children.  It was a disaster for easter since the bunny came to one room. I ordered room service at 730pm for dinner i was told it would arrive at 9pm. the food was delivered at 945 pm cold they added their grautity to the bill 25% i believe. anyways i received a letter from emily with chips and water and a free in room movie ticket for the mess up.    THEN I CHECKED OUT!!!   I was charged for 2 rooms, the movie that was suppose to be free. i was told by ryan that this would be taken care of  but wasn't. No one did anything. i was told that amanda the other manager would take care of it. nothing.... as i read other reviews. i read similar reviews  STAY AWAY!

findings.title: Janet T. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I'm sorry that I spent my vacation here.......food quality was very inconsistent, Stay away from the the on-property restaurant, Talavera. Average food, crazy-high prices and just 'ok' service. I booked through our concierge for my husband's birthday but they never even recognized his birthday! 

Now, a bit about a major issue we had onsite. Our neighbors had a full-blown party two nights in a row. Instead of resolving issue, the "manager" told us to pack and that they would move us to room on the other side of the property at nearly 10 pm. How is punishing the guest that follows the rules a solution? As I sit here, in my room, I am listening to the rowdy neighbors and just steaming. I've never seen something handled so poorly by a hotel, and I travel for business all the time. I actually went and begged them to leave the room because the manager onsite couldn't - the guests were regular conference attendees and it was "part of their contract". Why weren't they put in a hospitality suite then? Why were they put next door two people from the East Coast who came here to relax?
The whole situation was just handled so poorly. 

A few positives -- The rooms are getting just a little dated but they are very clean with great views. The tub is amazing! The turn down service in the evenings is wonderful. Overall, housekeeping has been great. Our check-in was swift and offered us everything we needed.

Pool service was lovely and the other main restaurant on the property, Proof was actually quite good with great service. Other than those few points of light, this resort is not worth the money. Do your research before you make this vacation investment. There are so many amazing properties in Scottsdale. Ironically, this one is not up to The Four Seasons standard!

findings.title: Jenn H. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Their service was excellent. The bar was great. The grounds are beautiful. It was so relaxing to sit by the pool and look at Camelback Mountain. The room was spacious and clean. The only issues were that the shower head was coming off the wall and the maid service starts rather early. We were across the hall from their "closet" and were woken up by their noisy carts running into the door. We would stay there again, but request a room away from the cleaning closet.

findings.title: Sherri S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I was so disappointed with the spa as it was highly recommended to me. I just couldn't wait to get there. I made an appointment for Friday, February 23 for the Crowning Touch and Desert Serenity Scrub Wrap massage. I was referred to the spa by my friend who said it was amazing - excellent salt baths, etc. I knew the spa was going through some renovations, however I had no idea that the Spa on 4th was just another hotel hallway. The website lists that there are limited amenities. 

The truth is that there are no amenities- the waiting area is a regular hotel room with a few chairs and lemon water. I had my service in another hotel room which was quite awkward. There were kids running around the hall during my treatment and the lady told me the other side of the hall is actually occupied with guests. My spa gal, Dawn, was amazing and was trying to do the best she could with what she was given, but this is not a "spa experience" as described on the website.

I've been to many spas-some full and some during upgrades. I was very disappointed and tried to talk to someone at the spa. I couldn't reach someone directly and they kept butchering my name even after I pronounced and spelled it. After several phone calls back and forth, I was told that the price reflected the renovation of the spa. That is simply not true - I paid $358 for almost 2 hours of service and nothing else. Now if I had never been to another spa, then maybe I would have understood. However, I've been very lucky to go to many spas and the price I paid at the The Phoenician was actually more than other spas where you can spend all day in the sauna, spa, pool, baths, etc. There was no option at this time. I have paid less than $200 at other spas and have received much more and also spent the entire day at the spa which is worth the money.

I was very disappointed with the lack of regard for my concerns and the high price of a "spa experience" that happened in a hotel room. I do understand the idea of the renovation but it is not communicated clearly about what services they actually offer during the renovation. This was not a spa - it was a service in a room. I paid way too much money for that and do not recommend it.

This is not a great place to be during construction. The loud construction started very early in the morning by 7:00am and it is not resort-like. The price is just too high to deal with those issues.

We did have a great time during the Trapeze activity!!!
Room Tip: Be careful if still renovating - some have terrible views and loud sounds

findings.title: Mike T. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Golf, mountains, pool bar, the perfect time zone away from ohio home away from home. Great staff on hand. Nice tennis courts.

findings.title: Alex F. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Unfortunately, my New Years trip to this resort has turned into a complete nightmare. After requesting that they look into a charge and switch the credit card the stay was billed to, it has now been a full 7 WEEKS and they still haven't been able to make it right. Management refuses to connect me with the actual accounting personnel that handles these transactions, and I've been promised a call back at least 5 times which haven't happened. It's embarrassing that they're not able to take care of a simple transaction, and it's turned what was a somewhat nice stay into a complete headache as I've had to call them at least 15 times and still haven't had the issue resolved.  

The resort itself is mediocre, so the cost and poor management aren't justifiable. For the rate that they charge this type of thing should easily be resolvable, but they've been incompetent the entire time. There's no chance that I would stay here again or recommend it to anyone.

findings.title: Amanda M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Really expensive resort.  So many additional charges per night it was insane.   It came out to nearly $350 per night!

Tried cocktails at multiple bars throughout the property, stick to the basics because the specialty cocktails are terrible.

Food was average, I think the kitchen really enjoys red onions because basically every dish had them.

I had a charge of $65.47 attached to my hotel bill from 11/17/17 for lunch at a restaurant on the property while I was on a plane headed back home that took 3 months to resolve.  Countless phone calls and voicemails left for accounting and no one returned even one of my calls.  How did I fix it you ask?  I had to dispute the charge with my credit card company because The Phoenician didn't feel like refunding me.  They were too busy to return my calls. 

There are better resorts in the area that are not only a better value but provide better service.  The stay, food and beverage and the grounds were just ok.

findings.title: Aunt M. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I want to startby saying this is one of my favorite hotels of all time and I will always love The Phoenician 

However...I booked this treatment online awhile back and didn't know the real spa was under construction during my visit.

Don't book anything at the "spa" here until construction is finished. I had a great service but ZERO amenities until the real spa opens back up for business. For now it is basically tables set up in guest rooms. Bizarre.

I was hoping at they would at least offer a discount on a service once the renovations are complete, especially knowing I am a local and would come back...

findings.title: Stephanie D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Friend was in town visiting the Phoenician for 1st time, I'm a local who was definitely looking forward to seeing it since remodel. From arrival at front entrance until check out customer service on every level was 5 star & the resort looks amazing! Dinner at J&G Steakhouse was delish & our server there was very knowledgeable. Knowing I was celebrating a Birthday not only did they personally write me a card but followed dinner w dessert & candle. I travel often, do many staycations & The Phoenician was by far one of the best experiences Ive had. Thank you to all the staff for going above & beyond in every way. Will be back soon & definitely referring all my out of town guests to stay there!

findings.title: L. M. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
As I approach my 68th birthday, I want to do something special.  Last February I asked 6 of my closest female family and friends to have High Tea with me at The Phoenician.  I have gone to High Tea at the former Inn On The Park  (now Four Seasons at Park Lane), a 5-star hotel in London, so I thought we would have a great time. Unfortunately, it was definitely not a 5-star experience.  Upon being seated, my daughter told the hostess that it was my birthday and we would ALL be having the Full Tea (without alcohol since our party included 2 nursing mothers) and that she would be paying.  When the waitress came to take our order, she completely ignored me sitting at the head of the table and went to my friend sitting on my right at the END.  My friend asked if she could have a glass of champagne which she would pay for. Two others in the party also wanted champagne. I attempted to tell the waitress to give them the Royal Tea which included champagne for an additional $11.  She seemed not to understand what I was asking so we asked for a manager.  We sat for 15 minutes with no service at all while parties seated after us had their teas.  Finally, we got the attention of another waitress who sent a THIRD server to our table.  We repeated what we had already told the first waitress. Finally our service began. The teas were excellent but the selection of scones and desserts were merely average.  I still had a good time as I was among friends and family.  Then the check came!  It wasn't given to me or my daughter seated at my right. She took it to my friend at the end of the table.  My daughter tried to tell the waitress that she was paying. But the waitress ignored her.  My friend who offered to pay for the champagne noticed that we were being charged over $200 for champagne by the glass rather than as part of fixed price Full Tea.  Again, my friend asked for a manager. Again, no one came.  So we just paid the bill.  It was incredibly humiliating for me since my birthday should have received more care and attention.  While other tables were singing "Happy Birthday" to their special person, we were trying to get our bill explained.  It was a disaster! 

What was particularly disturbing is that my daughter and I were the only black people in the room. We were consistently ignored and overlooked in favor of our own white guests.  It was though The Phoenician felt that a black person could not be able to pay.  I was the only person sitting at the head of the table, flanked on both sides by my 6 guests. Yet, the requests made by both me and my daughter were completely ignored.  

As much as I would like to make High Tea at The Phoenician an annual event for my birthday, I am sad to say that I never want to go through that kind of treatment again.

ADDITIONAL INFO:
In spite of a less than stellar birthday High Tea in February 2017, I went back for a 2-day "stay-cation" in June 2017 with a friend.  The Phoenician was in the middle of renovations so my room rate was about $150 per night with a $25 a day "Resort Fee".  I don't know what the fee was for since I had my own WiFi and don't play golf.  However we could have used the complimentary golf cart for the 1/2 mile trek to our room.  The distance was daunting enough but there were no signs to help us find the right building.  Even the numerous staff members along the way had no idea which elevators were operable or which corridors had not been closed up.  The room just ordinary. Nothing was special or inviting about our stay.  I've stayed in 5-star hotels around the world and The Phoenician is just a big Holiday Inn.  The area around the ice machine was filthy (see photo).  Dinner at J&G Steakhouse was the only high point. The service was outstanding and the food delicious. However, when served coffee at the end of our meal, the creamer was dirty with coffee droplets on the outside (see photo).

There was nothing "luxurious" about our stay. The staff was polite but not at all inviting. Other 5-star hotels that I've stayed at made me feel welcomed and special.  We didn't even get a housekeeping visit during out two nights.  I had to go out in the hall and track down a housekeeping cart for clean towels and water glasses!  No turndown service.  Definitely not a luxury experience.  The Phoenician is just an old "Faded Lady" with mediocre service. I would have been really pissed if I had paid full price (about $500+).

findings.title: Shawn R. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This place used to be nice and presentable but not any more, save your money and go somewhere else.  We stopped by after dinner at old town as we have done many times in the past and upon arriving in the lobby balcony, i was shocked of lack of service, there was no one to take your order.  i went inside and asked if there are any servers and then a gentleman came out and asked if we wanted something, i asked for dessert menu and he said that they only have churros.  I was shocked, they used to have a very nice dessert menu and when i asked if they have changed he said yes, and then he said "he might be able to get us some cheesecake"  but there is no dessert menu.  We decided to go somewhere else for dessert but parking cost $6 for less than 25 minutes of parking.  So disappointing and tacky for once a classy place.  If we used to go to Phoenician, it has changed and not for the better, save your time and money for something worthy of it.

findings.title: Mona A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We stayed here for Christmas weekend. It was SO Lovely. The decor was very classy and festive and the staff was so sweet. They gave our kids little toys to play with which was a sweet touch. The wait staff and the room staff are so nice as well. It really felt like a luxurious experience which is what we wanted. The room service was tasty and plentiful. We ate at restaurants around town, not in the resort. I'd recommend it for a family for sure.

findings.title: Jace M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Checked in right now to this ..... and water keeps coming out.  Called downstairs they said they were sending someone up - it's been an hour hasn't happened......
Shocked 
This is not 5 star
Very disappointed

findings.title: Caprimash F. (4/5)
findings.snippet: A wonderful experience and great service.  The staff was extremely friendly.  The views were stunning and great place to spend the evening with friends and family.

findings.title: B C. (1/5)
findings.snippet: My family and I always attend the Phoenician for The Christmas Day Buffet. We scheduled our table for noon, when we showed up there was no buffet. No one made us aware that the buffet was no longer available. We showed up an had a meal that was sub-par. I wish whoever took our reservations would of let us know they did not offer the buffet any longer. My family and I will never attend the Phonecian again unless they offer the buffet. Good day sir.

findings.title: Shelley C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We have been going to Santa's Breakfast for years, unfortunately this year will be our last. Each year Santa's Breakfast is magical and my children rave about the treats and how amazing it is. From the hot coco, Santa hat shaped pancakes, to the endless amazing desserts- it has exceeded our expectations. This year the cost was the same and the brunch was a plain, simple, far from magical and something you would find at a sub-par resort simply accompanied by a ticket to see Santa.  Next to Santa was a cookie decorating station that wasn't anything but some cookies and frosting with a few toppings. 

In addition to the less than magical experience, we were put at a table where I was in a walkway and constantly hit by people who walked by.  

The most disappointing thing to me was I expressed to the reservation attendant that we had been to Santa's breakfast in prior years and she failed to mention that this year was going to be different. Being honest about the changes would have allowed me to evaluate the value of paying $400 to see Santa.

findings.title: R J. (1/5)
findings.snippet: We are so disappointed in this resort.  Attended a wedding there in October. They overcharged us the porter and housekeeping charges which we were told were being picked up by the wedding party.  I called the same day, spoke to Jordon, and was told we would hear back in 1-3 days.  That was on 10/25/17.  Over a month.  Very bad customer service.

findings.title: Jan S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
The restaurant called Mowry and Cotton in the Phoenician was a big disappointment. Although there weren't many customers in the restaurant, the meal took forever to arrive. The food was poor with small portions.  
The waiter apologized twice for the long wait but did not offer an appetizer while waiting. Two of the four of us complained about the food quality. 
The waiter offered us one free dessert which we declined. Then he asked us to write some nice comments in the restaurant journal. Really?  
We had appetizers in the lounge upstairs beforehand which was lovely. Then we went downstairs to the restaurant for dinner. It wasn't worth it.

findings.title: K B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My husband brought me  J & G  to celebrate my birthday! They had Dover sole, I haven't had Dover sole since we lived in Michigan! We started with the  cold lobster appetizer (yum!) , then we had  the mushroom soup, it was delish, but different than most since it has ginger. We had the house salads, followed by the Dover sole, gratin potatoes and caramelized Brussels sprouts, all superb. They presented me with a wonderful little chocolate cake which oozed chocolate as you cut into it, a great ending to a wonderful meal! It was a great birthday!
We will be back, they had a really great menu, that we will try to work through!

findings.title: Pam S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed during their 100million dollar renovation, and customer service and hotel is still spot on! Rooms are completely remodeled and beautiful. The staff is what stands out the most. Attentive, friendly, personal, and goes above and beyond your expectations. They know the art of hospitality here. Also can't forget to mention, the food here is outstanding. Loved the market cafe for snacks, gelato, coffee, desserts, breakfast. In house chef is incredible!! Must stay in Scottsdale

findings.title: J W. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
The Phoenician isn't anything extraordinary. We were hoping for more of a five star experience, but the Phoenician would have a lot of work to do to get there. 
We knew this resort was going through a remodel and the pools were closed, so that didn't bother us. We just wanted a quiet, luxurious place to sleep. 
The rooms were new, but we could already tell that they needed maintenance in the showers. Grout and caulking needed to be fixed. Beds were comfortable, but the pillows were very flat. 
The first issue was how far we had to walk to get to our room. We were on the 6th floor, and it took two different elevators to get there. Our room felt like it was so far away from the lobby. We dreaded taking our luggage to and from our room. 
The biggest issue was housekeeping. They didn't come to our room. At all. We let the front desk know they didn't come the first day, and that was fine. However, they also didn't come the second day. We had to call the front desk and request more keurig cups and towels be delivered to our room both nights. Ridiculous. 
We expected more from the Phoenician. Hopefully they'll get it together when their renovation is complete.

findings.title: Susan F. (1/5)
findings.snippet: First of all, they have no coffee maker in the room.  Even the cheapest hotel that we stayed at had a coffee maker in the room.  If you want coffee you have to walk to the lobby which for us was a quarter-mile walk.  This place is so so big that it is easily half a mile to the pool, or to find somewhere to eat.  Although the room is very pretty, and the beds are comfortable, they get one star from me until they get coffee makers in the room.  Also, we asked for the Mountain View and were told we could have that. But on arrival they put us in a room facing the roof of another building.  When I brought that to their attention, they did not compensate us or try to resolve it.

findings.title: John S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Construction dumpster noise begins at 4:45am during the week. Front desk says that is when the new crew begins. Do not stay here.

findings.title: Kendra M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My husband and I stayed at The Phoenician a few weeks ago and I am very happy with the experience.
 
Yes, they are undergoing a HUGE remodel, so yes there will be noise/dust/etc. but it still felt like a 5 star resort even during the construction. People just need to understand it's a renovation and you are going to get noise and dust, and other things, but they are doing their best to make it as comfortable as possible. 

The staff was top-notch, seriously everyone was amazing!!! Housekeeping, front desk, bellmen, etc. we didn't encounter anyone that didn't seem like they thoroughly enjoyed their jobs.

The pool-- of course it isn't the new one that they're currently renovating, but the one they have by the tennis courts is still very nice. It's a short walk from the hotel. The pool attendants were phenomenal! I wish I could have gotten everyone's names that worked by the pool while we were there because they were THAT amazing, but I only got the names of Silvia, Shane, and Heather and they were all so incredibly nice and helpful. 

Their room service delivery food was d-e-l-i-c-i-o-u-s! 

We will hopefully stay with the Phoenician again someday, as the experience was so good.

findings.title: Scott D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I was here for about a week and a half and loved every minute of it. I'll definitely be back and I highly recommend it to anybody else

findings.title: Tara B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I love the Phoenician! I have stayed here several times over the years for anniversaries, staycations with the kids, girl's weekends, dinner, happy hours, spa days......you name it. Here is what I love about this place, and I cannot wait to see the new remodel! The staff is friendly and very accommodating. The property is vast, and gorgeous, with so many options for the family to enjoy, and it can accommodate many people without feeling overly crowded. The price maintains a certain level of class without being ostentatious or uncomfortable or completely unaffordable. The spa is lovely, serene and relaxing with quality, knowledgeable estheticians. The restaurants, shops and café provide something for everyone! My husband and I attended a complimentary bourbon an tequila tasting during our anniversary one year, and we discovered that we DO like tequila and bourbon after all!  The fireworks during the fourth of July are amazing from your own private patio and the activities for the children are a blast! You can take a nature walk, play a round of golf, soak in a different pool every day, walk endless paths throughout the lush gardens or listen to live music in the foyer while sipping on a cocktail and looking out at the skyline from Camelback Mountain. This is a truly wonderful place!!

findings.title: Holly M. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I had booked a room with a view of the golf course at the Canyon Suites for a special occasion and I was informed four days prior to my arrival that my reservation could not be honored due to renovations. I was told there were accommodations at the main hotel where I asked for a suite. Upon my arrival I found that I not only did not have a suite but I had a view of a rock. I watched construction from the table at one of the restaurants where I ate my overpriced breakfast and was given awful service. My guest and I had friends who reserved rooms especially for our occasion at this hotel and were equally disappointed. We decided to spend a day at the pool and on our way down the elevator abruptly dropped and the doors failed to open. We spent approximately 30 minutes stuck in the elevator while I placed two calls to the front desk for updates. I reviewed the call times. The only positive in that situation was Taylor, the front desk attendant who answered my call, who kept me in a calm state as I suffer from severe anxiety and claustrophobia. After all of this I have to say it was the worst experience I have ever had on a vacation. I travel often and I am an American Express Platinum cardholder, an SPG Gold Preferred Guest, and a Marriott Silver Member to name only what memberships I have that applies to this hotel. Words cannot express the disappointment I had in this hotel or the experience there.

findings.title: Jourdan P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: If you only take away one thing from this review, please heed my warning: DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY HERE. The resort is currently undergoing a renovation and offering $79 spa services. My friends and I (locals) decided to take advantage of this and book some services - hoping to make a day out of it. We knew there were renovations going on, but the web site makes it sound as if the spa has simply relocated. There is nothing on the site when booking the spa service that says for $79 you literally only get the service (no bathroom, no shower, none of the regular spa amenities such as sauna, etc, and no access to a pool).  In fact, the confirmation email they send out invites you to arrive early and "enjoy their amenities." So, being 8 months pregnant and living in Phoenix, that's exactly what I did. I arrived 2 hours early (as is acceptable with every other resort spa I've been to) to relax in the pool before my massage. After walking through what felt like a very long maze to finally find the relocated spa, I exited a small elevator and walked into a room that felt like I was still outside (except with humidity!). There was a man with a pony tail sitting at a small desk with a floor fan on him. I literally felt like I had walked into someone's makeshift office.  Furthermore, the AC was either broken or not working well, which is miserable when you're hugely pregnant and trying to find ways to feel comfortable in this heat! I asked the man at the desk if the AC was out in the whole facility and he said "Oh no, you'll be in one of the treatment rooms and it will be relaxing."  He clearly didn't see that I was drenched in sweat and out of breath from waddling around with a human inside of me and that my definition of "relaxing" included ice-cold air conditioning. He then said that since I had arrived 2 hours early, the only place for me to wait was in a waiting room (which just looked like two chairs set up in that hot room). I told him I wanted to use a pool and he said there was no pool for me to use. He then went on to let me know (in a manner that truly felt like he was shaming me) that the reason I had gotten such a great deal was because I was only paying for the service. As a side note, does this guy not realize that every resort in Phoenix gives great rates over the summer because the majority of their summer business comes from locals?!?! And in fact, I had just paid $90 - only $10 more! - a week prior for a 60-min massage at Valley Ho that came with full use of the spa and resort pool, a glass of champagne (which I unfortunately couldn't drink), and two additional day passes for use of their pool!!  I digress. Annnyways, I told him I knew they had at least one pool on the property open and he told me that was only for guests staying at the hotel. I had seen rates advertised for $119 and asked him about that (because at this point I was literally considering just paying for a room so I could use the pool - I was THAT uncomfortable). He told me that I still wouldn't be able to use that pool. At that point, I asked if I could cancel the service. He told me since they hadn't made it clear that the rate only included the treatment, he would let me cancel.  I stepped down the hall to confirm with my friends that we should cancel and a few minutes later went back to cancel. I gave him the names of the two friends whose appointments I also wanted to cancel, and he said he had cancelled all 3 appointments.  One of my friends headed over to the Montelucia spa and was able to book us all appointments for that same day for a discounted rate of $135. Their AC worked, they had a private pool for spa guests and their amenities were absolutely beautiful.  Furthermore, they immediately offered me water and everyone we encountered was extremely kind and accommodating. I was more than happy to pay the $55 more than what we would have paid at the Phoenician. So, I thought this would be the end of my terrible Phoenician experience..until the next day. The Phoenician had charged both of my friends a $40 cancellation fee (even though the guy said he was waiving the fee since they hadn't made things clear). When my friend called in to ask about the fee, the woman (a manager, supposedly) proceeded to LIE to her! She said that I had never mentioned cancelling my friends' appointments (lie), that she was standing there when I cancelled (second lie), that the AC had been working fine (3rd lie - I had actually heard a female employee talking about the AC not working), and that the only reason they didn't charge me a fee is because they found someone to take my appointment (4th lie!). She then went on to shame my friend some more and tell her she should feel bad that the spa employee didn't get paid because of her. Wow, just wow. No, Phoenician... you should feel ashamed. As an Arizona native, I used to love you, but I will not be back. There are too many other resorts in the Valley that still know what customer service is.

findings.title: Belinda B. (2/5)
findings.snippet: We had a very nice room, I can't deny this. However, every time they could sneak a charge in, they did. We had prepaid our room on points, but they still tried to stick us with extra fees. When I argued, they agreed the fees were already pre-paid with the points. At the restaurant we were over charged repeatedly and I have had to correct them several times.  They told me they were crediting me. But only emailed the larger bill to me. The fight goes on to keep this charge honest. It's a very nice hotel, but you need to keep your eyes open.

findings.title: Maureen G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Afternoon tea at the Phoenician:

I have been enjoying afternoon tea at the Phoenician for 20 years with friends. Sad when we arrived today that without notice to us when we made the reservation they had moved tea location to the golf course while doing remodeling, needless to say NOT the same experience!  But even more distressing, and again without notice when we made our reservation, they changed from free flowing champagne option to a 1 glass option - needless to say nowhere near the same experience . ONLY reason for 5 stars today is Wanda who is wonderful but trust me next visit, if there is one , might be a 2 or 3 at best. Please get your act together!

findings.title: Tom T. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Major remodel happening , they emailed me and let me know about it but not that all pools were down except the one by the tennis courts. It was an average set-up. The attendant was awesome , she set up our chairs and kept ice water coming. They had pool service but that was below average for the waitress  served us drinks and disappeared when we were read to close our tab. We waited about 20 minutes and another attendant helped us as we waved her over. 
Our room was nice but they placed us all the way to the back. Felt as if we were a mile from check in. The turn down service was nice, and the valet guys up front were super nice. They seemed to have several standing around waiting but it would of been nice to get shuttled on golf carts to and from parking, we chose not to valet $29.00 a day seemed excessive. Wifi was $12.99 a day up to 5 smart devices per room. It was very quiet due to being so far away.
This has the potential to be super nice, but I'd wait until the remodel is complete to get the best of the facility , I stayed at Fire-sky now "The Scott" last sept, and it was small as boutique. I'd recommend that stay for anyone until the remodel is complete.it wasn't awful, nor was it Great to our expectation. We never ain't there because the reviews weren't good, we didn't see bar or food close and our room service for 3 was $207 and not worth the price.

findings.title: Jessica N. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Absolutely love this resort. Impeccable service. The best wellness center. Great tennis pros. The staff is very warm friendly with the kids. We stay here every year before my birthday and always have a wonderful time!

findings.title: Holly R. (3/5)
findings.snippet: I was excited to come here because all the reviews were high and it seemed like a nice resort. I was actually a little surprised when we pulled up and I saw the hotel buildings. They were very outdated looking and the pool food was just that-pool food. We ordered the chicken 'wrap' which was actually just a pita that couldn't hold the contents of food inside and ended up falling apart. The burger my husband got was literally raw on the inside and they said it was medium rare -wrong. It just didn't feel like an upscale resort like I'd expect in paradise valley at this price point.

findings.title: Matt M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Ugh.  Stayed at hotel upon recommendation.  
Given a room next to idling valet car park.  Couldn't enjoy balcony at all.  Asked to move - told no.
Jean George food was amazing, service started out great but ended veeerrryyy slowly.
One day (3 night stay) we left our room a little late, were gone for hours, came back to unserviced room- at 3:45 pm!  As we were preparing for dinner, knock knock to service our room.  Ended up not EVER getting serviced.  I've never had that happen.  
Will stay somewhere else next time to Phoenix.

findings.title: Angela D. (1/5)
findings.snippet: The service is poor all around. We tried to have dinner at "the terrazzo" on Saturday night: the dining room was empty and so was the patio dining area and they would not give us a table because we had no reservations and the hostess claimed the restaurant was full... we finally got a table because the bar tender felt bad for us and intervened and the restaurant remained empty through he entire time we were dining there. The only reason we stayed was because our daughter wanted to watch the night movie by the pool, otherwise we would never have stayed. Are resort guests dining in the resort an afterthought?

findings.title: Jamie B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: We checked out of the Phoenician yesterday, 2 days early. The room was a dump for $750 a night and the so called mountain view was a tree and parking lot. We just moved to Hilton Garden Inn, closer to Old Town and only 170 a night. We just ran into a lady in the lobby who was a travel agent, and we told her our story...well, she had just left the Phoenician after one night and she said she would NEVER recommend it to anyone. She agreed it was a dump and told us it was because ownership changed a year ago and it has gone downhill.

findings.title: Marian L. (4/5)
findings.snippet: The grounds are beautiful & the staff is friendly. That said, there are some fundamental problems with the hotel. For a "luxury" experience, they nickel and dime you to death. We sent a small box ahead of us to their Fedex location, which is on the ground floor of hotel -- just a small box with extra bathing suits  and hiking boots (8 lbs). The box arrived the day we arrived. The hotel charges $15 to release the box to you-- its their handling fee. Or you can pay $25 to have box sent to room! We wanted contents of mini-bar removed from our 2 teenagers room--the Phoenician charges  $50 for this service. We have a rental car and the hotel  charges $14/day to self-park. And this list goes on and on!

findings.title: Kimberly S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Very mediocre property. Went for a last minute weekend getaway. Our casita was average at best. We had a view of the parking lot. The whole property is uninspiring. It's very crowded and pedestrian. Does not have an air of exclusivity at all.  Perhaps this is at least partially attributable to it being the busy season. However, the pool was so crowded that it did not appear inviting. It feels more like a Marriott to me. Lots of families and kids there, which is nice, but not what I had in mind for a spa/resort getaway weekend. 

The concierges were nice, as were the valets. The food at the Jean Georges restaurant was lovely.

findings.title: Lauren S. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful resort! Great accommodations and service , especially in Canyon Suites. Food not up to par and if you want a chair at the main pool you have to get there at the crack of dawn as everyone puts there stuff on the chairs to reserve them super early! We went to pool several times at 9 am to find every single chair was taken -- yet there were very few guests actually present. Bad policy and very frustrating to spend $1500 for a suite and not be able to get a seat!

findings.title: Frankie E. (3/5)
findings.snippet: This place use to have excellent service.  Now it is sad but not enough help and management seems in transition.   I hope this improves -- I love this place.

findings.title: JustIn T. (2/5)
findings.snippet: After staying there in at least 7-8 past occasions, Super POOR service during recent stay there. It took over 45 minutes to even get someone to answer a phone in housekeeping or at the front desk! Absolutely depending on their location and amenities - the staff is neutral, at best. They are not there to serve the customer or to please by asking if they can help. Would never recommend this place - especially at the price point. There are much nicer places and with great service at this price point.  Disappointed.

findings.title: Tracy B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Outstanding food!   Great staff! Excellent night out for dining, we will continue to recommend to all our family and friends.

findings.title: Julie B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This review is based solely on trying to book a spa appointment today. After 35 minutes, two online attempts where I created a login and two phone calls, I gave up! When I called I got an automated system telling me to please wait, which I did, it offered to press 1 to leave a call back number which I did, but then it would just say "please keep holding for the next available agent" and never prompting me for my phone number or anything. I waited and waited. Then it prompted me to leave a voicemail which I also did but the machine cut me off during the message. I called back and waited again and finally decided if it's this difficult to get through, I don't want to spend $240 for a massage that is this difficult to schedule. Please, just have a live person answer the phone. I'm in my 30's so it's not like I couldn't use the technology. I come to Scottsdale every winter and this is just not acceptable at this caliber resort.

findings.title: Kirin K. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I have stayed at this resort a lot of times. The rooms are fabulous and pools are fabulous. The restaurants like the steak house will not disappoint with the delicious food and gorgeous sunset views in evening!

findings.title: R A. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Definitely a nice place to stay when visiting Arizona, especially if you enjoy swimming, tennis & golf.  Lots of great activities without having to leave the resort.  Very comfortable bed and clean room. Lovely view of Camelback mountain.  Service was excellent- housekeeping and valet were awesome.  Food is a bit overpriced, but afterall, it is a resort in the desert.

findings.title: Tanya P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The Phoenician is possibly my favorite hotel. The newly renovated area makes this hotel more lavish, but expensive. The pool was my favorite place to spend our time, as well as the very good steak restaurant looking over all of Phoenix. My kiddos enjoyed the tennis courts and the water slide and I felt more at peace knowing they were being supervised by the staff. Overall, very great and very new but very expensive.

findings.title: Claudia C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: First time at The Phoenician for tea and was it ever special! Live piano, great views of the skyline from the tea seating area, great sandwiches and desserts (accommodating a no-soy requirement) and the best service provided by Wanda! Couldn't have asked for a better experience. All the selections are fresh, and you can have as many as you can stand. The scones were light as air. And did I mention the tea? Good selection - I had the golden tipped Himalayan Darjeeling - what a great choice, and my friend enjoyed the white tea orange spice. This is a must do when you're in the valley. Come hungry, you won't regret it.

findings.title: Regina D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We stayed here for 4th of July and was so happy with service and our room and it was just a lot of fun. We had a room to view firework show for the kids and the lazy river was nice to relax in after chasing around 5 kids. We also enjoyed Relish do Delish!!! And service was top notch! Definitely returning with family!! We had a great time!!! 
I love to come just my fiancé and I (no kids) to do golf.

findings.title: Bad B. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful resort with outstanding food and services. I am not comfortable however with the billing department. I found issues with the bills I received and although they corrected them per my request, a classy outfit as the Phoenician should have been more careful and transparent.

findings.title: Larry C. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I left the Phoenician a "5.0 star rating" back on 3/28/2007 - Today, I rate it a-OK. Yes, a drop from five stars down to 4 is huge when you actually go from seven (7) stars to "3.5". The good, the bad and the UGLY are here:

Don't. Believe. The. Five. Diamonds. 

Remember in Oceans 11 where the gangster, Andy Garcia, would do ANYTHING for a 'Five Diamonds'?!? Well, I do not know who blew whom..., but this resort is far from tantalyzing luxury that I once knew in 2007. It is as-if they are just resting on that AAA accomodation. Hey, I know food trucks and hole-in-the-wall dumpling shops that got a Michelin star. True story: "Don't believe the Five Diamonds."

Reason #2 of 6 why its ONE STAR: The Sunday Buffet is just 20-some bucks.

I am all for a happy hour burger deal or a $5 poolside mocktail promo. But, Sunday is sacrosanct! We had to dine with stuff the cat dragged in. Picture 50 yo bald dudes in balck clubbing gear. And a leather hat. Either it was a nightclub promoters convention in town..., or the price point of 20-something is just too low.

Also, there was a creepy dude with an eagle or a hawk. He seemed to be like a Santa-Monica-beach-child-molester-who-uses-a-parrot to touch kids. EXCEPT IT WAS AN EFFEN HAWK. Whether he worked for the Starwood Hotel Group, I dunno

REASON #3 of 6 why its ONE STAR: 

Play the game I call, "Where was the last SPG property X Phoenician employee, worked at." I ask you to play this because when basic hosting skills break down... I think

- You, the cruddy employee, worked at a Four Points
- You, the bad host, worked at en effen Marriott bushwood in upstate New York

Host staff seems to be recycled losers from Hotel Emergency. Always bracing for impact. Never empowered to make it right. My guess is that the hotel GM came strait from accounting because he turned around a S. American luxury collection hotel and now is here to make it rain TVPI, IRR and Internal Rate of Return. Hint: "Business models don't import well."

Reason #4 why its ONE STAR: 

There used to be rising talent employed all over the hotel. Some bright eyed, bushy tailed front desk host that just graduated from NAU (Northern Arizona U has a great hotel restaurant mgmnt program). This fluffy worker would be hesitant, inexperienced, but fresh new and energetic and helpful. And nice. Not jaded.

I met a lot of front desk staff that seemed pretty belligerent about sticking to their 2pm late checkout even though 4pm for a Platinum SPG is pretty standard, especially if you did not upgrade me to a big boy suite.

Reason #5 why its ONE STAR away from a good review:

Fellow SPG platinum had this to say over at PreferredGuest dot com

My family and I have flown to Phoenix four times solely for the purpose of visiting this hotel. I can't believe I'm about to give it only a four-star review, but here I am, and this will probably be my last visit here for a while"

Reason #6 why its ONE STAR

My goodness, What Chinese Fire Drill Is This?!!? How many Chinese smokers can cram around the ash tray in front of the Ice Cream Shoppe. The second hand SMOKEY air blows right into the shoppe that doubles as a decent coffee joynt in the morning. 

What is worse is that i am Chinese and it just feels like white people do not stay at this hotel. It is SO ASIAN! Ni hao ma, not-so-much. And please move the smoking lounge so that the front lobby is not looking into Chinatown, #ScottsdaleEdition. Correct me if I am wrong, but does anyone remember the high school smoking lounge and the dorks huddled around sucking those dumb cancer sticks!?

No one except Andy Garcia's casino pit bosses wants to see Gucci fanny packs protruding from skinny cigarette smoking, Asian smokers. No one!

findings.title: Ashley W. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This place needs better customer service. I left 3 voicemails trying to make a dinner reservation. Nobody ever got back to me, and by the time I called three different numbers and then transferred and on hold for over 20 minutes  ( the number on google maps is incorrect for the restaurant)  I was connected to the restaurant, which was already fully committed. They didn't do anything to help me, only offer me the last seating aka the cold food. Big big disappointment.

findings.title: Payton K. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Had a great time. It was a very memorable experience. It was highly overpriced and I would prefer some different resorts. The experience is amazing. The dining and pool is a great contribution to the hotel

findings.title: Leanne W. (4/5)
findings.snippet: We arrived at the hotel today. While waiting to check in, we went over to the Concierge desk to ask about reservations for dinner tonight and for NYE. We were fortunate enough to work with Dawn Banks. She is amazing. NYE was only 2 days away so it wasn't an easy task for her to find us a great restaurant between 8pm and 9pm. After a few phone calls she was able to secure a reservation at a great restaurant. Dawn was so accommodating and extremely pleasant to work with!  The only complaint I have is that the gym needs to have more cardio equipment. I went to go work out in the morning and there was no cardio equipment available and a line of 5 people waiting for one. Frustrating.... but ended up having a good walk outside.

findings.title: Jam A. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Been coming here for 18 years to relax patio side for lunch.   Always soothing from the hustle of the rest of the city

findings.title: Larry C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Started with a drink at the bar. Bourbon selection is adequate but extremely high priced. Expect to pay about half of the bottle cost for a drink. Ate a filet for dinner cooked just right but a little bland. Glad they served it samples of their sauces. The restaurant is decorated nicely and the atmosphere is good as is the service.

findings.title: Jim N. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
This hotel charges Ritz Carlton prices, which is fine, but fails to deliver service at anywhere near the level.  I don't mind paying good money for a nice hotel.  I also don't mind spending the occasional night away from home in a Days Inn.  This place was a lot closer to a Days Inn.

The carpet by the bathroom was pulling up and there was a half inch gap between the tile and the carpet where the sub-floor showed through.  The window over the bath tup was the dirtiest window I have ever seen (besides the occasional Jeep, but even most Jeeps have cleaner windows) and it overlooked a roof covered in trash.  Two lamps in our room had blue painter's tape on them.  Lastly, our shower had a non-matching tile, complete with contractors' notes scribbled on the tiles around it.

The food in the Italian restaurant is really good and I received great service from Adam at the front desk

findings.title: Todd M. (4/5)
findings.snippet: My wife and I had a wonderful time.  The room was comfortable.  We asked for an upgrade, and ended up in a rear cottage.  The restaurant was nice, and the grounds were fantastic.

findings.title: Kristen T. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My husband and I spent 6 days at the Phoenician on our honeymoon.  We had the best intentions to get out and go do things but we never left the property.  The rooms were beautiful (we spent several nights in the Casitas, and the rest in a 4th floor room overlooking the city), the restaurants are amazing,  the pool and pool service are great.  I can't say enough- if you just need an overnight staycation or a longer get away then the Phoenician is where it is at!

findings.title: Marika C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Wonderful experience!  My husband surprised me with a spa day at their wellness center.  From the 1st person that greeted us to the waitress at Relish and the employees at the pool area, everyone was so very attentive and friendly.  I love that they bring you a pitcher of ice water and cups at the pool even before you ask and they keep refilling.  Outstanding customer service!  The grounds are beautiful, the massage was amazing and the food was fantastic.  We live in the area, but will come back and stay at the hotel and enjoy their amenities again.  I would highly recommend!!

findings.title: Shara C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My husband and I were in town for only one night to attend a wedding. I had heard great things about the Phoenician, so even though it was a bit of a drive to the wedding venue, we booked our stay. I could not have been more pleased. The staff and the customer service were impeccable. The grounds were pristine. The rooms are spacious and well maintained. And surprisingly, the food is also delicious. We went to Relish Burger Bar, had breakfast at Il Terrazo, and even squeezed in a quick dinner at J&G, which was absolutely incredible. My husband and I travel a lot and my standards are pretty high - this place is not at the top of my list. The wonderful thing is it's a super quick trip for us coming from the Bay Area and I plan to come back often.

Oh, I think the reviews about the place being outdated are old - our room was brand-spanking new! 

The only bad thing I have to say is mostly out of the control of the hotel. There seemed to be a lot of guests that were really intoxicated. They asked someone to leave the bar who couldn't stand up or speak on Friday night and there was a very belligerent woman at the pool who was drunk and cursing about politics Saturday afternoon. The hotel staff seemed to address these things, so I'm not sure there's more that can be done.

findings.title: Smooji B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We just stayed this past weekend in a huge, beautiful Casita. It was our birthday weekend. We want to let the managers know how awesome the staff has been. Particularly, Al, our server at our Pink High Tea at the Lobby Court. He made our high tea experience even more awesome. Second person was Rachel Hughes at the front desk. She went above and beyond in helping us with transportation, boarding passes. She went above and beyond. Third, Chris Olsen (hope that's his last name) he is a bellman. He was our golfcart ride to start our Cholla hike. His awesome customer service was appreciated. So, thank you to all your staff. Customer service was on point. We come once or twice a year from California...and will continue to stay at The Phoenician.

findings.title: George Y. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We booked 2 spa services and took full advantage of the amenities. With our spa services we were able to sit by the pool all day and relax before our massage and facial. The spa services were great and the staff was extremely friendly.

The only thing i didn't care for was the price and quality of the food at the pool. For such a high end resort the food was really bad. I we hardly touched the food, and it wasn't cheap.

findings.title: Elsa B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
AWESOME hotel. 
I went here in 2009 (I was 9 years old) with my friends Nancy and Madeliene, and we had a BLAST!!! :)
The Jones Soda (green apple) was AMAZING and I kept ordering more! 
The hotel itself was too loud, and the waterslide kept bumping my hip on the way down, but other than that it was GREAT! :)
The facility itself was in a gated community and had lush landscaping. It was a very nice (but expensive) hotel.

findings.title: Cj B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Third stay...STILL AMAZING. I think they've gotten even nicer. Everyone who works here is so nice and super helpful. They are remodeling the entire hotel (it doesn't seem like they need to because everything is amazing!) and the Business Center was closed so I couldn't figure out how to print some stuff. One of the staff members offered to print it for me from his office if I just emailed him. It was the manager of the Ice Cream yummy bakery thing.

Had an amazing time again, can't wait to see the remodeled rooms!

findings.title: Monica Q. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Really beautiful hotel that is so ridiculously large. It's an interesting hotel in that there are no hallways for the rooms - rather there are outdoor rooms that then open up into the rooms. It's a very common set up in a dry environment. The golf course is also right on the hotel premises so it is super convenient to get to. There are also so many pools - I guess that makes sense given that this place is a resort. The breakfast and food is also quite good here. Happy stay here and I think you will also have one too.

findings.title: Ron V. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
The service is impeccable, so are the grounds, but for a luxury and pricey resort, the rooms are disappointing. In dire need of updating, the furniture is chipped, scratched and gouged. The decor is 1990s at best. Beds are comfy but linens retain a powerful smell of borax. For a place that will tack a charge onto everything (and not a modest charge at all) the Phoenician should but at the forefront of contemporary design and taste. 

The staff however is top notch. Without exception. Next time I travel to Phoenix, I'll likely stay somewhere else--Gainey Ranch perhaps.

findings.title: Lyvier C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My shoe fell apart a minute before I was to meet various business colleagues in the lobby bar for afternoon high tea.  The hostess was wonderful she took my shoe away and the concierge took a hot glue gun and put my shoe back together again.

They were so wonderful and concerned for me. They even offered some slippers so I did not have to be bare footed while they glued my shoe back together.

Thank you ladies!!!!

findings.title: Samantha S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Once you enter the Phoenician entrance you feel as though you booked the right hotel. Unfortunately, it went all down hill from there. We met with the concierge after our check in and they were extremely rude and unhelpful. My mother was upset the entire day because a pool attendant made a degrading comment about her. The rooms are standard - nothing amazing but not bad. The hotel is now under construction. When you're on vacation you want to sleep in peace but they were spraying paint outside our door and making loud noises at 8am. My boyfriend and I went to the spa and were under impressed. The jacuzzi was the same size as the one I have in my backyard. I highly recommend going to the Montelucia spa, which is 10 minutes away. We went there the following day and were blown away by the experience they provided us. There is a groupon for both spas for the same price but you receive two totally different experiences.  I wouldn't recommend staying here for the amount of money you spend. I was trying very hard to be optimistic about our stay here but we were repeatedly disappointed.

findings.title: Jessica H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My new husband and I had our wedding here on July 2nd. The grounds are absolutely beautiful. At sunset the lounge over looks the city and takes your breath away. It was a beautiful sunset on our wedding night. Yes, it is a bit more expensive but worth every cent. The staff are gracious and obviously experienced. We nearly chose Tapitio Cliffs but are delighted that we ended on the Phoenitian!

findings.title: K A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Spectacular! I had an amazing time. The service was top notch, the food was out of this world. Loved the pool

findings.title: Emily W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: So beaitiful! Amazing staff and the rooms are to die for! Worth every penny! Perfect place for a staycation!

findings.title: Tap G. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I'm giving this place 4 stars and will give it 5 if they update the place. The people are very friendly and helpful although the pool service is a bit on the slow side. The staff definitely follows through on the details. The location, views, and grounds are all unbeatable. Although the Phoenician represents itself and does feel like luxury resort, the place is definitely dated. It's very tasteful, elegant, and subdued decor from what I would guess is the 80's or maybe early 90's. Hope they update and hope the service stays as excellent. It would then be a no brainier for us to stay here again.

findings.title: Violet D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Where do I even begin. We stayed for the 4th of July weekend in this gorgeous resort and had the time of our lives. We have traveled near and far and hands down our stay in the Phoenician was one of the best experiences we have had. From the moment we checked into the resort we were treated like royalty. Everyone who we came across greeted us with a massive smile and enthusiasm. We were made to feel appreciated and welcomed. Basically the resort was like a home away from home. The interior decoration is absolutely stunning and screams "luxury" it has a very European feel to it. We stayed at the Canyon Suites and had a beautiful balcony facing the resort entrance and in the back was the most glorious cactus garden I have ever seen. Not to mention we were right next to the Camelback mountain. Just WOW! Breakfast is served from 6:30 am which is wonderful as most places start much later than that. We would start off our days downstairs eating some yummy food, then we would head to the pool area or shall I say "pools" there were so many different pools at the resort it was almost like being in a candy store. We hopped from one to the other. Also they have a fun waterslide which made us feel like kids again and a fun bar for the 21+ folks by the adult pools. In the evenings we enjoyed a glass of wine in their bubbly hot tub ( sooo relaxing). We really wanted to make the most of our time at the resort and booked spa sessions & nails (our masseuses and nail technicians were perfectionists and made us feel like gold after our treatments), tennis court time (which should be booked in advance) and golfed in their drop dead gorgeous golf corse. Everything was unbelievable, the service and care we received made us feel on top of the world. This place is worth every dime. Also we had talented musicians performing by the Thirsty Camel bar in the lobby area where we danced the night away, they have awesome cheese and meat plates, the gin fizz was perfect and so refreshing. Very dreamy!The restaurants on site have the most delicious food. If you're up for burgers and the most mouth watering "pickled pickles" ever go to Relish.
