If you would like a view for miles ahead and fireworks which we experienced then your best bet is to go to JG Steakhouse. The lobster dish is out of this world. The staff are so down to the earth and full of jokes. Jeff was our host on both nights and he is the most genuine guy and a witty sense of humor which we loved!

If you go to this resort make sure to take full advantage of all the things it has to offer. The location is amazing and so close to old Scottsdale which is full of old fashioned bars and restaurants. Really takes you back in time!

Thank you to the Phoenician and their staff for being so wonderful to us! You can really feel the dedication and job each one of you has in being a part of peoples' time spent in the resort. Can't wait to be back and have another adventure!! :)

findings.title: Andrea M. (4/5)
findings.snippet: This is a beautiful resort with impeccable amenities and for the most part all employees were on point.  Had an early flight Saturday morning arranged with the front desk to order a cab I watched as he took diligent notes.  4:30 am no cab the employee working the door tries to force a limo on me.  Walked back to the front desk they had no idea about any cab so she ordered another.  Another guest ordered an uber and invited me to share her car.  Moral of story do t rely on hotel for any mode of transport except a limo.

findings.title: Candy M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Amazing vistas, the Sonoran Desert is breathtaking and right outside my window!  Large, very private balcony with table and chairs along with a chaise lounge allows me to work or lounge while enjoying the view.  Check in was quick and very polite, efficient staff and good food both at the cafe and during the conference I attended.  Clean, spacious rooms and comfy bed, too.  The pool looks great, but I didn't have time to enjoy it;)

findings.title: Jennifer B. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I had towels with BOOGERS and a filthy tub and shower. Things were broken or not working. (See photos!) The view was wonderful and the out dated casita really wasn't too bad but the quality of housekeeping is with a motel 6 that had a nice turndown service. The only reason I gave two stars was for the thoughtful birthday cupcake that was sent and for outstanding service from Rich, our cabana server. 
Went to Relish and had outstanding burgers that better had been good because they took and hour and a half to receive. Unfortunately, the food server spilled our tray and the food had to be remade. We received no apology or accommodations for our starving family while we waited, and waited, and waited! We were celebrating a birthday and even though I made the server aware of this, and considering the mishap, they didn't even comp our $10 dessert. 
We had a wonderful day as we reserved a cabana and hung out by the pool and like I said the service was above and beyond from Rich. Most employees we encountered we very kind and professional. It was a shame that our casita was unpleasant. Although outdated, it was still beautiful. But you can not call such filth 5 star. We will most likely take our money elsewhere (Montelucia & Sanctuary are my suggestions) next time.

findings.title: Phuong N. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
The worst!! The Phoenician added almost 1k in charges on my bill so when I called they apologized and removed them.  A week later I was charged 200 from the spa. I never went to the spa.  I called again. Getting the run around. I had to call 4 times and they still couldn't figure out the charges.  They said they'd call me back after looking into it and  still have not returned me call. I  am livid.

And the hotel is so outdated and old.  Not worth it!

findings.title: James K. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We stay here a few times a year as we live in Phoenix.  All of our stays have been outstanding!  From the quality of our rooms, the great staff at the lobby check-in, the pool staff have been so helpful and friendly.  We think the Phoenician is one of the very best in Arizona.  Keep up the great work.

findings.title: Lauren M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I have been to many resorts came here to celebrate a anniversary and wow is all I got to say it was amazing took me out of Arizona for a bit I felt like I was a celeb! The bath tub was HUGE

findings.title: Mark S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Only problem was I didn't stay long enough! Incredibly friendly staff. Warm greeting. Great room, excellent pools (all three)  just can't say enough. I loved it. Not to mention Scottsdale is a nice area with a great mall and great restaurants close by. Sumo Maya was a great Asian Latin fusion spot. Have fun! We did.

findings.title: Philip V. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Just stayed at the Phoenician Resort this last weekend!  As a realtor from Orange County, I always appreciate my down-time and getting away and trying out different resorts.  It was memorial day weekend and the staff was on their toes.  Very personal, professional and helpful.  Will definitely come back to this resort in the future.  A great 5 Star experience.

findings.title: Lisha S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Made a last minute decision to go for the weekend here at a friend's suggestion. I am very happy we did. Dinner the first night at L&G steakhouse was superb. Breakfast was included every morning with our stay- also great. I had two spa treatments one with Maria , the other with Sara - both were AMAZING! Our room was perfect. The bathroom was huge, the bed was ultra comfortable. Finally the pool was very nice. There were a ton of kids at the resort, but it wasn't overbearing. Staff was extremely attentive Shane and Brian gave excellent service. No complaints at all. I have never been to Arizona, so I had no idea of what to expect. After my experience of the Phoenician, I understand why people come here to retire.

findings.title: Adrian S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Nice resort.
Management do not enforce the Do Not Reserve policy for chairs at the pools... So beware..watch where you sit as they will try and move you on..

findings.title: Victoria S. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Okay, so I'm conflicted with this property. I checked in and was so disappointed upon seeing the room that I left a 1 star review. After a 4 day stay, I'm updating my review to 3 stars. Let me start with the good stuff!

PROS:
-every single person that I interacted with was friendly. I can't rave enough about the employees. The bartenders at the Thirsty Camel were awesome too!

-the grounds are BEAUTIFUL!

-the fitness center is great. The equipment is updated and clean. It does get congested in the morning, so I saved my work outs until after pool time.  At that time, there were never more than 2 other people there. I also enjoyed the tennis courts. Best resort tennis courts that I've used. 

-location is fantastic!  I walked to Scottsdale fashion square every morning. It was about 1.5-2 miles each way.  So close to everything. At night, I took an Uber to the restaurants. 

-the pool attendants = amazing!  Brian was awesome!!  Plus, the skinny mojito drink that I had at the pool was ridiculously good!


CONS:

-fitness center is a pretty decent walk from the main building. They have golf carts that will transport you to/from, but it isn't super convenient. And in the heat of the day, the last thing you feel like doing is leaving the gym while hot and sweaty to walk a distance back to the building with the sun beating on you. 

-the rooms need a major renovation. Very old. The bathrooms are nice, but the room itself is very dated.  The carpet is dingy looking as well as the walls.  The bathroom and view of Camelback were the redeeming room factors. 


Marriott recently purchased the property and will be doing renovations very soon. I will definitely go back to stay after the renovations are completed.

findings.title: Desiree C. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Sunday fun day at the Phoenician pool! I laid by the pool with my boo all day. Very upscale and the scenery or set up was very petty. Umbrellas everywhere by the pool- they set up your towels and water once you find your chairs. Basketball hoop and volleyball is offered at the pool! I think I saw a little kiddie area and a slide. Family friendly area!

Customer service was soooo ridiculously slow. Our server was not attentive at all. I had to ask him for ranch 3 times. I waited 20 plus minutes for him to come back around so we can finally get my check. We asked 2 servers for our check. We usually are patient customers but that was just lame sauce. 

Overall it's a great place for relaxation but I'm not a fan of the customer service there.

findings.title: Tim C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Great for smokers; not so much for nonsmokers.  Their policy is to allow smoking on room balconies, so each morning we were woken up by smoke coming in to our room from the chain smokers next door.  We also couldn't enjoy using our balcony--a major part of the room experience--and needed to keep our door to the balcony shut--so no way to enjoy fresh air.  Not the way we wanted to enjoy our $600+ casita during spring break.  

The Phoenician is private property and I presume they can make their smoking policy however they like.  I also don't blame smokers for smoking in places where it is allowed.  And we can choose where we wish to stay.  We won't be back.

findings.title: Mary H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: What a property!  A definite must-see if you visit Phoenix.  Beautiful at night for drinks and dinner.  Friendly staff and excellent service all-around.

findings.title: Joe A. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Very impressed with our recent five day stay at the Phoenician.  Terrific facility and staff.  We enjoyed the view from our fourth floor, East wing room with a balcony faced toward the pool complex.  The restaurants and golf course are excellent too.  

Would definitely return again.  This Starwood Platinum is impressed with the Phoenician!

findings.title: Alex R. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Dated, dated, and dated that would be the only way to describe this hotel. I stayed here recently with my girlfriend and we got a room in a casita here and the place was jam packed so we waited for about an hour and a half to get our room keys. Oh and as we were getting the keys they also asked if we wanted to valet for $22.00 a day or SELF PARK for $14.00 a day??? Who charges someone to self park??? I am paying to stay at your "5 star" hotel and am paying you for the privilege of parking my own car???? Well that was the first bad sign of staying in an outdated hotel.

When we get to our room at the casita, there are no parking spots open?? So we have to park next to the curb in a non existent parking spot, at one point scratching the rims on my expensive rental car (thanks again for the $14.00 a day parking fee and not having enough parking spots to park at your casita??

Then we walk up to our room... Yeah the door looked like it was at least 50 years old and the bottom of the door was starting to rot away (see attached pictures). The carpets had stains on them and the balcony had what looked like mini wasp nests on the ceiling. 

And it does not end there, the whole room looks like it was designed in the 70's, complete with furniture that you couldn't get at a garage sale nowadays and the bathroom did not have a vent; or at least not a working vent so if you went to the bathroom you would need to give it some time before anyone else could use it.

Overall I would never stay at this hotel ever again, it was $600.00 a night and then at the end of our stay we also ended up paying an extra $340 some odd dollars for the "self parking fee" and the resort fees..

If you are old and looking to play a couple rounds of golf and are stuck in a time warp go to the Phoenician; otherwise do yourself a favor and stay at The Sanctuary or Omni hotel; as both are in a different class than this place.

findings.title: Frank S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This hotel is truly a suburb experience. It offers complete luxury from the second you pull up to the hotel and to the edge of the award winning golf course. The bartender Kris is very polite and always gets your order right. My most memorable take away from the hotel is interacting with the most kind, respectful and helpful employee Jarrett. Jarrett is truly a class act and is so polite. He runs the slide at the Phoenician resort. Jarrett makes sure the slide is orderly and always enforces the rules. He was truly a delight and I would go back to just see Jarrett and Kris. But Jarrett is really an example of the type of person we thrive to be.

findings.title: Connor S. (3/5)
findings.snippet: The Phoenician is definitely a fun resort with many different options of things to do, but where it exceeds on the big things it lacks on smaller things. For example, the shower in our average size and cost room was leaky and had horrible water pressure. Also, the customer service was bad. They forgot to bring things to the table while still charging us for them, they got orders wrong, and they took forever to do a simple task like get water. Even when we were the only ones in the Restaurant! But, all in all, it is a very pretty place with fun things to do and good food choices.

findings.title: Patrick P. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed at the Phoenician for a week during spring break. The rooms are well kept and clean and the service is phenomenal. The grounds are kept immaculate as well. Great resort for adults that enjoy golf with two golf courses on the premises. While there are signs that state reserving chairs around the pool is not allowed,  it is an absolute must. People start reserving their spots at 7:00 AM so if you don't get down there early enough, you may end up sitting on the lawn. Was disappointed in the lack of planned activities for teenage kids. Most activities are geared for the younger crowd so my 12 year old was a little bored. There is a poorly stocked game room that could user some new games and equipment. Overall a good vacation. We would return.

findings.title: Dwight T. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Absolutely the best high tea I have had. Sure it does not have the quaint little tea house feel, but I enjoyed a relaxed environment with high quality and no snobbery. I like dressing resort casual at the very least for high tea. Natalie was the best for service.

findings.title: Patrick R. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Love this place! I've stayed here a few times for work related events so I'm on the property for extended periods of time. Sometimes as much as two weeks. The property is AMAZING! The pools, the spectacular view of Camelback Mountain, the rooms, great gym, it's all simply stunning. The staff is amazing too. Always helpful, always friendly it's truly impressive. This is not the typical cookie cutter mega-hotel, it's drips of class. 

My favorites were:
- Nice little coffee shop located off the lobby. Perfect for light meals without breaking your budget.  
- The resort is located in close proximity to restaurants, grocery stores, anything you need. 
- The onsite restaurants are spectacular. The burger joint was my favorite :-) 
- The gym is huge, very nice and open 24/7. 
- You can walk to Camelback Mountain for an amazing hike.....for free!  

You will not be disappointed!

findings.title: John L. (1/5)
findings.snippet: My wife and I got engaged in early 2015 and wanted to have our wedding at the Phoenician. We were always frequent customers and had many "staycations" at the resort. We contacted the Phoenician and worked with Gregory Wirth. We set up an appointment time and drove up there on a Friday afternoon. Gregory Wirth started it off by being late. Since we were very excited about having it there we asked him for pricing and he said he is not sure he will send it to us via email. It was surprising to us that he didn't have it prepared since our emails were very detailed and we knew exactly what we wanted. After our meeting we felt very bad about our experience. Gregory Wirth treated us like we were second rate people and didn't treat us like we were used to at the Phoenician HORRIBLE SERVICE. At this point we started looking at different venues. Over the next two weeks he sent us 3 DIFFERENT quotes with grammatical errors and typos. There was also HIDDEN fees and extra charges worked in to the contract that people glancing at the quote wouldn't catch. I reached out to Gregory Wirth and let him know that we wouldn't be using his place as our Venue. We decided on the Arizona Biltmore and had a wonderful and pleasant experience. Please look at the Phoenix Biltmore if you want to have an event or wedding. Better pricing, more history, and MUCH better service.

findings.title: Shelley S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Wow!  This is heaven.

Beautifully decorated inside and out - what more could a girl want? Nine pools that are 24 hours.  I can't tell you how many times I've wanted to take a late night dip and been negated based on the pool hours, not here. 

One note, they have NO WIFI? Apparently some rooms have it, and some don't - mine didn't. 

The staff here go out of their way to be helpful. Very accommodating, very friendly, very available. Can't really ask for more... and I speak of the concierges and what I believe are managers that wander around helping guests.

The cactus garden is really cool. Definitely worth taking a stroll through. Convenient parking.  

The rooms are very nice, turn down service is a nice touch. The hotel is stocked with all the things you'd need for a stay - shampoo and conditioner, q-tips, bath wash, body wash, shower caps, face pads, slippers, bath robe, soaps, mini bar (they even have a wine opener!). If you are coming from outside of AZ, bring your own water. The tap water isn't the best. 

The have a bath tub and a nice walk in shower as well so you can bath how you like. The order in movies are a little pricey, they have flat screens but no DVD players. Room service is over priced, with a 22% gratuity automatically added and a $5 or something charge. 

The good thing is it's in Scottsdale, near a lot of awesome tourist places to go.  I will be back.

findings.title: Bruce H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
High tea at the Phoencian transports you to an afternoon of tranquility at a leisurely pace. Incredible view, lovely live piano music, great food and libations and of course Wanda. She runs the show. We would follow her anywhere and we have been coming here almost 15 years due in no small part to her. 

This tea is not to be missed!!!

findings.title: Herman H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Stayed here for 2 days,the hotel is laid out appropriately ,amenities in rooms well thought out.
Complimentary jug of ice water at the poolside served every 1/2 hour.
Everything is grand.
The steakhouse restaurant,on rooftop,is one of the very best we ever had.
Highly recommend .

findings.title: Lisa R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Love the afternoon - tea at the Phoenician. Great atmosphere and the tea was top notch

findings.title: Erin C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I have never stayed there but I go for tea a few times a year. It's a very special place for my family. They give you finger sandwiches, scones, deserts, and of course tea. It is all delicious. The ladies that work there are amazing, especially Wanda. Treat yourself and go get tea.

findings.title: David Rey S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Stunning GEM in the desert tucked into the east base of Camelback Mountain. Always my go-to hotel when visiting Scottsdale/Paradise Valley - as a Starwood Platinum this is one of my favorite hotels in the country. The accolades are well deserved at this luxury AAA - Five Diamond resort.
 
Throwback to another time when attention to architectural details of the resort layout and physical plant were primary considerations - very unique design. Walking into the lobby, just beyond an opulent marble water fountain, you are met with a stunning view of the East Valley. You will find yourself enjoying views and drinks on the lobby terrace often!
 
Beautiful 27-hole championship golf course (short layout, EXCELLENT condition at all times, real fun to play and convenient - walk right out of your room to the tee box), nine pools (including adult pool) with other unique features including a private art collection of paintings, sculptures, and statues located throughout the hotel, walking trails and cactus gardens.
 
While still in great shape, the property needs a mini-face lift (carpeting, bathrooms, some furnishings). Definitely wear and tear has been observed over my 15 years visiting, along with a drop in the quality of service from front desk to housekeeping. Still great but down a bit from prior years.
 
For a significant step-up - consider staying at the Canyon Suites (upscale option with personal services and suites located on campus). Separate porte co·chère / check-in required.
 
Request a room facing poolside when checking in!

findings.title: Lydia R. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
In deciding where I wanted to go for vacation, relaxation was the number one factor, followed by affordable luxury. As a Platinum SPG Member, the second factor became possible because I was given a gorgeous, expansive suite with lots and lots of privacy. It was really an amazing room and the balcony was as large as many hotel rooms in NYC! 

Along with my room, the entire resort is picturesque. Walking around the hotel and grounds made me want to constantly take pictures... Which I obviously did! They offer golf cart rides to take guests around the resort, but sometimes I really enjoyed walking because it was so beautiful out. While it was a record low temperature during my stay (boo) so I did not attempt to use the pools, there were a number of other activities that I enjoyed at the resort. My favorites, in a list:

1. Afternoon Christmas high tea in the main lobby the first day I arrived 
2. Cactus garden tour right across from the hotel
3. Exploring the pools, koi pond, and grounds surrounding the hotel and resort
4. Restaurants - J&G, Il Terrazzo for breakfast (especially the amazing holiday brunch), and Relish
5. Centre for Well Being and Salon Mila - I felt like a princess; and they constantly keep the spa immaculate
6. Fitness opportunities - the grounds are for golfers; there are tennis courts and an amazing gym with ongoing classes; and challenging hikes closeby (I climbed Camelback and thoroughly enjoyed it)
7. Customer service was amazing throughout my stay with concierge, housekeeping, and front desk all being very helpful and welcoming 

All in all, I highly recommend this resort to anyone looking for a vacation. There is something for everyone here!

findings.title: Darpan P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Amazing setting and views. This hotel is by far one of the best. The courses are amazing. The steakhouse onsite has a great bar, oysters and solid cocktails. Great for weekend away, business or vacation.

findings.title: Paige M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Once each holiday season we take an evening to enjoy the patio at the Phoenician. The decorations are festive, ambiance is warm and embracing, food very good and service excellent.

findings.title: Ed M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I'm not sure how many times I've stayed here, too many to count. This is a fantastic hotel for a couples getaway. Nice pools, golfing, hike to the top of Camelback Mountain just off the property. I come your annually for a conference but I've brought my wife many times and she loves this place.

findings.title: Katherine A. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I have stayed at the Phoenician for work before, and I was excited to come back again - this time for leisure. I brought my girlfriend for a short one night stay this past weekend. I had booked the room online months before for several hundred dollars. At check-in, I was informed that I had been "upgraded" to a different room. However, upon arriving at our "upgraded" casita room, I was shocked by how incredibly small it was - and I was flabbergasted by our "upgraded" view - literally directly into a parking lot. They must have been kidding.
I wondered to myself if perhaps the hotel was at max capacity, so I went online to look. Much to my dismay, I learned that they had many, MANY rooms available for that evening - and that they were going at a rate 75% cheaper than what I had paid. So what gives? As a Starwood Preferred Guest as well as a return customer, and a guest paying well over market price, I would hope (and expect) that I would be given a better room that doesn't look out into a parking garage, especially when they had so many available. But no.
I requested to be moved to a new room in the main hotel with a better view, and the front desk sent over a bellman with the new keys. After a long trek to the new room, which was NOT in fact in the main hotel, and which was actually facing rocks rather than the panoramic view of the pool and mountains, we learned that the door was completely locked from the inside --- the deadbolt had somehow locked itself. What a joke. I then went to a house phone and called the front desk, expecting that they would simply put us into a new room - one with a working door. The person who picked up was not particularly friendly or apologetic, but said that she would send Security up to try to get the lock open. After 15 minutes passed where we stood awkwardly in the hallway with all of our luggage and nobody came, I called again and requested to speak to the manager. They said that the manager was busy, and that Security would be coming. Eventually, Security did come and let us into the room, but by this point we were furious. It took us well over an hour to get settled into our room, and we never did receive a call from the manager or front desk apologizing for the immense inconvenience. That is not how you treat your paying, repeat customers.
Lastly, the television in our room wasn't functioning properly, as the sound kept cutting in and out. For a 5 star Luxury hotel, I expect all of the in-room amenities to be working.
The Phoenician used to be my favorite hotel, but after this experience with incredibly poor customer service, I won't return again, nor will I recommend it to my friends or colleagues. Such a disappointment.

findings.title: Ginger P. (2/5)
findings.snippet: My husband & I took my mother to the Thanksgiving brunch today, and we were all disappointed. First off, they no longer include mimosas. The waiter gave a flimsy excuse about liquor laws, then later a manager said "oh we just like to change things up". We waited 30 minutes for a bottle of champagne! Although there seemed to be a number of wait staff loitering about, we had to flag people down to get service. The food was pretty good, although a lot less variety than past years. Definitely not worth $95 per person, and oh yes, a mandatory 19% gratuity! I don't mind paying for quality, but I expect exceptional service, and that includes not having to refresh my own champagne glass.

findings.title: K. F. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed at the Phoenician in style. Was given the two bedroom Casita down on the golf course and all I can say is wow!! The place was like staying on a Presidential suite. My niece had never stayed in a hotel before and so for her birthday I decided to pull out all the stops. The service here is impeccable. My nieces eyes were as big as 50 cent pieces when she saw her own bathroom with jacuzzi tube. First thing she wanted to do was take a jacuzzi bath. The next thing she wanted was to order room service. The food here at the hotel is great: you can't go wrong with anything you may order up. The experience for my niece was worth every $$ spent just to see the look on her face. Have had lunches here at the hotel as well when quest come into experience AZ I always love to bring them here.  The landscaping and views from the dining room are incredible.

findings.title: Pratishruti M. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The Phoenician is definitely one of my SPG favorites, this is my second stay cation in two months and what keeps me coming back is that it completely captures my imagination.Located at the base of the Camelback mountain facilitates a view that is priceless! 

I prefer the golf course view with the mountains as a backdrop(it is sooo Romantic) especially if your witnessing it from the lounge chair of your private terrace.The rooms are Huge and the over sized bathrooms finished with Italian marble having separate bath and shower units are a plus.

The staff is friendly and i love how they always keep my room preferences in mind.The Golf course is great and another thing i love is the afternoon tea in the lobby(reservations are required). 
The only reason i deprive them of 5 stars is that the rooms are not at par with the grandeur of the lobby and the rest of the hotel.However the manager did tell me that they are planning to renovate soon.

Cheers!

findings.title: Lou V. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful grounds, excellent food, accomodations were good. The bell service and room service was somewhat slow at times.  Extremely expensive.

findings.title: Adrian I. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Amazing resort, first class food, service, and amenities.   I would recommend this resort for business or pleasure.

findings.title: Jen L. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We got the Travelzoo package for $109pp. We got one massage and the other got a facial.  Gratuity is a standard 20% of full price package so additional $32pp. The massage came with body brushing and a 50min massage. The facial was a normal facial. The package came with the NuFace wow brow but she didn't do it so that why not 5 stars.

On the other hand, Cindy, led the meditation at noon. Go!!! Do not miss this!!!! It was life changing. We ended up spending 3 hours talking with her. It was such a wonderful experience. She is so in tune with life, reality, just such a beautiful soul! We will be there again to see Cindy for sure! That was the best part of the whole thing. 

We did the pool thing too but the meditation and life discussion really made our day.

findings.title: Shoni S. (4/5)
findings.snippet: This is my neighborhood resort and I am never unsatisfied when I patron this establishment. You are greeted with lucious foliage and a warm welcome from the "gate keeper!" Self-parking is plentiful and easy to find. Complimentary valet. Always well kept up(swimming pools, rooms, eateries, lobby, courtyard, elevators). Always friendly and helping staff. Beautiful. We mainly go for high tea and the eateries!

findings.title: Caiden L. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
When you pay $180 for a 50 minute massage, you want it to be an awesome experience. Mind you, you can use all of the spa facilities and classes on the day you book and pay for a service, and the people are very friendly and customer-service oriented, but... the hot tub was REALLY overdue for a cleaning and really grossed me out. 

I had a decent enough masseuse and enjoyed the amenities but it didn't feel like a $180 value; I've spent less and gotten more at other spas. Not to mention the tip is automatically added for you at 20% minimum before your service begins, and if you have a gift card that leaves you with $20, you have to use it on your next service, nothing else. It would have been nice of them to explain parking as well- I was almost late because I had to wait 20 minutes for a spot that took me 10 minutes to walk to the spa. That's not terrible, but would have been nice to know ahead of time. 

If you hadn't set the bar so high with your website and prices, I wouldn't be leaving a 4-star review. I may be back but I'm thinking I'll get more for my money elsewhere. I'm still very glad my husband picked this place to get me a gift certificate for my birthday, and I'm glad I decided to use it for a massage; I just have high expectations for that kind of price tag since I have to be convinced to spend that kind of money on myself to begin with!

findings.title: Flora R. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
If you tout yourself to be a FIVE STAR resort, please act like it. This place is straight out of 1995 and the service is subpar. I've only been here one day and I already had to change rooms because of the moldy and musty smell. 

I'm sure in its heyday it was something to write home about, but for the price you pay, you can stay in a better place. Like the Phoenix rose out of its ashes, this places need to be burned down and raised to life again.

findings.title: Heather T. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Love Tea time here!!! And the dinner was phenomenal over at J&G's restaurant.. The people and service is always great, and the scenery is absolutely beautiful! Love this gorgeous AZ resort!!

findings.title: Stan F. (4/5)
findings.snippet: After 20 yrs in Phoenix, we decided to do a staycation. This is an incredible property, and I wish we saw more of it. We spent most of both days at the pool hydrating with cocktails and agua. Had a fun evening at the carnival, enjoying dinner from the food trucks. Crashed a 30th birthday party last night. They had their own photographer. Fun. Great brunch today. Great staff, very accommodating even when some guests are grade a a-holes. I love the nice big rooms. Just didn't have a good view.

findings.title: Ronald B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Hands down the best resort in Phoenix.   I'm very picky about hotels and this one is perfect.  The views, the service, the food and the location.

findings.title: Jon G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Surprisingly large resort with lots of amenities and access to hiking-- we especially liked the pools and tennis facility. Our room and bathroom were big and the bed was comfy. The decor felt a bit dated and the Internet was not very fast but we had a great stay. The food was good and the staff was without exception excellent.

findings.title: N A. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Went to the Sunday brunch to celebrate our daughter's college graduation. The food was great. The atmosphere was great. The service -- not so much.  The server made a big deal of making sure we knew the cost and that it was NOT a champagne brunch.  Okay, we already knew this information and she was annoying but I was willing to overlook it. Our group asked for hot tea, coffee and water.  There must be a shortage on these drinks at this restaurant as we couldn't seem to get anyone to refill the coffee or hot water for the tea the rest of the meal.  We finally gave up and just went with the water which at least the bus staff came and filled a couple times. There also seems to be a eagerness to remove plates they deemed finished but not replace silverware that was removed with the plates.  We had to ask for replacement forks and knives twice.  
We go out to eat very often and I'm not sure I'd put this restaurant on my 'return soon' list.  There are just too many other restaurants where both the food AND the service are great.

findings.title: Frank B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Course was beautiful! Just played and the greens were so true. If I could play this course everyday, I would. Service, value, pace of play are 5 star!

findings.title: Joel D. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Beautiful resort, landscape well kept. Rooms are slightly outdated and require refurbishment. Service level varies from lousy (check-in) to outstanding (bell captain and Cabanas Pool attendance).

Breakfast mediocre and Saturday night food availabity rather limited (after 9 pm).

Property will be regurbished and we will try again next April.

findings.title: G L. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful grounds and facility. Very clean rooms and fitness center. Service is friendly and accommodating

findings.title: Coley B. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Whether your travelling on business (hopefully you got the group rate!) or enjoying a vacation in the Arizona sun, the Phoenician is a great place to be! There are tons(!) of events to stay entertained with, many pools, cabanas, an amazing gold course with nearby tennis courts, and even though it's a "little touch," how cute is a cactus garden to wander through while enjoying your morning coffee!?

Why not 5 stars? The prices. It's located at the base of Camelback Mountain which is a prime area for those visiting the Scottsdale/Phoenix area, but the Phoenician takes advantage of this with their outrageous prices! Don't expect to find much in the "free" category (free sunshine?) as this place isn't doing your wallet any favors...however, if you're able to experience the resort at least once, it will be well worth it!

findings.title: David S. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I stayed here last month and really liked the place: big rooms (tho a bit Golden Girls decor), great pools, nice location.

Two thoughts to make it better:
1) at a resort like this, I'd expect wifi to be included, not an extra
2) I wish they policed the pool visitors better. There were clearly locals showing up on a busy day in street clothes and changing in the pool restrooms. I wouldn't expect this place to have pool parties, so I doubt that was the case. One woman by us told the pool server "I'm from corporate" when explaining she didn't have a room # - I doubt that too, as if "corporate" would encourage her to bring 8 friends and secure the best poolside spots and umbrellas all afternoon on a busy day. It would have been a LOT better without all the extra people.

findings.title: Zachary B. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I enjoyed the resort a lot. Especially the pools because they had 4 and 1 that is a hot tub which is very relaxing. I liked the pool at the bottom because it was quiet and less splashy. I also like that they have a water slide there.

Zachary B

findings.title: Courtney S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: im not a reviewer type, but I feel obligated to write one on this place to help others save their money.  This is the absolute WORST staycation I've ever experienced.  Our room was disgusting and very outdated.  The carpet had threads showing and literally looks as if it's the 1st carpet installed 20 yrs ago.  The grout in the shower had mold all over in it and the check out attendant said this is typical of older resorts but they would look into it. Absolutely disgusting to experience this at a luxury resort.  The bed was terrible and the furniture was definitely outdated with stains all over.  The cable in the room rarely worked during our 2 night stay which was ridiculous.  The air conditioner was leaking all over the tile outside our room creating the potential for a tragic fall for somebody.  We notified staff immediately and it wasn't even slightly tended to until late the next day.  Water was still all over.  The pools had noticeable algae in them and the pool furniture is very old and stained.  Gross!  We literally had to beg for towels at the pool and they were VERY slow to serve us.  We were advised of an adults only pool area, but that definitely wasn't the case because older children were running around throwing water balls BOTH days we were out at the pool and the pool attendants allowed this.  It made it even worse that it was inhabited by children's birthday parties going on.  The food is very mediocre for what you get and definitely NOT what you pay for.  We asked at 11am if any restaurants were serving breakfast on Saturday and were literally told we were out of luck.  After we had to settle on an overpriced meal at The Relish who had lousy servers, we learned that the hotel had a restaurant serving brunch that the hotel staff failed to disclose when told we were out of luck.  The staff at this supposed 5 Diamond resort is not Diamond quality.  They all need a job change and definitely need to get out of hospitality.  Our stay in this very outdated low quality resort is a huge mistake and we definitely didn't get what we paid.  I hope you listen to this review and stay elsewhere because there are MUCH better places with modern atmosphere and quality staff and even at lower prices.

findings.title: Thomas L. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
The Phoenician really dropped the ball and disappointed.  This was one of the worst customer service experiences or lack of I've ever had with a resort.  If I could give it a negative star I would in a heartbeat!  First all of all, I chose this place because my lady and I had a been here a while back and had a decent time at the lounge  and I wanted to come back here and purpose to her.  So I booked a the Delux executive suite for the night and reserved a table at J&G steakhouse for July 3rd.  Keep in mind I booked the room and made the reservation 1 week in advance.  When I booked the room I asked specifically does the room have a good view from the balcony and the lady said I would have a wonderful view from my room. I told them I will be purposing to my girlfriend and I want this night to be perfect...

July 3rd- I called the front desk at 11:00 and requested a early check in...They told me the room won't be ready probably until 4:00.  I told them I wanted to check in early so I can decorate the room for my engagement.  The lady told me I had to come down in person and at that point they could do an early check in for me.  Why in the f*ck do I need to come down in person for a early check in?  Regardless, I drove down to the place and checked in.  I finally got a call at 2:30 and told me my room was available.  I told the front desk lady I planned on having a Mariachi band to come to my room and play 3 songs, would that be OK?  They denied my request and said it wouldn't be allowed in the room, but could do it at the lobby.  I was pretty pissed, so I decided to cancel the Mariachi idea.  I arrived at my room and noticed it was on the 1st floor. Room 1010.  Since it was July 3rd, they had a concert and people were playing corn hole (baggo) and it was LOUD!  The view was garbage, it was a view of the pool and people walking around drunk.  I completely felt like I was duped.  I should of carried though with my mariachi plan, because since they had a concert outside, I doubt they would of heard the band in my room.

Overall I was pretty pissed and upset with the Phoenician, but since it was a special night for my lady, I didn't want to cause a scene or show any disapproval of the resort.  This place wasn't accommodating at all.  They didn't care about me as a guest or didn't do anything to make this night special.

There are a lot of great luxury resorts in the Scottsdale area, I highly recommend you go to one of those places instead of here.  This place is a joke.  Absolute nightmare.  Also I had some charges to my room, that I wasn't expecting, but I don't have the time or effort to write about that....

To top it off......I requested a booth for our dinner at J&G steakhouse and they couldn't even accommodate that, keep in mind I asked a week ago for this request.  Our reservation was at 9:00  We basically had a table in the middle of the restaurant and was poorly set up.  You could hear the fireworks going off, but had no view to even see them.  SMH.   Feel free to read my review on that horrible dinner experience as well.

To the staff and management at the Phoenician....You call yourself a 5 star resort?  You got to be kidding me.  You can probably guess, a future wedding won't be planned at this place.

I'm done.

findings.title: Fig C. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Had a staycation at the Phoenician for our 5 year anniversary.  We stayed in a casita with a pool view.  The room was nice and I had a good nights sleep on the bed.  For some reason they had crappy pillows, like every other hotel on this planet.  They have live bands in the lounge  and in the steak restaurant on the 5th floor.  The employees working the front desk were very kind and helpful when needed.  For out of towners, it is close to Old Town Scottsdale and Camelback Mountain.  It is also located in the nicest area of the Valley.

The negative part has to do with the pool.  We were in the pool and did not see a server for 30 plus minutes.  Asked to order food from the bar, and he stated only if we sit at the bar.  We were in the pool 2 feet from the bar, I guess walking this distance to give us food was to much.  We then finally spoke with a server, who said no server has our area, mind blown.  She said she can only serve to the other side of the pool.  We ended up getting food, after jumping through several difficult hoops.  The most romantic part of the pool was the caution tape around several pools, which remained our entire stay.  Was great for pictures.  The pool area was also a mess, tables full with dirty plates and bottles.

It was a little pricey for one night, and would not match the cheaper rates on line ($320).

It is a very nice resort, but we have had better experience at other resorts in the Valley.

If it was not for our negative pool experience, price being on the high side I would give them 4 to 5 stars.

If you are looking for a good steak place, and want to leave the resort try Steak 44 down the street at 44th st and Camelback Rd.  I heard the resorts Steak restaurant is good also.

findings.title: Audrey G. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Eh. Front desk lady was rude. Waited on bags awhile. Paid for desert view and got a casita facing a busy street/parking lot. Not at all what I expected from a "luxury resort," especially given the price tag. There are better resorts and luxury hotels in phx for the same price.

findings.title: Dennis M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We just spent 3 days here; best hotel we've ever stayed in! Great food, our two suites were great and a great staff.  The restaurants were great, the pool cabana was superb, and all the amenities were up to snuff.  The only complaint is the music in the steakhouse - how about some Sinatra or Tony Bennett or anything with a melody!  Next time I'll bring my own earphones!

findings.title: John A. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
GOLF REVIEW ONLY:

This is by far the nicest golf course I have ever played. Very cheap during summer months. If you like golf, you NEED to play here.

findings.title: Rob F. (3/5)
findings.snippet: 5 star resort if they monitor their own rules.. Bunch of 5 year olds doing cannonballs into the only thing that appears to be adult oriented ....the outdoor hot tub (because they don't have an adult only pool). Otherwise 5 star..

findings.title: Cristina C. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Stopped into the restaurant to dodge the rain a couple weeks ago...and was a little underwhelmed. The resort itself seems a little outdated, with wear and tear showing on all textiles, chairs, etc. Lunch itself was very mediocre...too much mayonnaise on an overly cooked 'panino' with cheap bread. For $70 for two without any alcoholic beverages, it felt a little greedy on their part. Compared to the Scottsdale Fairmont...no comparison. Service staff were inattentive, and I just that sense that they know they are on the decline. It was a sad thing to experience, and I really hoped that it was going to the opposite experience due to the brand name.

findings.title: Suzanne W. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This review is for people thinking of holding events here. I'm originally from Scottsdale, and grew up dreaming of getting married here.  Well, I did. What a horrific experience, from start to almost finish. I say that because my wedding was perfect, mostly thanks to ur amazing wedding planners, Trista and Alex at BTS Event Management. I can't even imagine what I would have done had I not been smart enough to hire them, they were life savers. I picked The Phoenician based on my own experiences there, which had always been top notch. I expected for a day as special as my wedding that things along the way in the months leading up to it would be seamless, or at least not crisis after crisis. Nope. From the start, nothing I was told was what actually happened. Where do I start? Because my wedding was small (38 people) I was never made aware that we wouldn't be getting a food tasting, since we weren't spending enough in food and beverage, apparently you have to spend 15 grand to taste the food. In fact, in our original meeting with catering, we were told we would get a tasting, and how the chef would be willing to work with us, blah blah blah. The area where we planned to get married in a gazebo had the gazebo torn down, so it looked nothing like what we signed on for, and no one told us there were plans to tear down or alter the appearance of the area. Because our wedding was small, and we didn't want to rent a ballroom, we asked to reserve a small section of the lobby bar after dinner for guests to have drinks, we were told absolutely not, its a public area, and there is no reserving seats. We planned to have a five course dinner at J and G, a very expensive steak house on the property. To say the managers there were unhelpful is an understatement. They also refused to provide a tasting, and when one manager was talking to my father about it she actually said "our steak tastes like steak, and our potatoes taste like potatoes, why do you need a tasting?" We did get one, after I called the GM, that cost us close to 400 dollars. They comped one entree, thanks. The one manager that made the steak and potato comment was rude to my dad so many times I stopped counting. About thirty days before my wedding, I was told that the rehearsal we had planned and already told people about (remember, people were traveling from out of town for this wedding, and especially the wedding party were making travel arrangements around what we were telling them), could not be held in the location my wedding would be in because they had booked an event there for that evening. Their solution was to let us rehearse "in a different location." Call me crazy (which they acted like I was), but what is the point of a rehearsal if it isn't where the actual wedding is? How do you know where to walk, etc if you aren't rehearsing in the correct location? The response to my anger was a resolute "Sorry, your rehearsal is not happening on the Orchid Lawn, deal with it." (Well they said this in much nicer words.) It actually took me reaching out to the General Manager of the hotel to get any movement, and we still didn't get the rehearsal as planned. He let us rehearse at 3 pm (many in our party had to pay to change their flights) and moved us into the presidential suite, for the rate of a regular room, and comped one night. Very generous, and we appreciated it, but again, it was another example of me literally having to scream and yell to get things somewhat fixed. What I found most challenging is all of their "corporate rules" and a real unwillingness to make us feel special and taken care of on such an important day. No upgraded room for your wedding night, no suite to get ready in, you get ready in a conference room. We ended up saying forget the conference rooms, since we had the big suite comped after I complained, but really, who wants to get ready in a conference room with a table and five uncomfortable chairs and a water station. No place comfortable to sit, no bathroom, no TV. I thought that was really silly. With all the rooms they have available, if you don't have a huge suite, they should at least let you get ready in a real hotel room. I don't fault the employees for this, they have to follow the rules, which are set by corporate and upper management. And the service here is outstanding, that's why we chose it. But tell me, because I'm sure a PR person will respond to this, are all these rules really serving your guests? Do I really have to almost throw a tantrum (which is not my personality at all) to get a tasting for food that's being served to my guests because J and G just arbitrarily doesn't do them or because I'm not spending enough? They have a saying that a happy guest will tell one person, and an unhappy guest will tell a hundred. I hope I've reached at least that many here. Get married at The R

findings.title: Queen P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This was a terrible experience. I spent two nights at this hotel and had to report two separate incidences of cockroaches where a employee had to catch them at 2am. I left my stay with bites all over my legs from the bed bugs also. As I was checking out I reminded the front desk about the cockroaches and the problems I had with my stay and they had no record of my report. This did not feel like a 5 star hotel at all.

findings.title: John K. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Beautiful property although some parts needs to be updated. Great place to have a meeting and bring your spouse.

Stayed in the Casitas and enjoyed that experience over the traditional hotel experience.

findings.title: Alan P. (2/5)
findings.snippet: I would've loved to have seen this place in its heyday. While well appointed there are just a few things not quite on par with a Ritz-Carlton or a Four Seasons although the prices are the same. First, the good: the rooms and bathrooms are huge! The pools are nice and spacious although the hot tub is ridiculously small. Has neat little trails for picture opportunities with saguaros, waterfalls and other fauna and the grounds seem well kept. The not so great: the staff is not "Ritz" ready. While nice you certainly get the feeling that you're "just another guest" no special "warm and fuzzy" feeling at all. I noticed lightbulbs that needed replacing, stained carpets, dirty HVAC vents, dead flowers and landscaping on balconies and don't expect housekeeping before 4 or 5 pm. Need extra towels or pillows from housekeeping expect to wait an hour. Some rooms have Motel 6 views (we did not book through a third party discount website) and or view was a joke. The spa is extremely dated and the staff is average. If you are looking for a spa experience in sure there are better local choices other than the hotel (never felt that way at a Ritz spa). Overall a nice visit but I wouldn't go out of my way to return.

findings.title: Janina P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: View from our room looked upon other hotel rooms. There were stains on the floor. There is a coffee maker in the room, they refilled the coffee for this morning but didn't refill the cream. We called room service for towels and it took 45 minutes to bring them. They planted flowers outside the patio, but they were all shriveled up and dead. The service at dinner last night was awful. The server was rude and it was obvious he was not happy to answer any questions about the menu. I would not return and at these prices, they should be ashamed.

findings.title: Paul P. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
A grand old hotel resting on its laurels.

The carpeting in my room was thread bare, down to the matting. The hallway carpet the same. When the bellman came for my bags on move out I asked him about the decorations. He agreed that it was embarrassing and that he was tired of making excuses to guests year after year. Apparently Barry Steinlicht of Starwood promises a complete rennovation every year and then cancels it. Why would he pay for it as long as idiots like us continue to patronize the place  based on its heritage.  The bellman thought it had not been redone for 20 yrs since Charles Keating finished the hotel and then went to jail. 

Service was just as disappointing. I asked for the Wall St. Journal to be delivered every morning and they were not able to do it once.  I had to go to the lobby to get it. Three out of five room service breakfasts had to be returned in order to get the correct food. 

A high speed internet connection is vital to my being able to stay in touch with my office and business associates. It is a critical requirement for my hotel selection. The Wi-Fi connection never worked the five days I was there. When I would call for service they would give me an 800 # to connect me with someone in India who I could not understand.  The Phoenician never dispatched a staff member to come to my room and check things out. 

To me it was a Super 8 Motel with Starwood prices.  I would never stay their again. I was told that the Fairmont Princess is the new "place to stay". 

I am suprised American Express Centurion shows  it in the list of Preferred Hotels. Phoenix is their home. It would not take alot to check their evaluation, if that judgement was being made without any additional influence.

findings.title: Jen G. (3/5)
findings.snippet: I did not stay here but attended the ASU/GSV conference. So please take my 3 star rating from that perspective. As a conference attendee there where not enough restrooms in the long wings and there were not enough food venues to accommodate all the people. The grounds were beautiful but for an event that big there needs to be more eating facilities and I'm not sure what you can do about restrooms.

findings.title: Trevor E. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I came here for Tea with my daughter, her friend, and our families for a 17 year old birthday. Was expecting an ultimate girl experience and the need for a real meal afterwords but ended up having a blast and was surprised at both the quality and quantity of the food.

That food was excellent. The food was also abundant. They just just kept bringing food. The service was amazing (quiet, frequent, polite, cheerful), the view was beautiful, and the location was ultra swanky (I'm probably not supposed to call tea 'swanky' but I felt like a million dollars).

Still, I was one of just two guys in the whole place for tea (the other being my buddy). That said, I did feel a little like I was at grandma's house and was worried about avoiding a minefield of faux pas (I had to ask my wife how to spell that, and I am not sure I got the plural right).

In case anyone else is in the same boat: 

Guys Guide to avoiding the dreaded faux pas while enjoying tea at the Phoenician: 
 -- Do not wear jeans or shorts (that is a faux pas). Wear slacks and a nice shirt. A golf shirt is okay, a sport shirt is better. 
 -- Sit up straight and fold your hands in your lap when not eating. (Slouching is a faux pas).
 -- Keep your phone in your pocket. (To do otherwise is a faux pas).
 -- There are baby showers and bridal showers going on throughout. Do not remark on the Victoria's Secret's bags on the table nearby while doing your best groucho eyebrows at your wife/date. (This is a faux pas).
 -- If you order champagne, enjoy knowing that excellent wait staff will continually refill your champagne flute throughout your meal. (This is awesome, and yes it that glass is called a flute. Calling it a glass is a faux pas).
 -- Tea and champagne pair wonderfully. When you are having tea with champagne, you should say things like "wonderfully" often. (This is not a faux pas). 
 -- Even though the sandwiches are tiny, delicious, and can fit in your mouth all at once, do not pop them into your mouth whole (that is a faux pas). You must take at least 2 bites, regardless of tiny sandwich size. Three bites is preferred.
 -- Do not stack tiny delicious sandwiches atop one another to make new creations (that is a faux pas).
 -- The stuff that looks like mustard on the table is actually delicious lemon curd for the scones. Scones are like sweet sweet biscuits. Do not put the mustard-looking lemon curd on your sandwich, Do save room for scones. Scones are the second course. Scones are delicious. The mustard-looking lemon curd is delicious on the delicious scones. (Curd is a funny word. Do not point that out to your server. That would be a faux pas).
 -- The third course are tiny pastries. In case you hadn't guessed, these are delicious. When you eat the tiny eclair in two (or more) bites eclair filling may squirt out the eclair hole. Do not exclaim "eclair poo!". (That would be a faux pas and a waste of eclair filling - attend to the tiny eclair hole). (So, it turns out that calling it an 'eclair hole' is also a faux pas. Who knew?).
 -- Do nor continuously ask if something is a faux pas. Nor should you ask, at the table, how to spell faux pas nor what the plural is of faux pas. All appear to be faux pas. Rather, just stare deeply into the eyes of your date / wife / daughter / mother. (That last one might be a faux pas).

findings.title: Breanna G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I stayed here and The Biltmore within the same month, and The Phoenician is by far a better resort. The service, amenities, decor, food, and scenery are the best in Phoenix. The water park and spa are ideal. I will only stay here from now on when in Phoenix.

findings.title: Beep B. (2/5)
findings.snippet: I called on Saturday and spoke with a lady who gave me a price on what it would cost for me to stay there four nights with my husband.  She actually was kind enough to give me the prices for what two different packages would be $1800 vs $1923.  She went over the property with me as I have never been there and she actually got me all excited about it by letting me know she would get me a room convenient for my pregnant body and my dog, and she let me know some of the amenities of the resort.  I thanked her and told her I would have to call back later because since the package makes it non-refundable I wanted to be sure the dates would be OK with my husbands work.  Well today, 4/8, I call around 5:40 and speak with Jason.  It was a completely different experience talking with him!  He kept stuttering, could not explain to me things about the property that I still had questions about, (example where do you go for breakfast on the property,) and gave me an amount of $2246 that I would be charged.  I asked him if he would be able to email me a breakdown and he said he didn't have that capability.  I accepted that and asked if I could have a breakdown of what I was paying and he could not give me that either!  Why would I give him my credit card for $2200 that is nonrefundable if he can't explain to me what I am paying for???  I also was curious to see why it was more then the $1923 package I was expecting to pay for.  Now I do expect to go there and pay a good chunk of change- I don't expect this place to be cheap- but it is ridiculous and incomprehensible that I would call somewhere that is supposedly a five-diamond resort and they can't tell me what I am paying for???  And add to that that it is absolutely not refundable.  I told him I would call back later.  No way was I giving him my credit card number.  I hung up and called the front desk again to reconnect me to someone new to make my reservation and I explained to her that the stuttering guy who I had just spoken to did not impress me and he didn't even seem familiar with the resort.  She said my best bet would be to call during normal business hours (until 5:30pm so I guess I missed it by ten minutes) to get someone who knows more about the property and would hopefully be able to give me the experience I wanted in terms of making reservations.  I'm sorry but I think I will be calling the Four Season after this nonsense.  It is inexcusable to not be able to call and make a reservation with someone who can tell you what you are paying for and why.

findings.title: Marie D. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
My boyfriend and I stayed here when we were in town for spring training. The hotel was beautiful and the service great. The turndown service each night was a nice little surprise to come back to each night. 

3 days into our 5 day stay my boyfriends phone got stolen while we were down at the pool. I put his phone on the lounge chair under a towel and hopped in the pool. We were in the pool for several hours enjoying the sunshine and when we got back to our stuff his phone was gone. My purse with my phone and both our wallets was still there.  I spoke to the staff around the pool, touched base with the pool manager. He had some staff go and look in with the towels, but the towel was still on the chair where we had been. I gave him my cell phone number. I proceeded to go to to the front desk and fill out an incident report as well as contact security and gave them all the information as well as our room number. Not a sole followed up. 

We were able to watch his phone leave the property later that evening on the "find my phone" app.   We never heard from ANY of the MANY people that I reported this incident to. I understand I am leaving my belongings and walking away at my own risk when at the pool. But this is a very nice and expensive hotel and I was pretty disappointed in the service and that they did nothing to help us out. He had to buy a new phone when we got back home.  The cost of buying a new iPhone when you don't have a upgrade, well, thats more than this hotel was worth.

findings.title: Scott C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Wow!  What more can I say for this spectacular resort hotel.  This place has luxury written all over it with the location right against scottsdale's famous camelback mountain and close proximity to the ultimate mall shopping experience that is fashion square.  If you want to get away from all the hustle and bustle then I would suggest something up north.  But if you want luxury and all the amenities at your door step, near one the best cities in the country, then look no further.  

Also, the 27 hole golf course here is immaculate as is the pool and activities for kids.  Absolutely the best golf course to play if you want to stay near old town.

findings.title: Melissa H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE THIS PLACE!!! Hotel is beautiful, staff rules and pool is so fun. Would go back in a second and will for sure. The kids club was the best and kids loved this trip as much as the adults did. 
i know there are lots of choices  but look no further. stat here you wont be sorry.

findings.title: Sungy V. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The water park area was nice for kids and the spa services were a little over priced but nice.

findings.title: A C. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
This review is in reference to my parents' stay at the Phoenician Dec 26-30.  I booked the stay as part of a birthday gift for my father's 70th birthday celebrations. I spent many hours researching hotels in Scottsdale, and given the numerous favorable reviews posted, I decided to choose the Phoenician. I booked the stay by phone with reservations agent Cheryl Byerle, who I have to say was the most helpful person throughout the entire ordeal. At the time of booking, I completed necessary paperwork to ensure that the entire stay and incidentals would be charged to my credit card, as the vacation was a gift to my parents. The paperwork was confirmed to be received, and in fact, 4 days before their arrival, Cheryl emailed me to reconfirm that they had my credit card info on file for the entire stay. I should add that I booked a rate that was to include breakfast.
So far, so good.... I thought. Upon my parents' arrival, they were asked to provide their credit card for incidentals. Not knowing what I had actually contracted with the hotel, they went ahead and gave them their credit card. Apparently, the front desk did not notice that MY credit card was on file. Mistake number 1. The events that followed are not a testament to the "five star" quality that the Phoenician advertises.
The day of checkout, my parents received a folio detailing every charge with the entire stay charged to their credit card. What a great birthday present. Not only did they give them the bill, but they charged them as well?! In addition, apparently my parents were never told at check-in that breakfast was included in their stay. This was only realized by my parents upon seeing the bill and noting it was a "bed and breakfast rate". On the bill were additional charges for room service (since my parents were not aware their rate included breakfast). Upon noticing his credit card was charged for the entire bill, my father went to the front desk to inquire about the situation. He told them that his daughter had paid for the stay... at which time they went back and looked at the notes and realized their error. Very little apology was offered. When he mentioned that no one ever told them about breakfast, and that they had used room service and were charged, he was offered a $10 credit (barely enough to cover a glass of juice). After more haggling (which at this point was purely ridiculous since there were multiple errors), the front desk removed the resort fee and some other charges, again offering very little in the way of an apology.
The story gets worse. Days after their stay was completed, I still had not received a copy of the folio, which I was told would be emailed to me upon checkout. When I emailed, then called to inquire, what I received was a very undetailed folio that showed my credit card was only charged for the room, not for incidentals. My parents had spa treatments, dined at the restaurant, etc. All that was charged to my father's credit card. 
I proceeded to contact Cheryl, who put me in touch with Nathan Davidson, reservations supervisor. He apologized for the error and told me all charges had been corrected after my correspondence and my father's credit card had been refunded. He was very nice via email and phone, but this was NOT ENOUGH OF AN APOLOGY! I subsequently asked for a detailed folio and to speak to the manager. I was referred to Bowen Kilker, front desk manager.
On January 9, I spoke to Mr. Kilker by phone. While the exchange was cordial, I reiterated my disappointment in the entire situation, and how upset I was that once the errors had been recognized, that I hadn't been notified. The only reason I became aware of the errors was when I inquired about the bill. My father was so upset and kind of embarrassed (for us) by the whole situation that he never told me about it. At that time, Mr. Kilker told me who would send out a personal letter of apology to my parents, as well as a voucher towards a future stay at the hotel. This was little comfort to me given my parents' celebration vacation had been ruined, but better than nothing. 
That brings me to today. As of yet, we have not received said letter of apology. On February 12, I emailed Mr Kilker to inquire about the status of said letter, and have received no response. I cannot express how disappointing and upset I am by this entire situation. I feel that the initial error was egregious enough, only to be snowballed by the ridiculous number of errors to follow. We, as well as our friends and family, are frequent visitors of the Phoenix area and its high end resorts, and this pretty much guarantees we will never again set foot in this hotel.

findings.title: Len M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is the best hotel in the Phoenix/Scottsdale area.  Hands down.  No question.  Nothing else to say.

findings.title: Bill S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This place has a very retro, first class feel.   

We used Starwood points and were upgraded to a one bedroom suite.  We could have lived here forever!  Parking was easy, Jenn, who checked us in, provided spectacular service, and the grounds were beautiful.  Nate, a waiter who we meet on the Cholla Trail, provided service the resort should be proud of.

The Flight of the Phoenix Bird Show was hokey.  The trainers had problems handling the birds and should have spent more time talking about how each bird was rescued.  

Otherwise, this is a special place.

findings.title: Scott H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Great rooms, great shops, great bars, great golf, the gym is large and clean and great views. What's not to like. Only suggestion would be to stay in the actual hotel vs casitas unless you're traveling with the family and need the extra appt like space. The casitas aren't as nicely appointed in my opinion.

findings.title: No H. (2/5)
findings.snippet: My 2nd time here. First time stayed in a casita which was incredible (4 stars) this time since I'm solo I chose a Premium room in the main building. It's terrible. there are 6 floors and I'm on the 5th floor. I paid an up charge for a mountain view. well...that mountain is in my face... I feel claustrophobic!! When I asked for a different room I was offered a room overlooking the drive up to the hotel and another building. I thought.. .oh well I'll keep the mountain and I won't be in the room much...then I asked the concierge to make a reservation for me and well that was poorly executed also.. I don't normally EVER complain.... but I normally get such great service when I travel solo. I won't be back... time to try the fairmont scottsdale

findings.title: Joe M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Great resort, the grounds are perfect, the staff was awesome. This place is perfect. We were here from a conf. So glad we came. Visited many of the restaurants while there. Yum, yum. You really don't have to leave.

findings.title: Luis S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I absolutely loved the canyon suite we stayed in. The view of the mountain was breathtaking and the hospitality of the staff was beyond expectation. This stay was short but we have fell in love and are planning a long stay to be able to enjoy all the complex has to offer

findings.title: Steph C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I've been to Phoenix twice in the last two years, both times to visit the Poisoned Pen bookstore in Scottsdale. Last year, I decided to save money and use Couchsurfing. It wasn't a bad experience, but I didn't get a bed (or even a couch, actually--I slept in an armchair). I also drove from L.A. to Phoenix and back in two days, blowing a flat on my way back about ten miles outside of Indio. This time, my husband and I decided to take a weekend trip, and booked a room at The Phoenician. Probably goes without saying, but this trip was more enjoyable than the first. The Phoenician must be one of the nicest hotels in town.

We used Starwood points to book our room (The Phoenician is in the Luxury Collection) and thought this hotel offered excellent value. We stayed two nights in a beautiful room with a comfortable bed and an attractive bathroom. We hung by the pool, drank at the hotel bar, and had an all-around lovely resort experience.

The pool was nice, nothing elaborate but very pretty, and I was impressed with the food and service we got from the comfort of our lounge chairs. I had a salad with spice-encrusted ahi tuna, watermelon, jicama, navel orange, cucumber, and baby field greens in a sweet chili vinaigrette--like a legitimate quality restaurant salad. My husband's cheeseburger was also tasty.

We also had good drinking, both at the pool and the bar, where we were able to use drink tickets that came complimentary with our Starwood reservation. We had Four Peaks pale ale and a solid Bloody Mary at the pool, and nice cocktails inside. I enjoyed a Prickly-Peño Margarita with tequila, lime juice, Cointreau, orange juice, and a jalapeño-prickly pear syrup. The Single-Barrel Mojito and the Lychee-Jito were also great.

Parking was free and easy, and service was pleasant all around. I only wish we'd had more time to hang out. Two days was just not enough time to do all the relaxing we wanted at The Phoenician. We'll have to come back again next year.

findings.title: Jennifer S. (4/5)
findings.snippet: 5 stars for the location, grounds and customer service, but 3 stars for the outdated rooms.  We love this property and hope that they will renovate the rooms to keep up with the other resorts in the Scottsdale area. The Phoenician is conveniently located close to Old Town Scottsdale and the vibrant dining and nightlife scene.  Their fitness offerings are nice for guests too - yoga, hiking etc. for an additional cost to guests.

findings.title: Carl A. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Staying here is like being in a time capsule and re-visiting a luxury resort from the 1980s. The place hasn't had much in the way of capex for a few decades and it shows. The owners - Starwood - are milking this for all its worth. If they could just hold off, it will probably be fabulous again in about a decade as that 80s-retro-resort-glitz comes back in style. But knowing Corporate America's lack of prescient timing, they will probably renovate at just the wrong time. Go to the steakhouse for dinner while there.

findings.title: Tommi M. (3/5)
findings.snippet: The Phoenician is gorgeously located in the heart of scottsdale. I will start with the pros- great location, near camelback mountain, fashion square mall and old town scottsdale. J & G restaurant (not run by Phoenician) is fabulous. Beautiful for sunset dinner. The pool is fabulous for kids. Cons- though a great property to cater to families they are for kids 5 and up. Most fine hotels that we stay at start at 4 and up. Phoenician will not allow your child at 4 to stay even if he/she is turning 5 the following week. The staff at Phoenician used to be amazing at service with a do-anything to help make your vacation amazing. Now, seems like hotel staff are over worked and underpaid and grumpy. Bummer. The rooms are dated, the spa is dated, overall the hotel needs to be majorly remodeled. Sort of shame they haven't done it yet as it's a great amazing property with fabulous potential.

findings.title: Melanie A. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Most Amazing Resort!!!
We absolutely loved it!!!
Stunningly Beautiful Views & Peaceful 
The Service was Excellent
  5 stars
Exceptionally Wonderful & Friendly Staff willing & ready to help - anyway possible - 
 anytime...
They go above & beyond to make certain that your stay is "all" it should be!!!

I can't wait until my husband & I go back again!!!
----love----

findings.title: Hollis E. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My husband and I stayed for 4 days and it was an all around wonderful experience. The staff and the service was exceptional! The cleanest and most well ran resort in Phoenix. The property is gorgeous as well as the inside of the hotel. We make multiple trips to phoenix a year and this is by far our favorite hotel. Everyone was very helpful and it was wonderful coming back in the evenings to a turndown service with chocolates and slippers by the bed. We played the golf course and it was immaculate. Very fun and friendly to every level of golfer. We can't wait to go back!

findings.title: Valencia D. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The concierge staff here is top notch.  Always willing to help you with whatever they can.  Only drawback was they could not order flowers or balloons for room delivery for me unless I gave them my credit card info.  They could not just charge it to our room?  I found that a bit irritating, but their service otherwise was impeccable.  

Love the Valet staff.  Traveling alone with baby can be challenging.  These guys were on it and so helpful.  

Baby & kids pool area is great!  It is set off away from the "adult" pool lounging area which I find nice.  They have an open space for Croquet which is fun to play anytime.  

Grille service was interesting.  For brunch of 5 we seemed to get top notch service.  But it seemed the smaller the party we were, the worst service we got.  Really.

findings.title: Cindy D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The Phoenician was nothing less than spectacular when we stayed in Scottsdale for the weekend.  The staff was extremely friendly and the service was great.

The food by the poolside was yummy and servers were very attentive as well. The restaurant that we had breakfast at Saturday and Sunday (see my other reviews) was great all around. We stayed in a casita which is just a more private room outside the main hotel and it was amazing.  The room was large with a balcony and we had a fantastic time.

When were were leaving, I left something back in the room and didn't realize it until we got home. I called the next day and the customer service was fantastic.  They shipped it back to me and I had it by the end of the week!

I'd definitely recommend this hotel to others!

findings.title: Michael L. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Very pricy, but they treat you like a king. Go down the water slide and hike Camelback Mountain.

findings.title: Angelo B. (1/5)
